For most marketplaces and independent retail it's completely fine and far cheaper; just confirm your channel's exact requirement first.
tools.best_for: sellers and small brands listing on marketplaces or in independent retail who want authentic, one-time-cost UPC/EAN barcodes without an annual GS1 membership
tools.skip_if: your target retailer or brand registry explicitly requires a GS1-issued company prefix in your own name — then buy direct from GS1
compare_with: GS1 costs more and can carry ongoing fees, but it's the only route when a channel demands a prefix registered to your company

tools.name: Beautiful.ai
tools.what_it_does: Presentation builder whose templates lay themselves out as you type. Pro is about $12/month billed annually but $45 month-to-month — a steep gap — and the constraints that make decks look consistent also block pixel-level custom layouts.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Pro about $12/mo billed annually ($45 monthly); Team about $40/user/mo annual ($50 monthly) with brand controls and shared libraries; Enterprise custom for 20+ seats. A single one-off presentation can be bought for ~$45; 14-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: The smart-template engine is the feature and the fence: decks look polished with zero design skill precisely because the system constrains you, so pixel-perfect custom layouts and heavy brand exceptions fight the tool. And note the billing gap — $12/mo annual becomes $45 month-to-month, one of the steeper monthly premiums around. If your organisation lives in PowerPoint workflows, test the import/export round-trip before committing.
tools.best_for: founders, sales and small teams that want consistently good-looking decks fast, where design consistency matters more than pixel-level control
tools.skip_if: you need intricate custom layouts or complex animations (designers want full control), or your whole company workflow is deeply PowerPoint-native
compare_with: Gamma is the AI-native rival with a freer canvas — Beautiful.ai's edge is disciplined, on-brand consistency at speed

tools.name: Beefree
tools.what_it_does: RGE Studio (formerly Beefree — renamed 14 May 2026): drag-and-drop email and landing-page design. Build responsive, on-brand emails fast and export clean HTML to any major ESP, no coding required. Beefree remains the company name and the name of its separate developer SDK; the builder itself now lives under reallygoodemails.com.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (verified 21 Jul 2026 on reallygoodemails.com/pricing) Sold as RGE Studio since the 14 May 2026 rebrand. Starter free — up to 10 designs, 6 exports/mo, landing-page builder, custom subdomain, 20GB/mo image traffic, unlimited users but no roles or permissions. Professional $25/mo billed yearly ($30/mo monthly) — unlimited designs and folders, unlimited reusable blocks, 2 editing users plus 4 view-only, AI writing assistant. Business $134/mo billed yearly ($160/mo monthly) — 2 editing users plus 10 view-only, 2 workspaces, approval workflows, advanced brand controls, QA assistant. Enterprise: custom, quoted by sales. The free trial is 15 days on the Business plan. The embeddable Beefree SDK is a separate product on its own price list (developers.beefree.io) and is not covered by these numbers.
tools.honest_knock: Read the seat row before the price row: Professional and Business both cap at two full editing seats, so a "mid-sized team" plan at $134/mo annual still buys two people who can actually build — everyone else lands in view-only slots (four on Professional, ten on Business) or an Enterprise quote. The free Starter is the odd one out: unlimited users, but with no roles or permissions at all, and exports metered at six a month rather than the unlimited free tier its old reputation suggests. And the naming is a live tripwire: since 14 May 2026 the builder is RGE Studio at reallygoodemails.com, while Beefree remains the company name and the name of the separate developer SDK — so check which product a plan or invoice actually refers to. It is purely a creation environment that never sends, so it always sits on top of your ESP: worth it when the ESP's native editor is the bottleneck (agencies, multi-brand teams, ESP migrations), duplicated effort when it isn't.
tools.best_for: agencies and in-house teams shipping email at volume across brands or ESPs — a dedicated builder with approvals, brand controls and one-click push to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Pardot and HubSpot, sitting above whatever you send with
tools.skip_if: solo senders whose ESP editor already copes — you would be paying for a second tool to do a job your sending platform already does, and you still need the ESP because RGE Studio sends nothing itself
compare_with: Stripo or your ESP's own editor
Stripo is the head-on builder rival — compare template depth, export connectors into YOUR sending stack, and how many real editing seats each plan actually gives you

tools.name: Beehiiv
tools.what_it_does: Newsletter platform with growth, automation, SEO and monetisation tooling, priced by subscriber count. You keep 100% of paid subscriptions where Substack takes 10%; the trade is a steeper start than Substack's near-zero setup and built-in discovery.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-16 from beehiiv's own machine-readable pricing file at beehiiv.com/pricing.md, which states USD) Subscriber-based, and you keep 100% of paid subscriptions — beehiiv takes 0%, against Substack's 10%, leaving only Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30. Launch is $0 up to 2,500 subscribers with unlimited sends. At up to 1,000 subscribers Scale is $49/mo billed monthly or $517 a year (about $43/mo), Max $109/mo or $1,151 a year (about $96/mo). At 10,000 subscribers Scale is $109/mo or $1,151 a year; at 50,000 it is $249/mo or $2,629 a year. The ladder tops out at 100,000 subscribers ($329/mo Scale, $459 Max) and Enterprise is custom above that.
tools.honest_knock: Next to Substack it's more to learn. Substack's built-in discovery network and dead-simple setup are easier if you're starting from zero with no audience and don't care about automation or SEO. Beehiiv's depth is the point, but it's a steeper start.
tools.best_for: newsletter operators who want growth tools, automation, SEO control and ad/referral monetisation — and to keep 100% of subscription revenue
tools.skip_if: you're a beginner starting from zero who wants the simplest setup and Substack's built-in discovery, and don't need automation or SEO

tools.name: BidX
tools.what_it_does: Amazon-advertising automation from German vendor BidX GmbH: bid and budget automation, campaign creation, dayparting and target-ACOS rules for Sponsored Products, Brands and Display, with Amazon DSP and Marketing Cloud reporting and organic-plus-paid share-of-voice tracking in the same dashboard.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-06, read in a live browser on their own pricing page, EUR view) Amazon PPC is sold in three tiers and every one of them is a monthly fee plus an unspecified percentage of connected ad spend: Self Service Platform €495/month, Managed Platform €1,995/month and Managed Service €4,995/month. The tiers differ mainly in how much of a human you get — one monthly strategy call on Self Service, up to two calls and up to 10h of assistance a month on Managed Platform, up to four calls and up to 32h on Managed Service. Amazon DSP is priced separately on the same page: Self Service €495/month and Managed Service €995/month, again plus a percentage of ad spend. Amazon Marketing Cloud is sold as reporting: €295 for the default report, custom reports quote-only. The Share of Voice add-on covers the first 100 keywords free and charges $250 a month per additional 500 keywords. All prices are net with VAT added on top, and the page states that plans are based on an annual commitment paid monthly; the FAQ adds that new customers can take a paid three-month proof-of-concept period first. Walmart Managed Service, high ad-spend volumes and large agencies are contact-sales. Sellers under €10,000 a month in ad spend are pointed to a separate product, BidX Essential, whose own landing page at get.bidx.io/essentials lists $195/month for up to $10K in monthly ad spend — a flat fee with no percentage attached.
tools.honest_knock:
The number that decides your bill is the one number the page does not print. Every Amazon PPC and DSP tier ends with “+ % of connected ad spend per month”, and that percentage appears nowhere — not on the tier cards, not in the footnotes, not in the FAQ. So €495 is a floor, not a price, and nobody spending real money on Amazon ads can work out their monthly cost from this page. Ask for the percentage in writing, and ask whether it is charged on all connected spend or only on what BidX manages, before you get as far as a contract.

The second thing to price is the commitment. The page states plans run on an annual commitment paid monthly, and the FAQ confirms it: the commitment is annual, and the only shorter path on offer is a paid three-month proof of concept. There is no free trial. That makes the cheapest visible door €5,940 a year net of VAT before a cent of the percentage — a very different proposition from the €495 the eye lands on.

Two smaller inconsistencies worth noticing, because they tell you how carefully the price list is maintained. On a page priced in euros, the one add-on with a hard number is quoted in dollars ($250 per extra 500 keywords), so ask which currency you are actually billed in. And BidX Essential — the $195/month product they route smaller sellers to — lives on a completely separate landing page carrying a 2024 copyright line and a different phone number; it is not listed among the tiers on the pricing page itself, so confirm it still exists at that price before you plan around it.
tools.best_for: brands and agencies already spending well past €10,000 a month on Amazon ads who want bid, budget and campaign automation, Amazon DSP and AMC reporting in one platform with a named growth manager attached — and who value a German vendor with EU invoicing, SEPA and direct debit, and support in English and German
tools.skip_if: your ad spend is under roughly $10K a month, because BidX itself routes you to a different product at that size; you want to try before you commit, since there is no free trial and the commitment is annual with only a paid three-month proof of concept as a shorter path; you need your total cost on paper before a sales call, because the percentage of ad spend is unpublished; or you advertise mainly outside Amazon and Walmart
compare_with: the closest peer we cover, and the comparison is unusually clean because both charge a fee plus a percentage of ad spend — the difference is how much of that they will tell you up front. Teikametrics publishes both halves: $149/month billed annually (or $179 monthly) under $10K of ad spend, and 3% of ad spend above $10K on the Advanced tier. BidX publishes the monthly fee and withholds the percentage on every tier. At the small end the gap is stark too: Teikametrics' entry plan is self-serve at $149, while BidX's answer under $10K is the separate Essential product at $195/month. Model both at your own real monthly spend rather than at the headline, and get the BidX percentage in writing before you compare — without it the two are not comparable at all. Verify both current price lists yourself; ours were read on 2026-08-06.

tools.name: Bill.com
tools.what_it_does: Accounts-payable and receivable automation for finance teams with real approval chains. Priced per user from about $45/month, with transaction fees stacked on top — roughly $0.49 ACH, $1.99 cheque, $9.99 international wire, 2.9% card.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) Accounts-payable and receivable plans priced per user: Essentials $49, Team $65 and Corporate $89 per user per month, plus a quote-only Enterprise. The separate Spend and Expense product is $0 per user per month. Transaction fees stack on top of the seat and are where the real cost hides — ACH or ePayment $0.59, a mailed check $1.99, an international USD wire $19.99, an international FX wire free, a virtual card free, instant payment 1.0% with a $9.99 minimum and a $100 maximum, and Pay Faster ACH $11.99. Expedited checks are $24.99 overnight, $19.99 two-day and $14.99 three-day. Paying by card costs 2.9%, and the receiver pays 2.9% on credit or debit card payments.
tools.honest_knock: Per-user pricing plus per-transaction fees means the real cost depends on team size and payment volume — it's built for finance teams with genuine AP workflows and is overkill if you pay a handful of bills a month.
tools.best_for: growing companies with real accounts-payable volume and approval chains that want to automate bill pay and sync to accounting
tools.skip_if: you pay only a few bills a month — your accounting software or a free tool like Melio's base plan covers it without per-seat fees
compare_with: the free-to-start AP alternative for smaller volumes

tools.name: BillingNow
tools.what_it_does: Invoicing and expense tracking with AI — unlimited invoices, expenses, clients and users on one flat $9.99/month plan, made in Geneva.
tools.pricing: (2026) One flat plan: $9.99/mo for unlimited invoices, expenses and clients with an AI assistant, no tiers and no per-user fees. A 3-day free trial (cancel anytime) converts to automatic billing, so set a reminder the day you sign up. SOC 2 Type II certified with European-standard compliant invoices; the site publishes no per-tier pricing page above the single flat plan. (re-verified 18 Jul 2026)
tools.honest_knock: The pricing is genuinely refreshing — one flat plan, no tiers, unlimited users. Two honest watch-outs: the trial is just THREE days and converts to automatic billing (set a reminder the day you sign up), and it’s a young product from a small Geneva maker — weigh ecosystem depth and longevity before migrating your billing history in.
tools.best_for: freelancers and small teams that want unlimited invoicing, expenses and client management at one flat $9.99 with AI assistance — and zero per-user math
tools.skip_if: you need accountant-grade features, payroll or deep integrations (the incumbents’ ecosystems are bigger), or you dislike auto-billing after a 3-day trial
compare_with: FreshBooks is the polished incumbent with tiered plans and client limits; BillingNow’s single flat unlimited plan undercuts it hard — you trade ecosystem depth for radical simplicity

tools.name: Birch
tools.what_it_does: Ad automation for performance marketers (formerly Revealbot): rule-based optimization, automated scaling and creative insights across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat — run and optimize ad campaigns on autopilot.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026, formerly Revealbot) Essential about $49/mo and Pro about $99/mo, both with a $10k monthly ad-spend ceiling; overages meter (~0.49% Essential, ~1% Pro of excess spend, monthly billing only); Enterprise custom with no cap. 14-day free trial, two months free on annual.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is that pricing tracks your ad spend — the tidy $49/$99 tiers assume you stay under a $10k monthly ceiling, and past it you either pay spend-based overages or move to custom Enterprise, so a scaling advertiser's real cost rises with their budget. It's also a power tool: rule-based automation across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat rewards advertisers who know what to automate, and can amplify mistakes if your rules are wrong. For hands-on performance marketers, it's a serious time-saver.
tools.best_for: performance marketers and agencies running real ad budgets who want rule-based automation, scaling and creative insights across Meta, Google, TikTok and Snapchat
tools.skip_if: you run small, simple campaigns a native ads manager handles fine, or you're not comfortable defining automation rules (bad rules scale bad decisions)
compare_with: Madgicx or the native ad managers
comparable ad-automation platforms — Birch's edge is granular rule automation; compare on spend-based pricing at your budget

tools.name: Bitdefender
tools.what_it_does: GravityZone endpoint protection for small business, managed from one console. Roughly $57–96 per device per year at list on an annual plan. The first year is promotional and renews higher, so budget for the renewal rate rather than the intro.
tools.pricing: GravityZone business tiers run roughly $57-$96 per device per year depending on tier (Small Business / Business / Premium), list price on a 5-device annual plan (2026); volume and multi-year discounts apply. First-year pricing is promotional and renews higher.
tools.honest_knock: Like most antivirus, the first-year price is a promo — renewals run notably higher, so budget for the renewal rate, not the intro. It's consistently top-rated on protection, so the real trade-off is cost, not efficacy.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want top-tier, independently-validated endpoint protection managed from one console
tools.skip_if: you're a solo user with basic needs — built-in OS defenses plus good habits may be enough before you pay for a business console
compare_with: Microsoft Defender for Business or ESET

tools.name: Bitvavo
tools.what_it_does: Dutch-regulated, euro-native crypto exchange with deep EUR pairs and an API for automation. No subscription — the base tier under €100k monthly volume runs about 0.15% maker and 0.25% taker, dropping through ten volume tiers. Sign up via our link for €10K fee-free.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-18, read on their own fees page) No subscription — you pay per trade. EUR markets (Category A) run ten volume tiers: 0.15% maker / 0.25% taker below €100,000 of 30-day volume, then 0.10%/0.20% from €100,000, 0.09%/0.18% from €250,000, 0.08%/0.16% from €500,000, 0.05%/0.14% from €1,000,000, 0.03%/0.12% from €2,500,000, 0.01%/0.10% from €5,000,000, 0.00%/0.08% from €10,000,000, 0.00%/0.04% from €25,000,000 and 0.00%/0.02% above €100,000,000. USDC markets (Category B) are a separate schedule from 0.05% maker and taker, and stablecoin pairs (Category C) from 0.10%; Bitvavo states that stablecoin trades do not count towards the 30-day volume that sets your tier. Deposits are free by SEPA, iDEAL/Wero, Apple Pay and Bancontact; a credit card costs 1%, PayPal 2% and EPS or Giropay 1.75%. Margin positions carry a separate hourly borrowing fee, published at 0.0023% an hour on every listed asset, plus a 2% fee if the position is liquidated.
tools.honest_knock: The honest caveats are crypto-wide, not Bitvavo-specific: fees are only part of the cost (spread matters on small orders), and no exchange removes market risk — the platform being cheap and MiCA-regulated doesn't make the assets safe. Note the disclosure: this is one of the few tools here we genuinely run — our own trading system executes on Bitvavo — which is experience, but also means we're an actual customer, not a neutral bystander.
tools.best_for: EU-based traders and builders who want a MiCA-regulated, euro-native exchange with low tiered fees, deep EUR pairs and a solid API for automation
tools.skip_if: you're outside the EU (it's euro-centric), you trade exotic altcoins it doesn't list, or you need derivatives-first infrastructure
compare_with: Kraken is the classic global peer; Bybit leans derivatives — Bitvavo's edge is euro on/off-ramps and EU regulation

tools.name: Blinq
tools.what_it_does: Digital business cards shared by QR code or link, with contacts syncing into your CRM. A free plan covers two cards; Business is about $4.99/user/month annual with a five-user minimum, and the event lead-capture add-on starts near $199/month.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free forever for individuals (2 cards, unlimited QR sharing). For individuals, Premium is $9.99 a month billed monthly or $7.33 billed annually. For teams, Business is $6.99 per user a month billed monthly or $4.99 per user billed annually, with a 5-user minimum, adding CRM sync, templates and custom reporting. Enterprise is custom. A lead-capture add-on for events starts around $199/mo. Note the individual plan costs more per person than the team plan — if there are five of you, the team tier is both cheaper per head and more capable.
tools.honest_knock: The core product is honestly cheap — the price jump hides in the event lead-capture add-on (~$199/mo), which is where teams that live on trade shows actually get value. And a truth about all digital cards: the wow factor works precisely because adoption is still low; the durable value is the CRM sync (contacts flowing automatically into your pipeline), so judge Business tier by that integration, not by the tap-to-share trick.
tools.best_for: teams and field-sales orgs that want consistent, branded digital cards with contacts syncing straight into the CRM — and events teams via the capture add-on
tools.skip_if: you're an individual (the free tier honestly covers you), or your networking volume doesn't justify per-user pricing
compare_with: the digital-card peer set — compare CRM integrations and whether you need hardware (NFC cards) versus pure app

tools.name: Bokun
tools.what_it_does: Booking management for tours and activities, by Tripadvisor. Manage availability, channel sales and online bookings in one place — built for experience businesses.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) A free version plus paid plans from about $49/mo (Start). Service fee on direct bookings varies by plan (~1.5% Start, 1.25% Plus, 1% Premium); crucially, zero Bokun booking fee on Viator reservations. Free trial available.
tools.honest_knock: Bokun is a Tripadvisor/Viator company, and that's both the draw and the lock-in: distribution to Viator and 2,600+ resellers is excellent, but you're building your booking backbone inside one OTA's ecosystem, and the per-booking service fee on direct sales is a real cut on top of the subscription. If most of your business is direct, weigh that fee; if you live on OTA distribution, the Viator advantage is hard to beat.
tools.best_for: tour, activity and experience operators who want booking management plus wide OTA distribution (Viator, GetYourGuide and more) from one dashboard
tools.skip_if: you're a tiny operator taking a handful of direct bookings where the fees and setup outweigh the reach, or you want to stay off OTA rails entirely
compare_with: close tour-booking peers — compare direct-booking fees and how much you rely on Viator/Tripadvisor distribution

tools.name: Bolt Business
tools.what_it_does: Business travel and mobility management. Give your team expense-tracked rides and travel with centralized billing and reporting.
tools.pricing: No subscription, no activation cost (2026): you pay per ride/rental taken, with consolidated monthly billing, spend limits and policy controls included. Genuinely commitment-free to pilot.
tools.honest_knock: The honest boundary is geography: Bolt's network is Europe/Africa-centric across 600+ cities, so US-only operations should look elsewhere, and ride availability varies by city — pilot it on your team's actual routes. Pricing is dynamic like all ride-hailing; the business layer adds control and receipts, not fixed corporate fares, so budget-predictability comes from your spend limits, not from locked prices.
tools.best_for: companies with European/African travel footprints that want employee rides centrally billed, policy-controlled and expense-integrated — at zero platform cost
tools.skip_if: US-only operations (network coverage), or you need guaranteed fixed-price corporate transport contracts
compare_with: the direct rival — Uber wins on US/global coverage, Bolt typically on per-ride cost in its home markets; run both where they overlap

tools.name: Bookyourdata
tools.what_it_does: B2B email lists and verified contact data on demand. Build targeted prospect lists with verified business emails and pay only for the contacts you need.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page) Pay-as-you-go, no subscription: one credit is one full contact. The published pack table runs 250 credits for $99 ($0.40 each), 500 for $159, 1,000 for $299 ($0.30), 2,500 for $599, 5,000 for $799 ($0.16), 10,000 for $999 ($0.10), 25,000 for $2,099 ($0.08), 50,000 for $3,699 ($0.07), 100,000 for $5,499 ($0.05) and on up to 2,500,000 for $24,999 ($0.010), with anything larger quoted. New accounts get a Free Pack of 10 credits once, with no card. Credits never expire and the 97% deliverability guarantee refunds credits, not money. BeSpoke, the hand-built private list service, is priced separately from $499 for 1,000 records.
tools.honest_knock: The model is honest — no subscription, credits keep, bad data refunded — so the real scrutiny belongs on usage: bought lists are only as good as your targeting and your sending infrastructure, and cold-emailing purchased contacts has legal boundaries that vary by country (GDPR territory especially). The data being accurate doesn't make the campaign compliant; that part is yours.
tools.best_for: sporadic, project-based prospecting where a subscription would idle — buy exactly the verified contacts you need, when you need them
tools.skip_if: you prospect continuously at volume (subscription databases price better), or your market is EU-consumer-adjacent where purchased-list outreach gets legally delicate
compare_with: subscription databases vs pay-per-contact — the crossover is usage frequency; occasional buyers win with BookYourData, daily prospectors with Apollo

tools.name: Boulevard
tools.what_it_does: Booking, point of sale and client management for salons, spas and self-care businesses.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced per location per month: Essentials $140 (shown as discounted from $176), Premier $234 (from $293), Prestige $328 (from $410). Enterprise is a bespoke quote. Paid add-ons sit on top, also per location — the page lists items at $45 and $65 per month per location, ePrescribe at $45 per prescriber, and email marketing at $0.01 per email beyond the included allowance. Every tier's button is 'Get a demo': there is no self-serve checkout at any price.
tools.honest_knock: Two things about this price list. It is per location, so the arithmetic for a second salon is not a volume discount, it is double — and the add-ons are per location too, which compounds it. And every listed price is shown struck through against a higher 'normally' figure, footnoted on 18 August 2026 as a limited-time summer offer for new customers only; treat the higher number as the list price a renewal may return to and the lower one as an introductory rate with an end date you should ask about. The third thing is not a price at all: you cannot buy this without booking a demo. That is a signal about how the deal is done, and it means the published numbers are a starting point rather than a checkout.
tools.best_for: salons, spas and clinics with staff to schedule and a front desk to run — the per-location pricing works out fine for one busy site
tools.skip_if: you are a solo practitioner with a calendar and a card reader, because the entry tier at $140 a month is priced for a team, and multi-location owners should price the add-ons per site before comparing
compare_with: the standing comparison in salon and spa software — compare per-location totals with your add-ons switched on, not the entry sticker

tools.name: Bouncer
tools.what_it_does: Email-list verification sold as credits that never expire: $8 per 1,000 (also the minimum purchase), falling to about $2 per 1,000 at the top volume. Unknowns and duplicates are not charged. Treat 'accept-all' domain results as unverified.
tools.pricing: Email verification credits, pay-as-you-go and never expiring (re-verified 2026-08-11): $8 per 1,000, which is also the minimum purchase, then $35 per 5,000, $60 per 10,000, $250 per 50,000, $400 per 100,000, $750 per 250,000, $1,250 per 500,000 and $2,000 per 1,000,000 - about $2 per 1,000 at the top volume. The same calculator offers a monthly-subscription mode for verification that Bouncer states is discounted against pay-as-you-go; it publishes no fixed monthly tiers, so price it at your own volume. 100 free credits to test; duplicates and 'unknown' results aren't charged. The $25/$125/$250 per month tiers are the separate Deliverability Kit, and Shield is a separate real-time product.
tools.honest_knock: Not charging for unknowns and duplicates is genuinely fair — many rivals do. The honest framing for any verifier: it removes invalid addresses, which protects deliverability, but it can't make a cold list warm or a purchased list legitimate. Verify before every big send (lists decay measurably per month), and treat 'accept-all' domain results as the gamble they are, not as verified.
tools.best_for: email marketers and outbound teams that clean lists regularly and want accurate verification with fair credit mechanics (no expiry, no double-charging)
tools.skip_if: you send rarely to a stable opt-in list (occasional pay-as-you-go beats any subscription), or your problem is content/reputation rather than list hygiene
compare_with: the verification peer set — accuracy claims are near-identical; compare per-1,000 rates at your volume and the unknown/duplicate billing policy

tools.name: Bread & Butter
tools.what_it_does: Lead-intelligence platform with server-side tracking: captures the full visitor journey from the first visit, then enriches, scores and nurtures the moment someone submits an email — verified identities instead of IP-based company guesses. 30-day full trial, then a genuinely usable freemium tier; Pro from $49 per website.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against breadbutter.io) (2026) Fully functional 30-day free trial that moves to a freemium tier after (200 lead profiles, unlimited traffic). AI Enabled Pro $49 per month PER WEBSITE: full AI lead intelligence, enrichment, intent scoring, nurture and attribution with 5,000 lead profiles. AI capacity scales via add-on blocks: +$49/mo per Scale-AI-Enrichment block (+10,000 compute credits) and +$89/mo per deep-profile-research block (100 → 300 profiles/month). Enterprise is custom.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters to watch: it prices per WEBSITE (multi-site setups multiply the $49) and the AI features run on compute-credit blocks that stack as usage grows. On privacy — refined twice in open dialogue with the vendor (16 Jul 2026, verified against their docs): the anonymous journey IS tracked from the first visit, server-side via their site plugin — so ad-blockers and Safari’s ITP don’t strip it the way they kill client-side scripts (the vendor estimates 30-50% of high-value traffic is lost to client-side blocking). What stays dormant until someone submits an email is identity resolution — the ‘hand-raise’ that connects the captured history to a verified person. You still owe normal GDPR care on enriched data, and the real trade-off is simply this: no IP-based guessing at which company an anonymous visitor works for.
tools.best_for: marketing and revenue teams that want engaged visitors — people who filled a form or left an email — automatically enriched, scored and nurtured, on a genuinely usable freemium tier
tools.skip_if: you want IP-based company guessing at anonymous visitors — that’s a different tool class (Leadfeeder-style) with a different accuracy and compliance profile — or you run many small sites, where per-website pricing adds up
compare_with: Leadfeeder guesses the company behind anonymous IPs — useful when it lands, though remote work and VPNs often return an ISP instead; Bread & Butter tracks behaviour server-side from the first visit and resolves identity when a visitor hands over an email. Pick by what your sales team acts on: company guesses or verified people

tools.name: Breezy HR
tools.what_it_does: Recruiting and applicant tracking made simple. Post jobs to 50+ boards, manage candidates on a visual pipeline, and automate scheduling and screening.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A genuinely permanent free Bootstrap plan: one open position, unlimited users. Paid, annual against monthly: Startup $157/mo or $189, Growth $273/mo or $329, Business $439/mo or $529, plus a custom-quoted Pro tier. Every paid tier includes unlimited users and unlimited positions, which is what separates it from per-seat applicant tracking. Onboarding is a separate product, starting at $49/mo for automated role-based workflows that sync with the ATS.
tools.honest_knock: The jump from free (one position) to the first paid tier is steep if you only hire occasionally — the free plan is genuinely usable, so live in it until you're filling several roles at once.
tools.best_for: small teams hiring for a few roles at once that want a visual, drag-and-drop pipeline without enterprise-ATS pricing
tools.skip_if: you hire once or twice a year — the free single-position plan is plenty, and the paid jump only pays off with concurrent open roles

tools.name: Brevo
tools.what_it_does: Email, SMS and a light CRM, priced by monthly send volume rather than contact count — cheaper for a large list you email selectively. Free forever at 300 emails a day with unlimited contacts; paid from about $9/month. Model your real send volume if you mail frequently.
tools.pricing: Free forever (300 emails/day, unlimited contacts); paid Starter from about $9/mo and Business from $18/mo, scaling by monthly send volume rather than contact count (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Charging by sends rather than contacts is genuinely cheaper for big lists you email infrequently — but the free daily cap and add-on fees mean high-frequency senders should model their real send volume first.
tools.best_for: businesses with large contact lists who email selectively and want to pay by send volume, not list size
tools.skip_if: you email your whole list daily — the per-send model can flip from cheap to costly at high frequency

tools.name: Bright Data
tools.what_it_does: The web data platform trusted by enterprises. Collect public web data at scale with proxies, ready-made datasets and scraping APIs — fuel for your market research and AI projects.
tools.pricing: Usage-based (re-verified 11 Aug 2026): residential proxies start at $4.00/GB with no commitment, against a struck-through $8 — the $2.50/GB rate the overview page leads with is the $1,999/month tier, not the entry price; datacenter from $0.90/IP and ISP from $1.30/IP. API side: Unlocker, Crawl and SERP APIs from $1/1k requests (free tiers available), Scraper APIs $0.75/1k records (sale; list $1), Data Firehose $0.20/1k, Datasets from $250/100k records; managed offerings from $1,500/mo (Managed Data Acquisition) and Retail Insights from $2,000/mo.
tools.honest_knock: This is enterprise-grade web data infrastructure at enterprise-grade prices — the per-GB meter looks small until you multiply by real scraping volume, and the committed tiers only pay off if your usage is steady. The bigger honest note is compliance: Bright Data is strict about KYC and use-cases (a feature, not a bug), and whatever you collect still has to respect the target sites' terms and applicable law. Budget legal thought alongside the gigabytes.
tools.best_for: data teams and enterprises with real, ongoing web-data needs (pricing intelligence, market research) that justify committed volume and pass use-case vetting
tools.skip_if: you need occasional small scrapes (Browse.ai-class tools or datasets are far cheaper), or your use-case wouldn't survive a compliance review
compare_with: the premium proxy/data peers — compare effective per-GB at your committed volume and the quality on your specific target sites

tools.name: Browse.ai
tools.what_it_does: No-code web scraping and data extraction. Turn any website into an automated data pipeline or spreadsheet automatically.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against browse.ai) Credit-metered (2026): Free ~50 credits/mo (2 sites); Personal about $19/mo annual (12,000 credits/yr, 5 sites); Professional ~$69/mo annual (60,000 credits, 10 sites); Premium custom (600k+ credits, managed). A credit ≈ 10 extracted rows; premium sites cost more credits.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest realities of no-code scraping: credits burn faster than expected (row counts, screenshots and 'premium' sites all multiply the meter — monitor a big site daily and do the math first), and scrapers break when sites redesign — robots need maintenance, which is your time even when the tool is no-code. Also check the terms of the sites you monitor; 'technically possible' and 'permitted' aren't the same thing.
tools.best_for: ops, research and growth teams that want to monitor competitors, prices or listings and pipe structured web data into sheets without writing scrapers
tools.skip_if: you need one-off extractions (free tools or a VA are cheaper), or mission-critical pipelines where you'd rather own the code than rent the robot
compare_with: close scraping platforms — Apify is more developer-oriented; compare credit math on YOUR row volumes and site list

tools.name: BuddyPunch
tools.what_it_does: Time clock and employee time tracking for hourly teams. Track hours, breaks, PTO and overtime with GPS and photo punch-in, and export payroll-ready reports.
tools.pricing: Per-user plus a base fee: Starter about $5.49/user/mo, Pro $6.99, Enterprise $11.99, each with a roughly $19/mo base fee (2026). GPS and scheduling are add-ons on lower tiers and a payroll add-on costs extra. 14-day trial, no card.
tools.honest_knock: That flat $19 base fee makes it pricey for very small teams — at three or four users the base fee dominates the bill, so it's better value once you're past a handful of employees.
tools.best_for: small-to-mid teams that need straightforward employee time tracking with GPS and payroll-ready exports
tools.skip_if: you're a team of two or three — the fixed base fee makes the per-head cost sting until you scale up

tools.name: BugHerd
tools.what_it_does: Visual bug tracking and website feedback. Let clients and teams point-and-click to report issues right on the page, turned into trackable tasks.
tools.pricing: Standard about $42/mo (5 members), Studio ~$67/mo (10), Premium ~$125/mo (25), plus custom Enterprise — all with unlimited projects and unlimited client users; annual billing runs $500/$800/$1,500 per year (two months free), extra members $6.60/user/mo. Free trial (re-verified 2026-07-19).
tools.honest_knock: The per-team-member tiers are the thing to size honestly: your clients report for free as guests, but everyone on your side who works the feedback needs a seat, so a growing agency steps up tiers. It's deliberately a visual-feedback layer, not a full project-management or dev-issue tracker — most teams run it alongside Jira/Trello rather than instead of. The new MCP feature is genuinely interesting but currently beta: treat AI-agents-triaging-your-feedback as a bonus to evaluate, not the reason to buy.
tools.best_for: web agencies and site teams that want clients to point-and-click feedback directly on the page — and, new in 2026, want AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor and others) to read, triage and action that feedback via BugHerd's MCP server, free in beta
tools.skip_if: you don't work with external clients or website revisions (a plain issue tracker is enough), or you need deep dev-workflow tracking that belongs in Jira
compare_with: close visual-feedback rivals — BugHerd currently stands out with its MCP/AI-agent integration; compare per-seat costs at your team size

tools.name: Buzz.ai
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered outbound platform: prompt it and it finds intent-ready buyers, writes multichannel sequences and books the meetings — per-seat plans with monthly credit allowances and a free start.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Core is $125 per seat a month with 500 credits per seat, currently on a launch offer at $75 a month for the first three months (and $75 per seat on annual billing, which the page shows as 25% off). AI Employee is $795 per seat a month with 5,000 credits, and the pricing page carries its own warning that it 'moves to $1,000/mo soon — lock in now'. Enterprise is custom and there is a free start. Treat the $795 as a rate with an announced increase attached rather than a settled price.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters run at once: seats AND credits — the $125 seat includes 500 credits a month, and real outbound volume means credit packages on top, so budget past the sticker. Watch the launch math too: $75 is a 3-month teaser that steps up to $125, and the top tier openly signposts a rise from $795 to $1,000 — decide on the post-rise price, not the promo. And the honest fundamental for any AI-SDR: it only books meetings as good as your list and offer, so keep a human reviewing what goes out in your name.
tools.best_for: GTM teams that want AI to run outbound end-to-end — prompt-driven prospecting of intent-ready buyers, multichannel sequences and meeting booking without adding SDR headcount
tools.skip_if: you send low-volume, hand-crafted outreach (per-seat-plus-credits is overkill), or you're not ready to QA an AI that writes to your market on your behalf
compare_with: Reply.io is mature multichannel sequencing you drive yourself and lemlist leads on deliverability and personalization — Buzz.ai's pitch is the autonomous AI-SDR layer that does the driving for you

tools.name: Bybit
tools.what_it_does: Crypto exchange covering spot, perpetuals and options. No subscription — spot is 0.1% maker and taker for non-VIP, derivatives around 0.02% and 0.055%, with volume tiers cutting lower. Funding rates on perpetuals are a recurring cost the fee table does not show, and availability differs per country.
tools.pricing: No subscription — per-trade fees, re-verified 2026-08-17 against Bybit's own fee schedule. At VIP 0 (non-VIP): spot 0.1000% maker and 0.1000% taker; perpetuals and futures 0.0200% maker and 0.0550% taker; options 0.0200% maker and 0.0300% taker. The VIP ladder cuts those toward zero — at Supreme VIP spot is 0.0300% maker and 0.0450% taker, derivatives 0.0000% maker and 0.0300% taker, options 0.0050% and 0.0150%. Note that the top derivatives maker rate is zero rather than a rebate: we found no negative maker fee in the published table. Your VIP level is set by either your asset balance or your trading volume over the past 30 days, whichever qualifies you higher, so one of the two is enough. Special trading zones have their own tables.
tools.honest_knock: Derivatives are the draw and the danger: leverage cuts both ways, and funding rates on perpetuals are a real recurring cost the fee table doesn't show. Regulation-wise, check what Bybit may offer in YOUR jurisdiction before funding an account — availability and product range differ per country, and that's the part most fee comparisons skip.
tools.best_for: active traders who want deep liquidity, low derivatives fees and a broad product range (spot, perps, options) with volume-tiered discounts
tools.skip_if: you're a buy-and-hold beginner (a simple euro-native exchange is safer territory), or derivatives aren't available to you locally
compare_with: Bitvavo is the euro on/off-ramp specialist, Kraken the regulated all-rounder — Bybit wins on derivatives depth

tools.name: Calilio
tools.what_it_does: Cloud phone system with international numbers and call menus, from about $12/user/month annual on Standard. Numbers, minutes and SMS meter separately from a credit balance, so an active team's real bill sits above the per-seat price.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Standard $15 per user/mo, or $12 billed annually ($144 a year); Premium $35 per user/mo, or $28 annually ($336 a year); Enterprise custom. Annual billing saves 20%. Each plan includes a stated value of free calls and SMS/MMS to US and Canada numbers — $6.75 on Standard and $33.74 on Premium — and beyond that calls and SMS draw from a credit balance, with numbers billed separately. Standard suits solopreneurs and small businesses; Premium is aimed at growing businesses, franchises and call centres.
tools.honest_knock: The subscription is the platform, not the talking: numbers, minutes and SMS meter separately from a credit balance, so an active calling team's real bill sits meaningfully above the per-seat sticker — model a month of your actual call volume before comparing vendors. It's a young player in a crowded VoIP field; the price is keen, so test call quality on your real routes in the trial.
tools.best_for: startups and small teams that want a modern, affordable cloud phone system with international numbers and clean dashboards
tools.skip_if: you need a battle-tested enterprise contact center with deep integrations and SLAs, or your call volume makes metered credits unpredictable
compare_with: close low-cost VoIP rivals — compare the metered call rates on the countries you actually call, not the seat price

tools.name: CallHippo
tools.what_it_does: AI-driven business phone system. Virtual numbers in 50+ countries, power dialer, call analytics and AI agents — set up your sales and support calling in minutes. Its omnichannel inbox threads voice, WhatsApp, SMS, email, Instagram and Telegram into one conversation per customer.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page in euros) Starter €19/user/mo, Professional €29 and Ultimate €39 on monthly billing for a 1-4 user team, above a genuinely free Basic tier where you pay only for the numbers. Unlimited landline and mobile minutes start at Starter with 100 SMS; call recordings, AI voicemail transcription and multilingual IVR at Professional with 500 SMS; smart DID, multilevel and holiday routing at Ultimate with 1,000 SMS. 10-day free trial on the paid tiers. The page carries selectors for currency, number region and team size plus a yearly toggle, and the tiers are priced per currency rather than converted — the same grid read in dollars on 19 July 2026 showed $19, $30 and $42. Call-centre 'Pro Suite' tiers run $32-48/user/mo annual and Enterprise is custom at 50+ users. AI copilot, AI voice agent and CNAM are paid add-ons.
tools.honest_knock: 'Unlimited calling' is unlimited to the US and Canada — international minutes meter separately, so teams calling Europe or Asia should price their real destinations first. The plan grid is busy (two suites, add-ons for the dialer and AI), which makes comparisons slippery: list the five features you actually need and find the cheapest tier that truly contains all five.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious sales/support teams wanting virtual numbers in 50+ countries with a free entry point and CRM integrations
tools.skip_if: your calling is mostly international at volume (metered minutes stack up), or you want one simple plan without add-on shopping
compare_with: the budget-VoIP peer group — decide on per-country call rates and which features are add-ons vs included

tools.name: CallRail
tools.what_it_does: Call tracking and attribution — which campaigns, keywords and ads produce phone calls and form leads. Plans run about $50–195/month, but included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest and overages meter at roughly $0.05 a local minute. It is an attribution layer, not a phone system or CRM.
tools.pricing: (2026) Four plans about $50–$195/mo: Call Tracking $50, +Conversation Intelligence or +Form Tracking $100, Complete $195. Prices assume tight limits (~250 local minutes, 5 numbers, 25 SMS); overages meter (~$0.05/local minute, ~$3 per extra number). 14-day trial, no free plan.
tools.honest_knock: The headline price is a floor, not a ceiling — the included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest, so an active campaign quickly hits metered overages that meaningfully lift the bill. It's also specifically an attribution tool: it proves which marketing drives calls and leads, but it isn't a phone system or CRM, so you add it alongside those, not instead of them.
tools.best_for: marketers and agencies that need to prove which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and multi-touch attribution
tools.skip_if: you don't run enough paid marketing to need call-level attribution, or your call volume would push overages past the value of the insight
compare_with: WhatConverts or a platform's native tracking
comparable attribution tools — compare on included minutes and how your real call volume meters

tools.name: Campaign Monitor
tools.what_it_does: Email campaigns with strong templates and client-friendly management for brands and agencies. Priced per contact rather than per send: Essentials at 10,000 contacts runs about $89/month, so dormant subscribers bill like active ones. Automation depth is lighter than dedicated platforms.
tools.pricing: Contact-based, on three tiers — Lite (with a monthly send cap of about five times your contact count), Essentials (unlimited sends) and Premier (priority and phone support). We could not re-verify a plan amount on 2026-08-16: the page publishes no plan price until you pick a contact count in its slider, and the only figure in the page itself is the Website Builder add-on, at €9 a month from an EU address (our July and August captures both read the same line as $10). There is no free plan; the trial runs 30 days with 500 contacts. Older readings put Lite around $12-13 a month and Essentials around $29-31 at 500 contacts, climbing steeply with list size — treat those as indicative and take your own figure from the slider. Note also that the product is now listed as Campaign Monitor by Marigold.
tools.honest_knock: You pay for contacts, not sends — so a large, quiet list costs the same as a large, active one, and dormant subscribers are literally a line item. Clean your list before comparing prices anywhere. Campaign Monitor's strength is polished, agency-friendly email; its automation depth is lighter than dedicated marketing-automation platforms, so know which of the two jobs you're actually buying.
tools.best_for: brands and agencies that want beautiful, reliable email campaigns with strong templates and client-friendly management, priced per contact
tools.skip_if: you need deep behavioral automation and CRM-grade journeys (ActiveCampaign-class tools fit better), or your list is large but low-engagement — prune first
compare_with: Mailchimp is the closest general peer, ActiveCampaign wins on automation depth — compare at YOUR list size, since contact pricing diverges fast

tools.name: Campaigner
tools.what_it_does: Email and SMS marketing for mid-market senders with larger lists. The useful features start high — automation and API only arrive on Essential at about $179/month, while Starter at $59 is a sending tool rather than an automation platform. Contact-based pricing bills dormant subscribers too.
tools.pricing: (2026) Contact-based: Starter about $59/mo (5,000 contacts, no automation/API); Essential ~$179/mo (25k contacts, dynamic content, 1,000 SMS); Advanced ~$649/mo (100k, workflows, API); an eCommerce plan runs ~$79.95-149.95/mo. 30-day trial requires a card and auto-converts.
tools.honest_knock: Two paragraphs of fine print worth reading: automation and API only arrive at the $179 tier — the Starter plan is a sending tool, not a marketing-automation platform — and the trial auto-converts to paid if you don't actively cancel, which tells you something about the retention strategy. Contact-based pricing also means dormant subscribers bill like active ones; prune first.
tools.best_for: mid-market senders with larger lists that want mature email plus SMS workflows and are comfortable at the Essential tier and up
tools.skip_if: you're small (the useful features start at $179/mo) or you dislike card-required auto-converting trials on principle
compare_with: Campaign Monitor shares the polish, ActiveCampaign beats it on automation depth — compare at your real list size and feature floor

tools.name: Capsule
tools.what_it_does: Deliberately simple CRM for small businesses: contacts, pipeline and tasks. Free for 250 contacts and two users, then about $21/user/month on Starter. The simplicity is the product — advanced automation, deep reporting and integrations thin out, and a scaling sales org can outgrow it.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free tier for 250 contacts and 2 users; then Starter, Growth, Advanced and Ultimate at roughly $21, $38, $60 and $75 per user a month, with a 14-day trial that needs no card. One correction from today's page: annual billing saves up to 14%, not the 15-20% our earlier note carried. The plan figures themselves render client-side, so treat the per-user amounts as our dated reading and take yours from the live selector. A Marketing add-on is sold alongside the CRM, and the AI features can be switched off in your account if you would rather not use them.
tools.honest_knock: Capsule's simplicity is the product: it deliberately does less than the CRM giants, which is why small teams actually use it. The honest flip side — advanced automation, deep reporting and integrations thin out at the top tiers, and a scaling sales org can outgrow it. Buy it to finally have a CRM the team fills in; plan a migration path if you're heading toward enterprise process complexity.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want a clean, genuinely simple CRM for contacts, pipeline and tasks — one the team will actually keep updated
tools.skip_if: you need marketing automation, complex territory logic or enterprise reporting (bigger platforms exist for a reason)
compare_with: the SMB-CRM peer group — Capsule wins on calm simplicity, Pipedrive on pipeline power; pick by which your team will really use

tools.name: Carbon6
tools.what_it_does: A suite of Amazon seller tools sold per product rather than as one subscription: Seller Investigators (FBA reimbursement recovery), ChargeGuard (1P vendor recovery for chargeback fees, shortages and accruals), PixelMe, DSP Prime and PPC Entourage (advertising), SoStocked (demand and inventory planning), ScanUnlimited (wholesale sourcing), plus ManageByStats, D8aDriven, AMZAlert and SellerAssist. Ownership matters here: SPS Commerce bought Carbon6 in Feb 2025 and folded the 1P deduction-recovery work into spscommerce.com, then transferred the 3P Amazon-seller business to Carbon6 on 30 Jun 2026 — the suite is sold under the Carbon6 brand again, with the partner programme rebranding from SPS to Carbon6 on 24 Aug 2026 and commission terms unchanged.
tools.pricing: What we can verify on the vendor's own pages today (checked 21 Jul 2026): SoStocked lists ProfitFlow at $97/mo and ProfitFlow + Inventory at "starting at" $250/mo; ScanUnlimited lists a free Limited tier, Unlimited at $720/yr and Unlimited Plus at $1,080/yr. SPS Ad Performance (the former PixelMe) publishes no price at all — it is contact-sales only. The 3P FBA-reimbursement service is a contingency arrangement, and since the business changed hands it publishes its rate again under its own name: Seller Investigators by Carbon6 states a 25% commission charged only after Amazon has deposited recovered funds, stated twice on its own site (read 2026-08-15), after a free 48-hour audit with no obligation. Our older suite-level figures — entry tools from about $49/mo, PixelMe from about $500/mo with a 6-month minimum, and $300-500+/mo for a working stack — stay withdrawn: none of those is verifiable against a live authoritative source today.
tools.honest_knock: The honest headline here is not pricing but ownership — and it has moved again, this time in the reader's favour. SPS Commerce bought Carbon6 for roughly $210M on 7 Feb 2025 and retired the brand into spscommerce.com. On 30 Jun 2026 it sold the entire 3P (Amazon marketplace seller) revenue-recovery business for $9.5M cash, booking an estimated $20M loss, and named no buyer at the time. There is a name now. The partner-programme notice we received on 17 Aug 2026, from Carbon6's own partnerships contact, states that SPS transferred ownership of the 3P business to Carbon6, that commission terms and payouts are unchanged, that existing links were redirected to the Carbon6 tool sites on 14 Aug 2026, and that the programme itself rebrands from SPS to Carbon6 on 24 Aug 2026. Reading carbon6.io on 17 Aug 2026 matches that: the whole suite is on sale there again as "by Carbon6". Read the two purchase numbers carefully, because they are not the same thing — the $210M bought the whole Carbon6 stack, the $9.5M was the 3P arm alone, and offloading it at a book loss seventeen months in still tells you how it performed. What remains undisclosed is who stands behind the Carbon6 entity itself, so the question is answered one level down and no further. Two more things to hold: Reuters reported on 23 Jun 2026 that SPS hired Morgan Stanley to explore a sale of itself under activist pressure, talks early and no deal assured; and the 1P side is no longer a clean split, because SPS kept the deduction-recovery business it bought while Carbon6's own site now lists ChargeGuard for Amazon 1P vendor recovery. Ask which entity your 1P work would sit with before you sign. For 3P reimbursements the July advice has expired — you can name the counterparty on your contract again.
tools.best_for: Amazon sellers who want reimbursements, advertising, inventory and sourcing tools from one vendor and are content to buy them tool by tool — the suite trades under the Carbon6 brand again since 30 Jun 2026, so there is a named counterparty on the contract
tools.skip_if: you want one flat subscription and one invoice: this is a suite priced per tool, each with its own contract, and the pieces have moved between owners twice since Feb 2025 — check which entity your existing agreement actually names before you add another one
compare_with: Helium 10 is the flat-priced seller suite with published tiers; GETIDA is the independent FBA-reimbursement specialist — against a suite that has changed hands twice in eighteen months, both still win on continuity, though the owner question itself is no longer open: the 3P business trades as Carbon6 again since 30 Jun 2026, on unchanged commission terms

tools.name: Checkr
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered background check and screening platform for hiring: fast criminal, employment and identity verification with automated adjudication and ATS integrations — speeds up onboarding while staying FCRA-compliant.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Pay-as-you-go per report, no subscription: Basic $29.99, Essential $59.99 and Complete $94.99 per report, with Enterprise quote-only. Tenant screening is priced separately at $24.99, $34.99 and $44.99 per report, and personal checks start from $49.99. Add-ons stack on top: MVR report $9.50 per check, identity verification $4.99 per check, employment verification $59.95 and income plus employment $64.95, billed per verification with no commitment or contract.
tools.honest_knock: The headline per-check price is rarely what you actually pay — passthrough fees vary wildly by county and search type, so budget for the effective cost, not the advertised one. It's overkill unless you hire at real volume.
tools.best_for: companies hiring hourly or gig workers at volume that need fast, API-driven, compliant background checks
tools.skip_if: you hire only a handful of people a year — a one-off check from a simpler provider costs less hassle than onboarding a screening platform

tools.name: ChemiCloud
tools.what_it_does: Lightning-fast cloud hosting with free migrations, daily backups, and 24/7 expert support. Perfect balance of performance and affordability for growing businesses.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Shared hosting is on a 10th-birthday promotion as we write: Starter $1.49/mo, Pro $2.49/mo and Turbo $3.49/mo, each about a dollar below the $2.49 / $3.49 / $4.49 we captured in July and August, with free domain year one, free SSL, daily backups and a 45-day money-back guarantee. The renewal is the number that matters and it did not move: those same three plans renew at $11.95, $17.95 and $21.95 a month, so the step up from the sale price is roughly eightfold and from the standard intro roughly fivefold. Managed WordPress starts at $15/mo ($12.50 paid yearly) with a $1 trial, reseller from $19.95/mo and managed cloud VPS from $32.95/mo. Note there is no monthly billing option on the promotional rates — these are per-month figures on a longer term.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is the one every budget host shares: the headline price is an introductory rate, and renewals land roughly three times higher, so judge it on the renewal cost, not the sign-up teaser. Support and performance reviews are genuinely strong for the price band, but this is shared/managed hosting — if you need serious dedicated resources or enterprise SLAs, you'll outgrow the cheap tiers. Great value to start, just enter with eyes open on renewal.
tools.best_for: small businesses, freelancers and growing sites that want fast, well-supported managed shared or WordPress hosting at a low starting price
tools.skip_if: you need enterprise-grade dedicated infrastructure and SLAs, or you'll be unhappy when the low intro rate renews at standard pricing
compare_with: comparable managed hosts — ChemiCloud competes hard on intro price and support; compare renewal rates and performance for your stack

tools.name: Circle
tools.what_it_does: Community platform for creator businesses: discussions, courses, events, memberships and messaging in one branded home — plus a no-code website builder, branded iOS/Android apps, email marketing, a member CRM, built-in payments and AI agents that answer member questions.
tools.pricing: (2026) Professional about $89/mo billed annually ($129 monthly), Business $199/mo annual, Enterprise around $419/mo annual, plus a custom Circle Plus tier for fully branded apps. On top of the subscription Circle takes a commission on every sale you make through the platform (roughly 2% on Professional, 1% on Business, 0.5% on Plus) plus standard Stripe/PayPal processing, and the Email Hub is a paid add-on around $99/mo for 10,000 contacts. 14-day free trial, but no always-free option.
tools.honest_knock: The sticker is only the entry: Circle keeps a commission on every sale on top of Stripe's processing fees, and email marketing is a separate add-on — so a monetized community's real bill runs meaningfully past the plan price. Model it at your actual sales volume before choosing a tier.
tools.best_for: creators and brands running a paid community — courses, memberships, events and discussions in one branded home, with a built-in payments stack and even branded mobile apps
tools.skip_if: you only need a casual chat space (Discord-style) or your margins are thin on high sales volume — the platform commission plus processing fees stack against you
compare_with: Skool wins on radical simplicity and flat pricing, Mighty Networks on affordable entry; Circle wins on breadth: branded apps, email, CRM, AI agents and a real payments stack

tools.name: Claude
tools.what_it_does: Anthropic's AI assistant for writing, coding, analysis and long-document work — strong reasoning and a careful, direct tone rather than an eager-to-please one. Free tier plus Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans, and a per-token API (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) for builders.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-07-31) Free tier at $0 with daily usage caps (2026); Pro at $20/mo (about $17 billed annually) lifts the limits and adds Projects; Max at $100/mo (roughly 5x Pro usage) or $200/mo (around 20x) for heavy daily users; Team from $25/seat/mo Standard (min 5 seats, $20 annually) with Premium at $125/seat adding Claude Code; Enterprise custom. The API is separate, billed per token across the Opus, Sonnet and Haiku models.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is usage limits: even on Pro you can hit a ceiling mid-session on a heavy day, and the step up to Max is a real $100 to $200 a month — you're buying headroom, not extra features. It also doesn't generate images, so if that's your main need it's the wrong tool, and its third-party plugin ecosystem is smaller than ChatGPT's.
tools.best_for: developers, writers, analysts and researchers who want best-in-class reasoning, coding and long-document work — and a model that's careful and direct rather than eager to please
tools.skip_if: you mainly need image generation or the widest third-party plugin ecosystem (a general assistant like ChatGPT fits better there), or you're a light user the free tier already covers
compare_with: ChatGPT leads on image generation and third-party plugins, Gemini on native Google Workspace integration — Claude's edge is reasoning depth, coding, long context and writing quality

tools.name: Clay
tools.what_it_does: Waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows for go-to-market teams. It enriches rather than sends, so you still need a separate email tool. From about $185/month (Launch, 2,500 credits) to $495 (Growth), with credit spend that is hard to forecast and a two-to-four-week learning curve.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page; the model has changed since most write-ups, ours included) Clay now meters two things separately: actions and data credits, and each plan is an expandable volume rather than a fixed tier. The entry paid plan is $167/mo billed monthly, starting at 15,000 actions a month, and the volume ladder runs $60, $150, $200, $290 and $540 a month for 15K, 40K, 60K, 100K and 200K actions monthly; billed annually the same ladder starts at $54/mo for 180K actions a year and runs to $486/mo for 2.4M. The recommended plan is $446/mo starting at 40,000 actions a month, expanding from $185/mo annually. Data credits are a separate meter again: from $125/mo for 2,500 credits a month up to $2,125/mo for 50,000, or $113/mo for 30,000 a year up to $1,913/mo for 600,000. Annual billing saves 10%. Waterfall enrichment spends credits per lookup, so the credit meter rather than the plan is what decides the bill.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest catches: a steep learning curve (expect 2–4 weeks, many teams need a dedicated Clay expert), and credits that are hard to forecast at scale. It's an enrichment engine, not a sender — you still need Instantly, Lemlist or Outreach to actually email.
tools.best_for: modern GTM and ops teams who want best-in-class waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows — and have someone to own it
tools.skip_if: you want to sign up and prospect on day one, or you can't dedicate time to learn it — the curve and credit spend frustrate casual users

tools.name: ClickUp
tools.what_it_does: The 'everything app' for project and work management. Centralize your tasks, docs, sprints, and team communication in one hub.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page with both billing tabs open) A Free Forever plan with unlimited tasks but 60MB of storage; Unlimited $7 and Business $12 per user/month billed yearly, which are $10 and $19 billed monthly; Enterprise is quote-only. AI is priced on top of the plan: Brain AI $9 and Everything AI $28 per user/month.
tools.honest_knock: The everything-app breadth is also the downside — it's feature-dense with a real learning curve, and teams can drown in options. Powerful and cheap per seat, but only if you'll actually configure and adopt it.
tools.best_for: teams that want one highly customizable app for tasks, docs, goals and reporting and will invest in setting it up
tools.skip_if: you want something simple your team adopts in a day — ClickUp's depth becomes overwhelm for a light use case

tools.name: Clonable
tools.what_it_does: Creates a continuously-translated clone of your existing website — fast multilingual versions that stay synced as your site changes, without rebuilding it.
tools.pricing: (2026) Starts with a free trial. At research time the public pricing was JavaScript-gated and not cleanly readable; the model is a continuously-synced translated clone of your existing site, typically a monthly subscription scaling by domain and traffic. Verify current rates in-app before committing.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest caveats. First, it's a continuous subscription, not a one-time translation — you pay ongoing to keep the translated clone synced with your site. Second, it's machine translation under the hood, so quality varies by language pair; always have a native speaker spot-check high-stakes pages. (Public pricing was gated at research time — confirm current tiers yourself.)
tools.best_for: businesses that want a fast, continuously-updated translated version of an existing website without rebuilding it as a multilingual site
tools.skip_if: you need human-quality translation for legal, medical or brand-critical copy, or you only need a one-off translation rather than an ongoing synced clone
compare_with: Weglot is the established website-translation layer with published pricing; Clonable positions as a full continuously-synced clone — both are subscription localization, and both need a human spot-check on quality

tools.name: Cloro
tools.what_it_does: API that reads AI search engines — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini, Grok, AI Overview and Google Search — and returns the sources and citations behind every query as structured JSON.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 on cloro.dev/pricing) Credit-metered, and the credit table matters more than the plan price. Free is $0 for 500 credits a month, one concurrent job and one seat. Paid runs Lite $30 (37,500 credits, $0.80 per 1k, 10 concurrent jobs), Hobby $100 (250,000, $0.40, 20 jobs), Starter $250 (650,000, $0.39, 50 jobs), Growth $500 (1,350,000, $0.37, 75 jobs), Business $1,000 (2,800,000, $0.36, 100 jobs), then four Enterprise steps from $2,000 to $5,000 where the rate falls to $0.31 and concurrency reaches 255. Seats are unlimited from Lite up. What a request costs varies by engine: ChatGPT full response 7 credits, ChatGPT web search 5, Copilot 5, AI Overview including the SERP 5, Grok 4, AI Mode 4, Gemini 4, Perplexity 3, Google Search and Google News 3 plus 2 per extra page — and a synchronous call adds 2 credits on top of all of those.
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is a sampler, not a trial of the real thing: 500 credits is about 100 async ChatGPT answers at the 5-credit rate we were actually charged (their table lists 7 for a full response), fewer if you call it synchronously, and one concurrent job means you queue. Anyone running a daily visibility check across a hundred keywords burns through it in about two days. Read the credit table before the price table — the same $100 buys 250,000 credits, which is 35,700 full ChatGPT calls or 83,000 Perplexity ones, so your engine mix decides your bill more than your plan does.
tools.best_for: SEO and marketing teams who need AI-search visibility as structured data — who gets cited for which query on ChatGPT, Perplexity, Copilot, Gemini and Google's AI Overview — rather than as a dashboard someone else designed
tools.skip_if: you want a finished rank-tracking dashboard rather than an API; this returns JSON with markdown, sources and citations, and you build the reporting yourself

tools.name: Close
tools.what_it_does: Sales CRM unifying calling, email and SMS in one inbox, for teams that live on the phone. Seats run about $9 (Solo) to $139 (Scale) per user/month billed annually, and call, SMS and Power Dialer credits bill separately on top — a $99 plan can land nearer $160 once a rep dials all day.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own pricing page) Per-seat: Solo $19, Essentials $49, Growth $109 and Scale $149 per user/mo, or $9, $35, $99 and $139 billed annually. No free plan; the trial runs 14 days and close.com states no credit card is required, with $5 of calling and enrichment credits included, and the page carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. AI credits are pooled per tier (500 a month on Solo, then 1,000, 1,500 and 2,000 per user up to 10,000, 15,000 and 20,000). Call minutes, SMS and dialer credits are billed separately and can meaningfully raise the real cost: outbound calls run about $0.02 a minute, phone lines start at about $1 a month, premium numbers are $19 a month per line, and the Call Assistant add-on is $50 a month per organisation plus $0.02 a minute.
tools.honest_knock: The built-in calling is the draw, but call and SMS credits stack on top of the seat price — a '$99' plan can effectively cost ~$160/user once a rep dials 50+ times a day. Great for call-heavy teams, pricey if you barely dial.
tools.best_for: inside-sales teams that live on the phone and want calling, SMS and CRM in one place
tools.skip_if: your sales are mostly email or self-serve — a cheaper CRM without built-in calling covers you

tools.name: CloudTalk
tools.what_it_does: Cloud call centre with call routing, analytics and CRM integrations, from €19/user/month on annual billing (Expert €49 needs at least three licences). AI voice agents are separate subscriptions from €99/month for 200 minutes, and number rental plus outbound minutes stack on top of the seat price.
tools.pricing: Lite €19, Starter €25, Essential €29 and Expert €49 per user/mo on annual billing, and Expert needs at least 3 licences (re-verified 2026-08-16). The add-ons are where the bill grows: Power Dialer €15 per user/mo (already included in Expert), Parallel Dialer €39 per user/mo, AI Conversation Intelligence €9 per user/mo. AI voice agents are separate subscriptions: AI Receptionist from €99/mo with 200 minutes, AI Specialist €349/mo with 1,000 minutes, and above 10,000 minutes a month custom pricing CloudTalk advertises as low as €0.15 per minute. There is a 14-day trial that includes 50 AI voice agent minutes. Note the page quotes us in euros from an EU address while the same page carries a $99 figure for the same AI bundle — check the currency at your own checkout.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat price is only part of it — number rental, outbound minutes and the AI add-ons stack on top, so a call-heavy team's real bill runs above the plan rate. Solid CRM integrations, but model your call volume first.
tools.best_for: support and sales teams that want a cloud call center with strong CRM integrations and call analytics
tools.skip_if: you make only occasional calls — a basic VoIP line or your CRM's built-in dialer costs far less

tools.name: CloudTask
tools.what_it_does: Managed marketplace for LATAM go-to-market hires — SDRs, BDRs and similar — with payroll and compliance handled. $299/month membership, plus an all-in monthly rate per hire that is not published. Direct Hire instead costs 30% of first-year salary.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) Three models, all published. The Hiring Membership is $299/month with no contract and cancel-anytime, and when you hire, each team member is billed as a single all-in monthly rate covering salary, compliance, payroll and support — that rate is not published, and it is the number that matters. Direct Hire has no access fee and costs 30% of first-year salary as a one-time payment, with a 6-month replacement guarantee against 24 months on the membership. Graduating a managed hire onto your own payroll is a flat $7,500.
tools.honest_knock: The $299 is the honest part and also the small part. What you will actually spend is the all-in monthly rate per hire, and that figure appears nowhere on the pricing page — you get it after you talk to them, once you are already invested in the process. Work out before you start what a comparable LATAM salary is on your own, so you can see what the managed layer costs on top. The $7,500 graduation fee is worth reading twice too: it is the price of ending the arrangement while keeping the person, which is exactly the situation a good hire creates.
tools.best_for: companies hiring GTM roles — SDRs, BDRs and similar — who want LATAM talent without setting up their own payroll and compliance in another country, and who value the 24-month replacement guarantee
tools.skip_if: you only need one hire ever, where Direct Hire's 30% one-time fee is cleaner than a subscription; also skip it if you cannot get the all-in monthly rate in writing before you commit
compare_with: the comparison worth doing, because they solve overlapping problems from opposite ends. Deel publishes its floors and handles employment for people you already found; CloudTask finds the people and wraps employment around them, but does not publish the all-in rate. Decide by whether your bottleneck is sourcing or paperwork, then insist on the missing number

tools.name: Cloudways
tools.what_it_does: Managed-hosting layer that rents you servers on DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS or Google Cloud through one dashboard, with the stack, caching, staging, cloning, backups and 24/7 platform support pre-built on top. You buy a server and put as many sites on it as it holds — no per-site plans and no visit metering — billed hourly and invoiced monthly in arrears with no contract. The trade is control: Cloudways' own documentation states there is no root access and no bring-your-own cloud account, so the server lives in Cloudways' name. Owned by DigitalOcean since September 2022.
tools.pricing: (read 21 Jul 2026) No free tier, but a 3-day free trial with no credit card required (Cloudways documentation). Billing is hourly and post-paid, invoiced in the first week of the following month, with no annual contract. The entry plan on DigitalOcean is Micro — 2GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 50GB storage, 2TB bandwidth — at $11/month. Further up, the DigitalOcean 8GB/4 vCPU/160GB/5TB plan lists at $88/month, against $48/month for the identical droplet bought direct from DigitalOcean on the same day. Add-ons are monthly and separate: Cloudflare Enterprise CDN from $4.99 per domain, Site Manager from $3 per app, Malware Protection from $4 per app, Rackspace email $1 per mailbox, offsite backup storage $0.033 per GB. Advanced Support is $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, on a six-month minimum; Premium Support is $500/month or 10% on the same terms (a discounted promotion was running when we checked — promotions move, so read the live price). Cloudways Autonomous is a separate autoscaling product at $99, $199 and $399/month. Markups on AWS and Google Cloud cannot be calculated because Cloudways does not publish the underlying instance types. US list prices, excluding tax.
tools.honest_knock: "Fully managed" here means the server, not your site — and that distinction is where the money is. Cloudways' own support page puts infrastructure and platform work in the included tier but treats application help as guidance only: plugin and theme troubleshooting, database work and performance tuning sit behind Advanced Support at $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, on a six-month minimum. On a small server that add-on costs more than the server it supports. Content changes, custom code debugging and code audits stay out of scope on every tier, paid ones included. The deeper catch is ownership: Cloudways documents that you get no root access and cannot use your own cloud credentials, so the machine sits in Cloudways' account — you cannot fire the management layer and keep the server, you migrate. And read the billing terms before you rely on it: their help centre states that an unpaid invoice restricts server access and can lead to the server and its backups being deleted, with backups kept for only 14 days after deletion.
