tools.best_for: agencies and PHP shops running many sites who want servers managed but not metered — one server holds as many sites as it can carry with no visit caps, billing is hourly and post-paid with no annual term, and Magento and Laravel are first-class alongside WordPress, so it suits teams who genuinely do not want anyone patching kernels at 2am
tools.skip_if: you are comfortable in a terminal, or you run a single small site — going direct to the cloud provider with your own control panel keeps the server in your own account for materially less, and one low-traffic site is better served by shared hosting or by a per-site managed host that bundles CDN and application support. Cloudways also has no email hosting of its own, reselling a Rackspace add-on instead
compare_with: Going direct on DigitalOcean with your own control panel

DigitalOcean owns Cloudways and sells both sides, which makes this the honest comparison: the same 8GB machine is $48/month as a droplet and $88/month wrapped in Cloudways. Add DigitalOcean's own daily backups and a control-panel licence and a like-for-like self-managed box lands nearer $75-80, so the real premium is smaller than the sticker gap suggests. The decisive difference is not price but ownership: with your own droplet the account and root are yours and you can drop the panel and keep the server, whereas leaving Cloudways is a migration

tools.name: Cloze
tools.what_it_does: AI shopping assistant for Shopify: a chat widget wired to your live catalogue, inventory and knowledge base that answers product questions, compares items, tracks orders and hands off to a human. Free for 25 conversations a month; paid runs $49, $99 or $199 a month on the App Store, with extra conversations at $0.10. New listing: no reviews yet as of 19 Aug 2026.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/cloze, listed as “Cloze: AI Shopping Assistant”) Free plan available: 25 AI conversations a month, up to 100 synced products, core assistant customisation and 7 days of conversation history. Paid tiers are Starter $49, Pro $99 and Scale $199 a month, each with $0.10 per additional AI conversation and a 3-day free trial. Starter covers 250 conversations a month and 1,000 synced products with full customisation and 30 days of insights; Pro covers 750 conversations and 10,000 products with advanced insights and 90 days of history; Scale covers 2,000 conversations, unlimited products, a year of history and priority support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Worth knowing before you install: the vendor's own site, cloze.bot/pricing, advertised a different and cheaper ladder on the same day — Free forever with 50 conversations a month, Pro $29 a month and Business $79 a month, and on that page both paid tiers say unlimited conversations rather than a monthly allowance. Our link goes to the App Store listing, so the $49/$99/$199 ladder, with its caps of 250, 750 and 2,000 conversations, is what you pay when you install there. The screenshot further down is their own page exactly as we captured it. Developer Optify, Lyon, France; the app launched 24 April 2026, carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge and had no reviews at all at the time of writing.
tools.honest_knock: Two things to weigh, and the first is the price itself: on the same day, the App Store listing sold this at $49, $99 and $199 a month for 250, 750 and 2,000 conversations, while the vendor's own site sold it at $29 and $79 with unlimited conversations on both paid tiers. The screenshot below is that page. Two prices and two different meters for one product is not a discount you can claim, it is an inconsistency to ask about before you pay. The second is the track record, or the absence of one — the app launched 24 April 2026 and had zero reviews when we read the listing, so there is no merchant experience to lean on and the “Built for Shopify” badge is a technical bar, not a verdict on the answers. Also note what a conversation costs when it goes wrong: an assistant wired to live inventory and order tracking is answering with your data, and the free tier's 25 conversations a month is enough to test the tone but not enough to see it handle a bad day. The 3-day trial on paid plans is short for a support tool.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with a catalogue big enough that shoppers ask which item to buy, who want a chat assistant that reads live inventory and hands off to a person, and who will watch the transcripts
tools.skip_if: your support volume is low, or you want proof from other merchants before you put an AI in front of customers — there are no reviews yet

tools.name: Clutch
tools.what_it_does: B2B services marketplace — submit a free project brief and get matched with verified, best-fit agencies for your project, no research required.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read in their own help centre) Free for buyers: Clutch's help centre describes the Project Brief as the buyer's route in and says it goes to up to 9 service providers that best match your project requirements, with no fee named anywhere in that flow. Clutch is a B2B services marketplace — the providers being listed pay for visibility, the buyer does not. A free provider profile covers the listing, client review collection, badges and widgets, contributed content, awards eligibility and a profile on sister-site The Manifest; Sponsorship, Featured Listings and Clutch Verified are the paid upgrades on top.
tools.honest_knock: It's genuinely free to submit a brief — but be clear on what it is: a lead-generation marketplace, not a neutral directory. Your brief goes straight to agencies who will reach out to pitch you, and providers pay to be visible and matched. It's a fast way to shortlist vetted agencies; just expect the outreach that comes with it.
tools.best_for: businesses that want to skip manual agency research and get matched quickly with vetted, best-fit service providers for a specific project
tools.skip_if: you already have trusted agency relationships, or you'd rather research independently without agencies contacting you
compare_with: G2 and traditional directories make you scroll and compare yourself; Clutch's brief-matching narrows it to a handful of vetted providers fast — the trade-off is that it's a matching marketplace where you'll field agency outreach

tools.name: Cognism
tools.what_it_does: B2B contact data with a GDPR focus — phone-verified mobile numbers and intent signals.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Two named plans, Standard and Pro, both stated to include 5 seats, with everything routed to 'Talk to sales' and 'Get a personalised quote'. The model is credit-based — their own wording is that 1 credit equals 1 revealed contact — with credits included in the subscription per seat, but no allowance is published. CRM Enrichment is sold standalone or as an add-on; Data-as-a-Service is priced by volume and delivery method.
tools.honest_knock: No price, no credit allowance, and a five-seat minimum on both named plans. That combination means the smallest deal is five seats of something you cannot price, so budget conversations start with a sales call rather than a number. The credit model is the part to nail down: one credit reveals one contact, so your real cost per usable lead is the credit price divided by your connect rate, and neither figure is published. Before the call, work out how many contacts a month you actually reveal — that is the only number that lets you judge the quote you get, and it is worth asking whether unused credits roll over, because nothing on the page says.
tools.best_for: outbound sales teams in Europe who need mobile numbers that are actually verified and care about GDPR provenance — that is the specific thing this is better at
tools.skip_if: you are one or two people prospecting, because both named plans include five seats; also skip it if your market is US-only, where the data advantage is smaller and cheaper options exist
compare_with: the standing comparison in B2B data — Apollo publishes its prices, which makes it the honest starting benchmark for whatever Cognism quotes you

tools.name: CometChat
tools.what_it_does: In-app text, voice and video chat infrastructure to embed into your own software — secure and scalable, with a free developer plan and, via the new Air release, fully on-prem or air-gapped deployment for regulated enterprises.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against CometChat's own machine-readable pricing reference, which they publish for AI agents and last verified themselves on 2026-05-20; USD) Build is free for development: all features, up to 100 users and 25 concurrent connections, no card. Paid Chat plans are priced by monthly active users. Billed yearly, shown as a monthly equivalent: at 1,000 MAU Basic is $239 and Advanced $359; at 10,000 MAU Basic $299, Advanced $399 and Enterprise $999; at 25,000 MAU $699 and $949; at 50,000 MAU $1,349 and $1,649. Paying monthly costs about 20% more — $298.75 and $448.75 at 1,000 MAU. Above 50,000 MAU everything is quote-only. Concurrency is included at 5% of your MAU on Basic and Advanced and 10% on Enterprise. On overage CometChat charges $0.10 per extra MAU (falling at higher tiers) or $1 per extra concurrent connection — and where both are exceeded it bills the higher of the two, not both. Enterprise has no listed overage; usage above the plan is upgraded to the appropriate plan instead. Messages and storage are unlimited on every plan, and message retention is 6 months across the board, extendable at extra cost.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing cliff is the honest headline: from a 100-MAU free tier straight to ~$239/mo is a brutal jump for an early-stage app, and users report plan structures changing under them — so model your MAU growth curve and the overage math before you architect around it. Chat infrastructure is sticky by nature; the time to compare vendors is before launch, not after.
tools.best_for: product teams that want proven in-app text/voice/video chat with SDKs for every major framework, without building messaging infrastructure themselves
tools.skip_if: your app is pre-revenue with growing users (the free-to-paid cliff will hit mid-growth), or chat is peripheral enough that a support widget covers it
compare_with: the premium chat-SDK peers — all three are MAU-priced; compare at YOUR projected MAU including overages, not at the entry tier

tools.name: Compliancely
tools.what_it_does: Compliance and verification API for US businesses and individuals: real-time and bulk IRS TIN matching, KYB business verification, USPS address and Secretary of State lookups, Form I-9 and E-Verify, consent-based IRS tax transcript retrieval, and ongoing OFAC, watchlist and FATCA monitoring. Built by Zenwork, the company behind Tax1099.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-29, re-verified 2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on their own pricing page, both billing toggles) The published price list covers one product only: TIN-match volume. Billed annually, Essential 25 is $16.95/mo for 25 monthly TIN verifications ($0.67 per match), Essential 50 $32.54/mo ($0.65), Essential 75 $45.79/mo ($0.61), Plus 100 $57.99/mo ($0.57) and Plus 250 $135.04/mo ($0.54). Switch the toggle to monthly billing and the same five tiers read $19.95, $38.49, $53.95, $67.95 and $159.95 per month, at $0.79 down to $0.63 per match — the page advertises 15% off for annual billing, and the real gap holds at roughly 15% on every tier. Enterprise is quote-only. Everything else Compliancely sells carries no public price at all: the business verification and credit-risk report packages, address verification, Form I-9, IRS tax transcripts and income verification each end in Contact Sales or Book a Demo rather than a number. Compliancely's partner team told us on 5 August 2026 that the published tiers are meant for buyers up to roughly 3,000 checks and that anything above that moves to a custom quote — that threshold is theirs, not a number the pricing page states. They confirmed on 11 August 2026 that buyers over that line are sent to their demo-request form at compliancely.com/demo-request, where the quote is written by hand; there is no published rate card for that range at all.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing page prices one product and the marketing sells about a dozen. Every tier you can actually buy online is an allowance of TIN verifications; the moment you want the things the homepage leads with — KYB business verification, credit-risk assessment, address verification, Form I-9 and E-Verify, IRS tax transcripts, OFAC and watchlist monitoring — the button changes from Get Started to Contact Sales. So the compliance stack this tool is pitched as has no advertised cost, and the number you can see is the smallest part of it. The second thing to read carefully is that the tiers are allowances rather than rates. You commit to a monthly verification count up front, and the per-match price moves against the smallest buyers: $0.79 a check on the cheapest month-to-month plan versus $0.54 on the largest annual one, a 46% spread that falls the wrong way for anyone testing the product at low volume. If your usage is lumpy — a filing-season spike and eleven quiet months — an allowance you buy every month is the wrong shape, and the prepaid option the page offers as a third toggle is worth asking about before you subscribe.
tools.best_for: finance, tax and HR teams with a steady monthly volume of US identity and business checks, who would rather buy TIN matching, KYB, I-9 and sanctions screening behind one API than integrate three separate vendors — and who are willing to run a sales conversation to price the modules beyond TIN matching
tools.skip_if: you need a handful of one-off verifications a year, because the cheapest plan still bills a monthly allowance whether you use it or not and the per-match rate is at its worst down there; or you need the full cost of a compliance stack on paper before you talk to a salesperson, since only the TIN-match tiers are published
compare_with: the honest head-to-head is Checkr, which owns one slice of what Compliancely does — employment and identity screening — and owns it with the more mature product and public self-serve pricing. If background checks are the job, Checkr wins; Compliancely is the broader bet when IRS TIN matching and KYB sit at the centre of the workflow rather than hiring. Tax1099 belongs in the conversation for an odder reason: it is family. Zenwork, Inc. is named in Compliancely's own footer and builds Tax1099 too, so the filing product and the verification product come out of one house — complements rather than rivals, and worth raising as an integration question before you price either. Verify both current price lists yourself; ours were read on 2026-07-29.

tools.name: Connecteam
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one app for managing deskless teams. Scheduling, time clock, tasks, training and team chat for hourly and frontline workforces.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) The free tier is real and not a trial: the Small Business Plan is $0 for life, covers up to 10 users and includes all hubs and features. Above that you buy per hub — Operations, Communications or HR — and each hub is priced for the first 30 users with a per-user surcharge after that. The published per-user rates run from $0.50 to $5.00 a month depending on hub and tier, with the yearly and monthly columns shown side by side; the cheapest paid entry is well under a dollar per user a month at the Basic level, which is why the headline looks so low against competitors. Price it per hub you will actually switch on, not per user.
tools.honest_knock: The free-for-10 plan is one of the most generous in the category, but the three-hub structure means costs can stack if you need all of them — price the specific hubs you'll actually use, not the full bundle.
tools.best_for: deskless and frontline teams (shift work, field crews) that need scheduling, a time clock and comms in one app, on the free-for-10 plan
tools.skip_if: your whole team sits at desks with email and Slack — this is built for the frontline, and a general PM tool fits an office better

tools.name: Consensus
tools.what_it_does: AI search across peer-reviewed literature: it reports what published studies found, not whether those studies are sound. A free tier covers basic search; Pro is about $15/month, or roughly $10 billed annually. Study quality and conflicting results still need your own judgment.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, with a caveat) Consensus blocks plain fetches of its pricing page and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount, so today's figures are not independently confirmed. Our dated reading: a free tier with essential search; Pro about $15/mo, or roughly $10/mo billed annually, with unlimited Pro searches and 15 Deep searches; a Deep tier adding around 200 Deep searches for power users; Teams and Enterprise quoted. The unit that matters is Deep searches rather than seats — that is what the tiers ration.
tools.honest_knock: It searches peer-reviewed literature, which is its strength and its boundary: it can tell you what published studies found, not whether those studies are good — study quality, sample sizes and conflicting results still need your judgment, and the AI summary layer can smooth over genuine scientific disagreement. Treat it as a dramatically faster literature scan, not an oracle; click through to the papers that matter.
tools.best_for: researchers, clinicians, students and writers who want evidence-backed answers drawn from peer-reviewed papers instead of the open web
tools.skip_if: your questions are practical/commercial rather than research-based (a general AI assistant fits), or you need full systematic-review rigor (this accelerates it, not replaces it)
compare_with: the research-AI peer set — Consensus leans consumer-friendly consensus summaries; Elicit leans structured extraction for reviews

tools.name: Contractor Foreman
tools.what_it_does: Construction management — estimating, scheduling, daily logs and financial tracking — priced per company rather than per seat, with unlimited projects on every tier. Annual runs $49/month for one user up to $332 for unlimited; quarterly billing costs about 26% more and Basic is annual-only.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced for the company rather than per seat, with unlimited projects on every tier. Annual: Basic $49/month ($588 a year, 1 user), Standard $105 ($1,264, 3 users), Plus $166 ($1,997, 8 users), Pro $221 ($2,654, 15 users), Unlimited $332 ($3,984, unlimited users). Quarterly costs more for the same plans: Standard $132/month, Plus $206, Pro $282, Unlimited $415. Basic is not offered quarterly. Their own wording: the fee listed is the fee for the company as a whole.
tools.honest_knock: Credit where it is due first: this is company pricing with unlimited projects and no per-user overage inside your tier, which is rare in construction software and genuinely cheaper than per-seat rivals for a crew. The catch is the billing term. Quarterly costs 26% more than annual on the same plan — $132 against $105 on Standard — and Basic is not sold quarterly at all, so the cheapest way in requires a year paid up front. The user counts are the real ladder: 1, 3, 8, 15, unlimited. A five-person crew is not on Standard at $105, it is on Plus at $166, so count your licence holders before you compare against anything else.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size contractors who want estimating, scheduling and daily logs in one place and can commit to a year — the company-wide fee makes it cheap per head once you have a crew
tools.skip_if: you are a sole trader with a handful of jobs, because Basic at $49 a month annual is real money against a spreadsheet and a calendar; also skip it if you need to try before committing, since annual is where the price works
compare_with: the standing comparison in construction software — compare total company cost at your crew size, since the per-seat rivals overtake this quickly

tools.name: Convert
tools.what_it_does: Privacy-first A/B testing platform — experiments, personalization and feature rollouts, priced by tested users. Via our link: an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (standard is 15 days).
tools.pricing: (2026) 15-day standard free trial — through our link it's an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (verified 16 Jul 2026, no credit card). Growth $399/mo, or $299/mo paid annually ($3,588/yr), for 100K tested users a month; Pro $599/mo, or $420/mo annually ($5,040/yr); Enterprise on request. Overuse is metered — $399 per extra 100K on Growth, $699 per 250K on Pro (it can be switched off) — and each additional custom domain costs $1,000/year.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is tested users, and it keeps running: blow past your monthly allowance and overuse blocks land at $399-699 unless you hard-cap them — and every extra custom domain is $1,000 a year. The friendly $299 headline assumes annual prepay; month-to-month is $399. One thing people misprice, and it is not the test itself: everyone expects an experiment to end when the subscription does. The trap is the winner. Convert describes itself as a client-side tool where “adding just one snippet of code on your site will then do all of the magic”, so a winning variant you leave running in the visual editor is not a change to your site — it is a rendering by their script. Ship the winner into your own code, or you are paying rent on a result you already bought.
tools.best_for: CRO teams running serious A/B and multivariate testing who want a privacy-first, GDPR-friendly alternative to the big experimentation suites
tools.skip_if: your traffic is modest — statistical significance needs volume, and 100K tested users a month is more than most small sites can use — or your landing-page tool's built-in testing covers it
compare_with: VWO is the broad experimentation suite where testing is one module; Convert focuses squarely on A/B testing with GDPR-first positioning — compare the add-on costs (API, domains) on both before deciding

tools.name: CrankWheel
tools.what_it_does: No-download screen sharing for sales calls — a prospect clicks a link and sees your screen on any device. Deliberately narrow: no video conferencing, webinars or collaboration. The free plan covers one user and 15 meetings a month; Solo is about $29/user/month.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against crankwheel.com) (2026) A free plan (1 user, 15 meetings/mo), Solo about $29/user/mo (unlimited screen sharing, ~48% off on annual), Team about $89–$99/mo with shared meeting pools; Enterprise custom. Free trial available.
tools.honest_knock: It's deliberately narrow — instant, no-download screen sharing for sales calls — so it's excellent at that one job and thin everywhere else: no full video-conferencing suite, no deep collaboration or webinar tooling. The free and Solo tiers cap meetings, which an active rep will hit. If you want an all-purpose meeting platform, this isn't it; if you want prospects to see your screen in seconds with zero friction, that focus is exactly why it works.
tools.best_for: sales reps, insurance agents and consultants who need prospects to view a screen instantly with no download or install, on any device
tools.skip_if: you need full video conferencing, webinars or team collaboration (Zoom/Meet fit better), or your call volume stays under the free tier
compare_with: general meeting platforms — CrankWheel's edge is zero-friction, no-download instant sharing for live sales, not full conferencing

tools.name: Crazy Egg
tools.what_it_does: Website optimization with heatmaps, scroll maps, session recordings and A/B testing — see how visitors behave and lift conversions with data.
tools.pricing: From $29/mo to $499, billed annually only (no real monthly option); it bills per pageview, so your bill swings with pages-per-session (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The entry plan is thin on recordings (~100/mo vs Hotjar's free ~1,050), heatmaps need manual per-page and per-device setup, and annual-only billing locks you in. Like all these tools it's diagnostic — it shows what's broken, it doesn't fix it. Worth knowing before you treat a result as banked: Crazy Egg states it can run A/B tests “after implementing just a small code snippet directly on the website”, which means a winning variant is served by that snippet rather than written into your pages. Stop paying and the original page is what visitors get. Move the winner into your own templates once a test settles.
tools.best_for: lean marketing teams that want heatmaps and built-in A/B testing in one affordable, consolidated tool
tools.skip_if: you want generous recordings, automatic heatmaps and qualitative feedback — Hotjar's free tier and product depth suit product teams better

tools.name: Credit Repair Cloud
tools.what_it_does: Software for running a credit-repair business: client management, dispute automation and letter workflows. It is not a tool for repairing your own credit. Plans run from about $49/month (Personal) to $599 (Enterprise), scaling by active clients and seats.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Five plans from Personal about $49/mo up to Enterprise about $599/mo (Start ~$179, Grow ~$299, Scale ~$399), scaling by active clients and team seats; roughly 20% off annual, 30-day trial, no contract.
tools.honest_knock: This is business-in-a-box software for starting a credit-repair company, not a tool that repairs your own credit — the price only makes sense if you're actually building a client business on it. The middle tiers jump fast as you add clients and seats, and success depends far more on your sales and compliance discipline (credit repair is a regulated space) than on the software. Buy it as an operator, not a consumer.
tools.best_for: entrepreneurs building or running a credit-repair business who need client management, dispute automation and done-for-you letter workflows
tools.skip_if: you just want to fix your own personal credit (you don't need this), or you're not prepared for the sales and compliance work a client business demands
compare_with: Dispute Fox or Client Dispute Manager
comparable credit-repair business platforms — compare on client limits and automation depth at your stage

tools.name: CrowdStrike
tools.what_it_does: Endpoint protection built around a cloud-delivered agent: antivirus, EDR and threat hunting.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced per device. Falcon Go $7.99 per device per month, or $59.99 per device billed annually — capped at a maximum of 100 devices. Falcon Pro $14.99 monthly or $99.99 annually per device. Falcon Enterprise $19.99 per device per month. Larger tiers and managed services are quote-only. A free trial is offered on every tier.
tools.honest_knock: Two numbers decide whether this is for you, and neither is the headline. The first is the 100-device ceiling on Falcon Go: it is not a soft limit you grow through, it is the point where you change product. The second is the annual rate, which is worth doing the division on — $59.99 a year against $7.99 a month is $95.88, so annual saves 37%, one of the larger annual discounts in security software. Beyond that, be honest with yourself about which tier you are comparing: Go is antivirus with a good agent, and the endpoint detection and response that CrowdStrike is famous for starts at Pro. Comparing Go against a full EDR product from a competitor is comparing the wrong things.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size companies that want a serious endpoint agent without running a security team — Falcon Go is genuinely priced for businesses under 100 devices
tools.skip_if: you are under ten devices and already run a maintained operating system with its built-in protection, because at that size the management overhead outweighs the gain; also skip Go if you actually need EDR, since that starts a tier up
compare_with: SentinelOne or Microsoft Defender for Business
the direct endpoint peers — Defender is often already in your Microsoft licence, so price that first before comparing per-device rates

tools.name: Customer.io
tools.what_it_does: Behavioural messaging: email, push and in-app campaigns driven by product events rather than lists.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Essentials starts at $100 a month billed monthly, scaled by profiles. Premium starts at $1,000 a month billed yearly. Enterprise is quote-only. Overages are published, which is unusual and useful: additional people and object profiles $0.009 each on Essentials, additional 1,000 emails $0.12, additional AI credits $10 per 100,000. Essentials includes 2 workspaces; Premium and Enterprise unlimited. Early-stage companies that have raised under $10M can get twelve months free through their startup programme.
tools.honest_knock: The gap between the two published tiers is the thing to plan around: $100 to $1,000 a month is ten times, and there is nothing in between. What pushes you across is not a feature you choose but your profile count growing, so the honest question at signup is what your list looks like in a year rather than today. Credit where due — the overage rates are printed, at $0.009 a profile and $0.12 per thousand emails, which most tools in this category will not tell you until the invoice. Use those numbers: growing into overage on Essentials is often cheaper than the jump to Premium, and you can work out exactly where the crossover is.
tools.best_for: product-led companies whose messaging is triggered by what people do in the product rather than by a list — that is what this is built for and it is genuinely better at it than list-first tools
tools.skip_if: you send newsletters and campaigns to a list — that is a different job and much cheaper elsewhere; also skip it if your profile count is unpredictable, since profiles are the meter
compare_with: the direct behavioural-messaging peers — Klaviyo for ecommerce, Braze at enterprise scale; compare on cost per profile at your projected list size

tools.name: Databox
tools.what_it_does: Centralized KPI dashboards. Pull data from all your software tools into one clean interface to monitor your business health. A free Skills Marketplace adds guided analyses on top: the paid-ads skill standardizes every ad channel into one efficiency table with CPA gauges against your own targets, judged per funnel role. A native MCP server (mcp.databox.com) puts those metrics inside ChatGPT or Claude — ingest data and query it in plain language. It runs on every paid plan, not on Free, and its queries spend from the same monthly AI-credit pool as Genie.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page) There is a free plan: Free at $0 with 3 data sources, 1 user, 1 dashboard or report and 50 AI credits a month. Paid tiers, billed annually: Analyst $64/mo (5 data sources, 1 user, 500 AI credits), Pro $159/mo (3 sources included, $5.60/mo per extra, unlimited users, 1,500 credits), Growth $399/mo (4,000 credits, 15-minute sync) and a custom tier. AI credits are one shared monthly pool for the Genie assistant and the MCP server, so heavy AI use is what moves you up a tier rather than seats.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing model bites: Pro connects only 3 data sources, so the per-source fees stack up fast — and for agencies juggling many clients with diverse tools it gets expensive. Power users may also find the custom-metric and data-modelling depth limited next to a full BI tool.
tools.best_for: SMBs and agencies that want clean KPI dashboards from 130+ one-click integrations without building them by hand
tools.skip_if: you only need one or two data sources (the per-source fees add up), or you want deep custom data modelling — a free tool like Looker Studio fits better

tools.name: Deel
tools.what_it_does: Global hiring, payroll and EOR platform — pay contractors and employees compliantly in 150+ countries, from $49 per contractor per month, with HR tools and US PEO options.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Per-worker pricing, demo-led, and each product is priced separately: HR and hiring tools from $14 per worker a month; contractor management from $49 per contractor a month, or $325 per month per Contractor of Record if you want Deel to carry the compliance risk; US PEO from $125 per employee a month; and EOR, where Deel employs your international hire, from $599 per employee a month. There is a free demo and final quotes come through sales. The spread is the point: the same headcount costs $14 or $599 a month depending on which relationship you need, so identify the employment model before comparing vendors.
tools.honest_knock: Every price is a ‘starting at’ and every button says ‘book a demo’ — the real bill depends on countries, benefits and add-ons, and only firms up in a sales conversation. And know what EOR money buys: at $599+/month per employee you’re paying for compliance risk transfer, not software — worth it in unfamiliar jurisdictions, expensive where you could open your own entity.
tools.best_for: companies hiring internationally without local entities — contractors paid compliantly in 150+ countries, or full EOR employment where you need someone on the ground fast
tools.skip_if: your team is all-domestic (a local payroll tool is far cheaper), or you hire enough people in one country that opening your own entity beats paying per-employee EOR fees forever
compare_with: Gusto is the friendly US-payroll incumbent for domestic teams; Deel is built for global — contractors, EOR and payroll across 150+ countries. Pick by where your people are

tools.name: Deputy
tools.what_it_does: Workforce management for hourly and shift-based teams: rota building, time clocking, timesheet approval and labour-law compliance, with payroll and HR integrations.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-31, read in a live browser session on deputy.com/pricing with both billing toggles) Three plans, per user per month and excluding tax. On annual billing Lite is $5, Core $6.50 and Pro $9; switch the toggle to monthly and the same three read $5.50, $7.25 and $10. Add-ons are billed monthly on top: HR $2 per user, Messaging+ $1.95 per user and Analytics+ $1.50 per user (the last two are included in Pro), plus Deputy Payroll enabled by Paycor at $8 per user plus a $49 monthly base fee, which is only available on annual Core and Pro plans in the US. The page also states a minimum monthly spend of USD $30 / AUD $30 / GBP £20 per invoice on the monthly Lite, Core and Pro plans. Lite and Core start with a free trial; Pro is Contact us rather than self-serve.
tools.honest_knock: The minimum monthly spend is the number to check before anything else: at $5.50 per user on monthly billing, a team of fewer than about six people still pays the $30 floor, so the headline per-user price is misleading at small scale. Beyond that, the plan you probably want is not the one you first price — auto-scheduling, demand forecasting and labour budgets sit in Core, and SSO, custom access levels and location hierarchies only in Pro, which has no public self-serve checkout. The add-ons stack per user as well, and the payroll add-on is US-only and annual-only.
tools.best_for: shift-based businesses — hospitality, retail, healthcare, any hourly workforce — that need rostering, clocking and labour-law compliance in one system and have enough staff to clear the minimum spend
tools.skip_if: you run a small salaried desk team: the $30 monthly minimum means you pay for roughly six users whether you have them or not, and salaried staff rarely need shift-level clocking at all

tools.name: Descript
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered video and podcast editor: edit media by editing the text transcript — cut, overdub and remove filler words like editing a doc — with screen recording, AI voice cloning and an AI assistant (Underlord) built in.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free plan with 60 minutes a month and watermarked 720p exports. Paid, per person per month, annual against monthly: Hobbyist $16 / $24, Creator $24 / $35, Business $50 / $65, with annual billing saving up to 35%. Media hours and AI credits are capped per tier (roughly 10, 30 and 40 hours a month, and 400 to 1,500 credits), so the meter that matters is footage rather than seats — a weekly podcast can outgrow Hobbyist on hours long before it needs the features above it.
tools.honest_knock: It's per-editor pricing with two meters running underneath: media hours AND monthly AI credits. Heavy podcast or video volume burns through the caps fast, and the free tier watermarks 720p exports — model your real production hours before picking a tier. The API changes the arithmetic rather than escaping it: their own API page states access is included for paying users at no additional cost, but the work it does draws from the same AI credits and media minutes, so automating a pipeline burns the caps faster, not slower. It also stops just short of the finish — the same page says direct media file exports are not supported yet, so the export step stays a manual one in the app. (read on their own API page, 2026-08-14)
tools.best_for: podcasters and video creators who want to edit by editing the transcript — cutting, overdubbing and stripping filler words as easily as editing a doc, and teams who want those same edits triggered from code or from an AI assistant via Descript’s API and MCP connector rather than from the app
tools.skip_if: you need frame-precise, effects-heavy editing (a traditional NLE fits better) or your monthly volume blows past the media-hour caps
compare_with: Riverside wins on recording-quality-first workflows, CapCut on quick social edits; Descript wins on the text-based editing workflow itself

tools.name: Devs.ai
tools.what_it_does: Build and ship AI agents and apps across many models without engineering work. The seat price is the smaller half of the bill: Personal includes $10 of model usage a month and Business $21, metered on top — and the plan cards state the included amount without stating the rate once it runs out.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on devs.ai/home/pricing with both billing toggles) Devs.ai does publish its pricing — on the marketing site at devs.ai/home/pricing, not at the app's /pricing route, which bounces you to a login screen. Free is $0 forever, but Agent Builder and App Builder appear there in "Core" rather than "Full" form, data upload is capped at 2 GB, and workflows, APIs and integrations are marked absent. Personal is $15 per seat / month billed annually or $18 billed monthly; Business is $30 per seat / month annually or $36 monthly; Enterprise is a custom annual contract. The seat fee is not the whole bill: Personal includes $10 of usage per month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. Data upload runs 2 GB, 10 GB, 20 GB and custom across the four tiers. Team governance and collaboration start at Business, while SSO (OpenID/SAML), access control lists, custom connectors and white-labelling are Enterprise-only. Separately, Devs.ai told us by email on 5 August 2026 that organisations upgrading to a paid Personal or Business plan can earn up to $100 in usage credits for completing setup steps — starting a conversation, creating an agent, connecting an integration, deploying an app — that the credits are shared org-wide and do not expire, and that Enterprise is excluded while orgs already on a paid plan before July 2026 are not enrolled by default. That last paragraph is the vendor's own statement to us, not something we found published on the pricing page.
tools.honest_knock: The seat price is the smaller half of the bill. Personal includes $10 of usage a month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat — and the plan cards state the included amount without stating the rate you pay once it runs out, which is exactly the number you need to forecast a real workload. The free plan is a demo rather than a working tier: both builders are limited to "Core", and workflows, APIs and integrations are absent entirely, which is much of what would make the platform useful past a first agent. And for a product sold on IT governance, the governance controls are the ones you cannot buy with a card — SSO, access control lists and white-labelling sit on the Enterprise tier, behind a custom annual contract.
tools.best_for: teams that want to prototype and ship AI agents and apps across multiple models without engineering overhead, and that can absorb model usage metered on top of the per-seat fee
tools.skip_if: you need SSO, access control lists or white-labelling without going through an Enterprise contract, or you need one predictable all-in bill rather than a seat fee plus metered usage
compare_with: the agent-builder field — all three meter model usage differently on top of their base price, so compare on the metered layer rather than on the seat fee

tools.name: Dext
tools.what_it_does: Receipt and invoice capture that extracts the data and feeds it into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage. It is the capture layer, not accounting software, so you still need one of those. From about £24/month on Starter, and extraction accuracy varies enough to need manual correction.
tools.pricing: From ~£24/mo (Starter) to £42 (Growing) and £84 (Business) — roughly $31–239 depending on plan and region (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's a data-capture layer, not accounting software — it feeds Xero, QuickBooks or Sage, so you still need one of those. Extraction accuracy varies and sometimes needs manual fixes, the UI is tricky for beginners, the mobile app is more limited than desktop, and sole traders find it pricey.
tools.best_for: accountants, bookkeepers and growing businesses drowning in receipts who want fast, accurate capture flowing straight into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage
tools.skip_if: you're a sole trader with few receipts (pricey for low volume), or you want all-in-one accounting — Dext only does the capture layer
compare_with: the free-with-Xero and the do-it-yourself routes

tools.name: Dify
tools.what_it_does: Open-source platform for LLM apps and agent workflows: visual builder, RAG pipelines, model-agnostic. Free to self-host, but you own the servers, updates and reliability, and LLM tokens bill separately on every plan. Managed cloud runs about $59/month on Professional.
tools.pricing: Genuinely open-source and free to self-host (you pay only infrastructure plus your own LLM API bills); the managed cloud adds a free Sandbox, Professional about $59/mo and Team around $159/mo (2026). LLM inference always bills separately from your provider.
tools.honest_knock: 'Free' self-hosting isn't free — you own the servers, updates and reliability, and LLM tokens cost extra on every plan. It's powerful, but you need some technical comfort to run and maintain it well.
tools.best_for: technical teams that want to build and ship LLM apps and agents on an open-source platform they can self-host and control
tools.skip_if: you want a no-maintenance, non-technical builder — a fully managed no-code AI tool saves you the infra and upkeep
compare_with: Flowise or a managed platform like Lindy.ai
other LLM-app builders, self-host or managed

tools.name: Diginius
tools.what_it_does: Digital marketing and e-commerce performance platform. Manage PPC, analytics and product feeds to improve online sales and visibility.
tools.pricing: (2026) Essential about $20/mo (single user); Pro ~$99/mo (5 users); Core ~$249/mo (10 users, most features); Business/custom above. ~20% off annual; 14-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: All-in-one marketing dashboards live or die on data depth per module: Diginius bundles PPC, SEO, lead intelligence and reporting affordably, but specialists (a dedicated SEO suite, a dedicated PPC optimizer) go deeper in their lanes — so buy it as consolidation for a lean team, not as a replacement for expert-grade tooling in your primary channel. Verify the integrations you depend on (especially Microsoft Ads, its historical strength) in the trial.
tools.best_for: lean teams and agencies that want PPC, SEO and lead intelligence consolidated in one affordable dashboard instead of five subscriptions
tools.skip_if: your growth lives in one channel where a specialist tool's depth pays for itself, or you need enterprise analytics rigor
compare_with: the specialist suites — deeper per channel at higher cost; Diginius wins on breadth-per-dollar for generalists

tools.name: Digit
tools.what_it_does: Inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system for manufacturers and distributors. Starter $400/month with 5 users, Growth $750, Professional $1,300, extra users $63 each. Watch the add-ons: integrations beyond two, API and MCP access are $100/month apiece.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) Four tiers with three published: Starter $400/month including 5 users, Growth $750 including 10, Professional $1,300 including 15, and Enterprise on quote. Extra users are $63/month each on every tier. Paying quarterly takes 10% off and annually 20%. Two integrations are included; each one after that is $100/month, and API access, MCP access and webhooks are $100/month each on top.
tools.honest_knock: The tier price is a floor, not a ceiling, and the add-ons are where an inventory system quietly doubles. Two integrations are included — but a working setup usually means an accounting package and a webshop, which is your two, and then Amazon or a second sales channel is another $100/month. Want the API, or your data inside an AI assistant? $100/month each. A Starter customer on QuickBooks, Shopify and Amazon with API access is at $600/month before adding a sixth user. Price the whole configuration you actually need, not the tier.
tools.best_for: manufacturers and distributors outgrowing spreadsheets who need inventory, production, purchasing and sales in one system, and who genuinely need lot tracking and traceability rather than just wanting them
tools.skip_if: you are a small operation where $400/month for five users is heavy against what a warehouse module in your existing accounting package would cost; also skip it if your integration list is long, because the $100-per-connection model punishes exactly that
compare_with: the natural head-to-head for manufacturers leaving spreadsheets. Both cover inventory and production; the difference shows up in how they charge for the edges. Price the full configuration you need on each — every integration, the API if you want it — because Digit's $100-per-connection add-ons are where the tier price stops being the price

tools.name: Disputifier: Smart Chargebacks
tools.what_it_does: Chargeback automation for Shopify: submits dispute evidence for you, buys chargeback alerts that refund incoming disputes before they land, and screens orders for fraud and late shipments. Free to install; recovery costs 20% of every won chargeback (capped at $250 a win), alerts run $17-$27.50 each and the two prevention add-ons $0.05 an order.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/disputifier and on disputifier.com/pricing) Free to install, with everything billed on use. The listing shows a single plan — Basic, free to install, with a 7-day risk-free trial — and names two charges: chargeback fighting at 20% of won-back revenue, and chargeback alerts from $17 to $27.50 per alert. All charges are billed in USD. The vendor's own pricing page fills in the rest: recovery is 20% of the recovered amount with the fee capped at $250 per win (win a $50 chargeback and they debit $10), fraud prevention is $0.05 per order, and 'order not received' prevention another $0.05 per order. Alerts are sold there as custom volume-based pricing by quote, so the $17-$27.50 band on the listing is the only public number for them. There is no monthly subscription anywhere in this: the bill is a function of how many disputes and orders you have, so it cannot be read off the pricing page in advance. Developer Disputifier, 294 Trillium Way, Clayton, North Carolina; the app launched 23 September 2020 and carries a 4.5 average over 84 App Store reviews.
tools.honest_knock:
Free to install is doing a lot of work here. All four services bill per event — a fifth of each recovery, $17 to $27.50 an alert, five cents an order twice over — so the cost lands after the fact and scales with exactly the thing you are trying to reduce. Model your worst chargeback month before you switch alerts on, not your average one.

The reviews deserve a straight look too. The 4.5 average across 84 reviews is not a middle: 88% are five stars and 11% are one star, with almost nothing in between. The most recent one-star, from June 2026, describes a security incident at the vendor and a dispute over unpaid invoices and billing descriptors; Disputifier replied in July that it does not block merchants from moving providers and disputes the account of the charges. We have not verified either side and are not taking one. What the pattern does show is where the friction sits: merchants either rate this perfect or fall out with it over invoices, not over whether disputes were won.

And know what alerts cannot reach. Coverage depends on the shopper's bank and card: smaller issuers do not participate, Amex and Discover frequently cannot be set up, Klarna alerts do not exist yet and PayPal alerts are recent. The prevention rate the vendor quotes is a ceiling for a well-covered card mix, not a promise for yours.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with a chargeback problem big enough to cost real money and nobody in-house to fight disputes, who would rather pay a share of what is recovered than a monthly fee
tools.skip_if: your dispute volume is low or lumpy, you need a predictable monthly bill, or your margins are high enough that auto-refunding an alerted order costs more than losing the occasional dispute

tools.name: doola
tools.what_it_does: Business formation and compliance made easy. Launch your US LLC or C-Corp from anywhere globally, complete with banking and tax management.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Starter $297/yr for LLC or C-Corp formation, EIN, registered agent and a US address, with a 30-day trial and renewal at $300/yr; state filing fees are extra ($50-500 depending on the state). Bookkeeping runs $329/yr. Tax and Compliance is listed at $1,999/yr and Business-in-a-Box at $2,999/yr, both currently discounted by 20% to $1,599 and $2,399 — a saving of $400 and $600 that the page presents as a limited premium offer. Annual billing is advertised as saving 25% against the alternative.
tools.honest_knock: Formation is the cheap part; the recurring bookkeeping and tax tiers are where the real cost sits, and state fees are extra on top of doola's price. Convenient especially for non-US founders, but a local accountant may be cheaper once you're established.
tools.best_for: founders (often non-US) who want US LLC/C-Corp formation, EIN and compliance handled in one place without the paperwork
tools.skip_if: you're a US resident comfortable filing formation yourself — the state fee plus a cheap registered agent costs far less than the bundle
compare_with: other formation services, or doing it yourself

tools.name: Drip
tools.what_it_does: Ecommerce email and onsite marketing built around your store's order data — segments, abandoned-cart and welcome playbooks, pop-ups and A/B testing, with one-click links to Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce. Priced purely on list size from $39/month for 2,500 people, 14-day trial without a card. Two things the headline price hides: chat support only starts at $99/month, and the promised unlimited sends turn into a hard cap of twelve emails per contact per month somewhere above 25,000 contacts (read 12 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026-08-12, read off their own pricing calculator) One ladder, no tiers: you drag a slider to your list size and Drip prints a monthly price. 2,500 people is $39, then $49 at 3,000, $59 at 3,500, $69 at 4,000, $79 at 4,500, $89 at 5,000, $99 at 6,000, $109 at 7,000, $169 at 12,500, $369 at 25,000, $699 at 50,000, $1,299 at 110,000 and $1,949 at 175,000. Above roughly 175,000 the number disappears and the page says “Let’s chat”, so the top of the range is quote-only. The trial is 14 days and takes no card, but Drip states unlimited sends are switched off during it. Two things the ladder does not advertise. Chat support is not included at the entry price: up to 5,000 people the line reads “Email support”, and “Chat and email support” only appears from $99 (6,000 people) — their FAQ says the same in words. And “Unlimited email sends” stops being literally true as you climb: it still says unlimited at 25,000 people, but at 50,000 the same line reads “600,000 email sends”, at 110,000 “1,320,000” and at 175,000 “2,100,000” — in every case exactly twelve sends per contact per month. Every plan carries the same feature set otherwise, including up to 50 workflows and unlimited sub-accounts, so what you buy going up the ladder is list capacity, not capability.
tools.honest_knock: The word “unlimited” quietly expires. At the prices most small shops pay the send allowance really is uncapped, but from somewhere between 25,000 and 50,000 contacts the same bullet turns into a hard number — 600,000 sends at 50,000 people, twelve per contact per month — and Drip never flags the switch. If you run a daily-deal or high-frequency list, do the arithmetic before you migrate: twelve sends per contact is generous for a monthly newsletter and tight for anything that mails several times a week. The second thing to price in is support. The page sells one product at every level, but you cannot talk to anyone in chat until $99/month; below that it is email only, which is a real difference on the day a broken automation is sending to the wrong segment.
tools.best_for: an online store on Shopify, WooCommerce or BigCommerce that already has order data worth segmenting and wants ecommerce playbooks — abandoned cart, welcome series, post-purchase — without assembling them by hand. The pricing model suits a list that grows steadily and mails at a normal cadence, because you pay for people rather than per seat or per feature, and every plan carries the whole feature set
tools.skip_if: you are not selling online: Drip says an ecommerce store is not required but that the platform is built for one, and you would be paying for the half you cannot use. Skip it too if your list is large and you mail often, because the send allowance caps at twelve per contact per month once you are past the small tiers, and if your list is heading beyond 175,000 people, where the published ladder ends and pricing becomes a conversation
compare_with: the comparison Drip picks itself — it publishes a Drip vs. Klaviyo page — and the one most ecommerce teams actually make. Both price on list size and both live off store data; the practical question is what the send allowance and the support line look like at your volume, which is where Drip's ladder is unusually easy to read and unusually quiet about the twelve-sends ceiling

tools.name: Dripify
tools.what_it_does: Cloud-based LinkedIn outreach automation — drip sequences of connection requests, messages, InMails and profile views, with configurable daily limits and a built-in email finder. From $39 per user/month billed annually, 7-day free trial without a card.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-24, read on their own pricing page) Four tiers, priced per user: Basic $39, Pro $59 and Advanced $79 per user per month billed annually, plus an Enterprise tier that is quote-only. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. Those are the annual-billing rates. Month to month the same tiers read $59, $79 and $99 per user (both columns read in a live browser session on 2026-07-24), so the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded — you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range: about 34 percent on Basic, 25 on Pro, 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here: Basic gets you one drip campaign and what the page calls 'limited daily quotas'; unlimited campaigns and full quotas start at Pro; Advanced adds multi-team management and the safety feature Dripify itself recommends. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month.
tools.honest_knock: Understand what you are buying before the price matters: LinkedIn prohibits this entire product category. Its User Agreement bans using 'bots or other unauthorized automated methods' to 'send or redirect messages', and its prohibited-software page says members using such tools 'risk having their accounts restricted or shut down'. There is no carve-out for cloud tools or low volumes, and Dripify is not an outlier here — every competitor sits on the same side of that line. Dripify's own documentation is candid about the consequence, warning that LinkedIn 'may issue warnings, temporary restrictions, or even permanent bans', and it publishes a recovery procedure for exactly that scenario. Two things follow. First, the advertised ceiling is not a working speed: the app allows up to 75 connection requests a day, while Dripify's own setup guide tells beginners to run 10 to 15, and brand-new accounts 2 to 5, building up 10 to 20 percent a week. Anyone buying on the headline number is buying capacity they are told not to use. Second, Activity Control — the feature Dripify names as its best protection, which adjusts your pace automatically — sits on the $79 Advanced tier. On Basic and Pro, safe pacing is your own manual responsibility. And when a vendor writes that a feature 'makes sure your LinkedIn account won't get flagged', read that as a claim about a third party's enforcement decisions that no vendor can actually guarantee.
tools.best_for: sales teams that already run LinkedIn outreach, understand that automation breaches LinkedIn's terms, and accept that risk with their eyes open — the cloud architecture means sequences run with your browser closed and no extension injected into your session
tools.skip_if: anyone whose LinkedIn account is not expendable, since a restriction can be permanent and no tool can promise otherwise; or anyone tempted by the 75-a-day ceiling, because the vendor's own advice is roughly a fifth of that
compare_with: the closest head-to-head — both are cloud-based with a regional dedicated IP, so the 'cloud versus extension' framing you will read in affiliate roundups does not actually separate them. The real difference is the pricing model: Expandi sells one Business plan with everything included at $99 per user a month, 20 percent off annually, while Dripify tiers both quotas and safety features. Watch the $39-versus-$99 gap that roundups quote — that is Dripify's annual rate against Expandi's monthly one. Month against month it is $59 to $99 versus $99, and at the top of Dripify's range the two cost the same. Both price lists read on 2026-07-24; verify them yourself before you buy.

tools.name: Dripshipper
tools.what_it_does: Private-label coffee and tea dropshipping for Shopify: they roast, bag and ship from their own US facilities within 3-5 business days, with your brand on the packaging. Starter $30 a month or $240 a year, Professional $99, Elite $197, all with a 14-day trial and per-order product and shipping cost on top.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/dripshipper, listed as “Dripshipper: Coffee & Tea”) Starter $30 a month, Professional $99 and Elite $197, each with a 14-day free trial. Starter is also sold annually at $240 a year, which is $20 a month for the same tier. Product and shipping cost is charged per order on top. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.7 from 142 App Store reviews. Developer The Doughty Organization.
tools.honest_knock: Read the ladder before you climb it. Starter already carries unlimited orders, unlimited products and automatic fulfilment — the whole product, in other words. Professional at $99 adds live monthly training, priority support and a success manager; Elite at $197 adds monthly one-on-one coaching on top. You are buying people, not capability: nothing above Starter makes the coffee ship faster or cost less per bag. The annual rate is the move worth noticing in the other direction, since $240 a year against $30 a month is a third off the same tier. Beyond that the model is narrow by design — one product category, roasted and shipped from their own US facilities in 3-5 business days, with no route to source elsewhere or negotiate the per-order cost.
tools.best_for: someone who wants a turnkey private-label coffee or tea brand on Shopify — their roasting and packaging, your label on the bag — and is content to stay inside one product category
tools.skip_if: you want product breadth, fulfilment outside the US, or control over sourcing and packaging cost — this is a single-supplier pipeline and the higher tiers only add coaching

tools.name: DropGenius
tools.what_it_does: Generates a Shopify dropshipping store — products, branding and copy — as a starting template, not a finished business. Monthly runs $39 to $299, and annual billing drops Starter. Trustpilot sat near 1.6/5 at research time, with recurring complaints about charges after cancellation.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 5 Aug 2026) Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 14-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). Their own FAQ still quotes an older $39.99-$299.99 range plus a $1.99 one-time store-creation fee, so the marketing copy and the checkout do not agree. The store it builds runs on Shopify, which bills you separately — DropGenius does not state that cost anywhere on its pages.
tools.honest_knock: We have to be blunt here: DropGenius carries a very poor Trustpilot rating (around 1.6/5 at research time), with recurring complaints about charges continuing after cancellation and refund difficulty. An AI-generated store in 30 seconds is also just a starting template — the product selection, marketing and margins remain entirely your problem. If you proceed: pay attention to cancellation mechanics from day one, screenshot everything, and treat the Renewal Radar as mandatory equipment.
tools.best_for: absolute beginners who want a pre-built Shopify dropshipping store scaffold in minutes and understand it's a starting point, not a business
tools.skip_if: anyone uncomfortable with the documented billing complaints — or expecting an AI-generated store to sell by itself
compare_with: building on Spocket directly (same ecosystem) gives you the supplier network without the store-generator layer — and cleaner reviews

tools.name: Dryground AI
tools.what_it_does: Full-stack AI implementation services: helps businesses design and integrate AI across their tech stack — for teams that want AI built and shipped, not just advised.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-17, read in a browser because the site renders client-side and a plain fetch returns only the title) No public pricing anywhere, and we checked before saying so: /pricing, /plans, /services, /about and /contact all return 404, the words “pricing”, “price” and “$” appear zero times on the homepage, and the navigation carries no pricing entry at all — it runs Solutions, Products, Verticals, Case Studies, Research, Book a Consultation. Tiers do exist with no numbers attached: the AI Velocity line is described as “six tiers from pilot to full enterprise transformation” on 90-day outcome cycles. Budget this as a consulting engagement scoped per project, not a subscription you can read off a page.
tools.honest_knock: This is consulting, not a tool you log into: best when you want AI designed and built for you, not when you'd rather DIY with software. Read the headline numbers carefully too — the 20-50% efficiency and 10-20% revenue figures on their homepage carry the caption “2025 industry benchmarks”, so they describe the market rather than this firm's own results, and the case studies underneath them name no clients.
tools.best_for: businesses that want AI solutions built for them as a services engagement rather than assembling tools themselves
tools.skip_if: you're looking for self-serve software with published pricing — this is custom, quote-based consulting

tools.name: EasyDMARC
tools.what_it_does: DMARC, SPF and DKIM monitoring — stop others sending email as your domain.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Plus €44.99/month (€35.99/month billed annually), 2 domains, 100,000–1,000,000 messages/month, 3 months of report history, 1 invited user. Premium €89.99/month (€71.99 annually), 4 domains, up to 5,000,000 messages/month, 1 year of history, unlimited users, a customer-success manager on yearly billing only. Enterprise quote-only with unlimited domains and 3 years of history. A free plan exists and the comparison table now itemises it: 1 domain, 1,000 messages a month, 14 days of report history and 1 invited user.
tools.honest_knock: You are buying domains and history, not features. Plus covers two domains; a company with a main domain, a marketing subdomain and a legacy domain it forgot about is already over. And the history window is the part that bites later: three months on Plus means that when you are investigating a spoofing campaign that started in the spring, the reports are gone. The page also does not say what happens when you pass the message volume — their own FAQ does, and the answer is that you lose access to your reports and dashboard rather than being billed for overage, which is a harsher failure mode than an overage charge and worth knowing before you size the plan.
tools.best_for: anyone who sends email from their own domain and has not yet got DMARC to enforcement — the reporting is the part that makes that safe rather than guesswork
tools.skip_if: you have one domain, send little email, and are willing to read raw XML reports yourself, because the free tier plus patience covers the same ground
compare_with: the direct DMARC-platform peers — compare on domains included and history retention, not on the feature list

tools.name: eDesk
tools.what_it_does: E-commerce helpdesk: one unified inbox for Amazon, eBay, Shopify and email, with order data and an AI Agent that bills per resolved outcome. Free plan; paid from $39/agent/mo (annual).
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free plan to start; Essential $39 per agent/mo, Growth $89 (recommended), Professional $119, Enterprise custom — all billed annually, with monthly billing 20% higher ($49 against $39 on Essential). The AI Agent is included on every paid tier, but its automated resolutions bill separately at $0.99 per outcome: you pay when it actually resolves a query, not per attempt. eDesk claims the agent can automate up to 65% of support across channels, so model the outcome fee against your ticket volume — at 1,000 resolved tickets a month that is $990 on top of the seats.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters, and the second one is easy to miss: the per-agent price is the entry ticket, but the AI Agent charges $0.99 for every automated resolution on top — great when it deflects real tickets, but a variable line item that scales with your support volume, so model it against your ticket count before assuming a flat bill. And the honest fundamental for any e-commerce helpdesk: the value is only as good as your marketplace integrations actually syncing — test Amazon/eBay/Shopify connections with your real accounts during the free trial.
tools.best_for: e-commerce and marketplace sellers who want one unified inbox across Amazon, eBay, Shopify and email — with order data and AI-assisted replies where support and revenue overlap
tools.skip_if: you run a non-commerce SaaS or service business (general helpdesks fit better and cheaper), or your ticket volume is low enough that a shared inbox already copes
compare_with: Gorgias is the other big e-commerce helpdesk, deepest on Shopify; eDesk leans harder into marketplaces (Amazon, eBay) and per-outcome AI pricing — pick by where your orders actually live and how you want the AI billed

tools.name: ElevateForward
tools.what_it_does: An operational execution and alignment platform (Elevate Studio) for scaling companies, structured in three layers — Strategy (set priorities and initiatives), Execution (track initiatives, workstreams, ownership and KPIs), and Momentum (adoption, change management and follow-through). It turns strategy into structured, visible execution rather than task lists.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-12, read on their own pricing page) The prices are published, despite the consultative first impression: an Elevate Insight Report is $500 per report and a bundle of three is $1,350, a 10% discount on buying them separately. A report is scoped to one focus area you choose, delivered within five business days of submission, with up to two rounds of feedback-based adjustments and a review consultation included. Above the reports sit the Elevate Studio subscriptions — Elevate Strategy, Elevate Execution and Business Enablement, the last marked coming soon. Those cards carry a price toggle whose two states we could not tell apart in the markup ($250/$500/$750 a month in one state, $8/$16/$149 in the other), so we do not repeat a monthly figure we cannot pin down.
tools.honest_knock: It's a strategy-to-execution layer, not a task app or a dashboard — so the value only lands if leadership actually adopts the framework. 'Operational alignment platform' is also a fuzzy, crowded label, so press them on the concrete deliverables (the diagnostics, KPI blueprints and execution plans) before committing.
tools.best_for: scaling companies where growth is outpacing alignment — leadership lacks execution visibility and strategic initiatives keep stalling halfway
tools.skip_if: you already have solid execution discipline, or you just want a simple task or project tool — this is a strategy-and-alignment layer, not a to-do list
compare_with: an EOS/Traction-style operating system plus your existing PM and BI tools
the pieces EF tries to combine into one

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what_it_does: Market-leading AI voice platform: hyper-realistic text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing, sound effects and conversational agents — with a developer API and a free tier to test voices before you pay.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 16 Jul 2026) Free $0 with 10k credits/mo; Starter $6/mo (30k credits, commercial license); Creator $22/mo — first month 50% off at $11 — with ~121k credits; Pro $99/mo (~600k credits, 44.1kHz PCM); Scale $299/mo (~1.8M credits, 3 workspace seats); Business $990/mo adds low-latency TTS. Extra usage runs roughly $0.36 down to $0.17 per additional minute depending on tier.
tools.honest_knock: Credits are the meter and retakes are the tax — regenerate a paragraph three times and you pay three times, so real usage lands well above the calculator estimate. And read the free-tier fine print: $0 gets you 10k credits to play with, but no commercial license — anything you publish commercially needs at least the $6 Starter. Voice realism genuinely leads the market; niche names and jargon can still need manual retakes, so run your hardest paragraph through the free tier before subscribing.
tools.best_for: creators, developers and product teams that want the most realistic AI voices available — voiceovers, audiobooks, dubbing, conversational agents and a well-documented API
tools.skip_if: you generate hours of long-form audio on a tight budget (credit math punishes volume — flat-hour tools or the TTS built into your video editor may be enough), or you need acted emotional range only a human voice actor delivers
compare_with: Murf counters with studio workflow and per-language breadth, Descript bundles voice into a full video/podcast editor — ElevenLabs' edge is raw voice realism and the developer API

tools.name: EmailListVerify
tools.what_it_does: Email verification with never-expiring pay-as-you-go credits — bulk list cleaning, real-time API, inbox-placement testing and free DMARC/SPF tools, plus a credit-based email finder.
tools.pricing: (2026) Pay-as-you-go credits that never expire: 1,000 for $5 ($0.005/check), 5,000 for $17, 10,000 for $27, 25,000 for $54, 50,000 for $98 ($0.00196/check). A monthly subscription saves ~10% vs pay-as-you-go; API included. The email finder costs 5 credits per found address. Free tools: email validator, inbox-placement test, DMARC/SPF generators.
tools.honest_knock: The $5 entry pack is the most expensive way to buy: $0.005 per check versus $0.00196 at the 50k tier — a 2.5x spread that rewards guessing your volume upfront. And the email finder quietly consumes 5 credits per found address, so a 1,000-credit pack finds 200 emails, not 1,000.
tools.best_for: teams cleaning real sending lists before campaigns — bulk verification at volume rates, with credits that never expire
tools.skip_if: you verify tiny batches occasionally (the entry rate is the worst per-check price), or you mainly want prospecting — the finder burns credits five at a time
compare_with: Bouncer leans into deliverability polish and EU data residency; EmailListVerify wins on raw per-check price at volume, with never-expiring pay-as-you-go credits

tools.name: Emergent
tools.what_it_does: AI app builder. Describe what you want and Emergent builds full-stack web apps for you — an agentic, credit-based platform that turns prompts into working software with no manual coding.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free $0 (10 credits/mo), Standard $20/mo (100 credits), Pro $200/mo (750 credits), Team $300/mo (1,250 shared credits); ~17% off annual. Credits meter the work: simple changes 1–2, medium features 5–10, complex refactors 10–20+.
tools.honest_knock: The real cost is credit consumption, not the flat sticker — a genuinely complex app burns 10–20+ credits per big change, so serious builders move up tiers faster than the price list implies. Now do the division, because Emergent's own pricing page doesn't. Standard is $20 for 100 credits, so 20 cents a credit. Pro is $200 for 750, which is 26.7 cents. Team is $300 for 1,250, or 24 cents. Moving up a tier makes every unit of work more expensive, not less: Pro costs 33% more per credit than Standard, and annual billing keeps the gap (17 cents against 22.3). That is the opposite of the volume discount the ladder looks like — you are buying seats, support and headroom, not cheaper work. Check what your month actually needs before you upgrade; two Standard months and a top-up may beat one Pro month. And AI-generated code still needs a human eye: review it for security, correctness and maintainability before anything touches real users. It's a superb way to go from prompt to working prototype or MVP fast; it's not a hands-off factory for production software.
tools.best_for: founders, PMs and builders who want to turn a prompt into a working full-stack web app or MVP fast, without writing the code themselves
tools.skip_if: you need a hardened, security-audited production system with no human review, or your usage would burn through credits faster than the value returns
compare_with: close AI app-builder rivals — compare credit economics and output quality on the kind of app you actually build

tools.name: Employment Hero
tools.what_it_does: Modular HR, payroll and recruitment platform for small and mid-size employers.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Sold as separate modules rather than one plan. Recruitment: a free ATS tier at $0, then $199, $359, $639 and $959 a month for 50, 100, 200 and 300 AI video interviews — their page notes no HR or payroll subscription is required for these. HR Essentials $10 per employee per month, HR Engage $14, Payroll $10. Chat is $2 per employee per month with a stated $20 a month minimum. Every price on the page carries an asterisk.
tools.honest_knock: There is no such thing as the Employment Hero price. HR, payroll, recruitment and chat are four separate subscriptions and three of them are per employee, so the number you want is a sum you have to build yourself. A twenty-person company on HR Engage plus Payroll is $14 plus $10 per employee, which is $480 a month before recruitment. The recruitment tiers are the odd one out: they are priced by AI video interviews rather than by people, so a hiring push moves that line independently of your headcount. And every figure on the page has an asterisk against it — find out what those say before you compare this with anything.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size employers who want HR and payroll from one vendor and will genuinely use both, where the per-employee rate beats separate systems
tools.skip_if: you only need one of the four modules — each is sold separately and priced as though you are buying the platform, so a dedicated payroll or ATS tool is usually cheaper on its own
compare_with: the usual comparison — build the total for the modules you actually need at your headcount, because the entry per-employee rate is only one of three or four lines

tools.name: EngageBay
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one CRM, marketing, helpdesk and live chat for small teams — a genuine free tier (250 contacts) and per-user suites that undercut the big names.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 16 Jul 2026) Genuinely free tier: $0 for 250 contacts with email marketing, CRM, helpdesk and live chat. All-in-One suite per user/month: Basic $14.99 (500 contacts), Growth $64.99 (5,000 contacts, marketing automation), Pro $119.99 (unlimited contacts) — note the pricing page defaults to biennial ‘15% off’ display (Basic shows $12.74, Growth $55.24, Pro $101.99), so toggle to monthly for the list price. Single bays (Marketing or CRM & Sales) from $11.04/user/mo on that same biennial display.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is contacts AND seats at once: prices are per user, and each tier caps contacts — Basic’s 500 contacts fills fast, and the Growth jump is steep ($15 → $65 per user). The advertised ‘starts at $12.74’ assumes biennial prepay — two years upfront for the friendly number. Real automation only starts at Growth.
tools.best_for: small teams that want CRM, email marketing, helpdesk and live chat in one affordable suite — the free tier is a genuine trial-for-life, and it undercuts HubSpot hard at small scale
tools.skip_if: your contact list is big (per-tier caps push you up fast) or you need best-of-breed depth in one area — all-in-one means good-at-everything, not best-at-anything
compare_with: Keap is the automation-first veteran at a higher price point; EngageBay is the budget all-in-one with a real free tier — pick Keap for automation depth, EngageBay for breadth per dollar

tools.name: Envoy
tools.what_it_does: Workplace platform for visitor sign-in, desk and room booking, deliveries and emergency notifications.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Five products, each metered differently and all billed annually. Visitors: Basic free, Premium $362 per location per month, Enterprise quote-only. Emergency Notifications $2 per user per month. Reservations $5 per bookable resource per month. Screens $12 per device per month. Deliveries $250 per delivery location per month. Every product section carries the line 'Price excludes platform fee', and the page never says what that platform fee is.
