Year one on Professional is therefore $800 × 12 + $3,000 = $12,600 if you pay annually, or $890 × 12 + $3,000 = $13,680 month to month. The onboarding adds roughly a third to the first year, and no amount of shopping around removes it — it is mandatory. Enterprise does the same thing at $7,000 on top of $43,200 a year.

The third is the seat count, because it is not the meter that usually bites. Professional includes 3 Core Seats and 2,000 marketing contacts. For a marketing platform, contacts are the axis that grows on its own: your list gets bigger whether or not you hire anyone, and the contact tier moves the bill without anyone deciding to upgrade. Price your next two years on the list you expect to have, not the team you have now.

One more thing worth knowing before you start on Free. The free tier is genuinely usable — two users, 1,000 contacts, no expiry — and that is exactly how the ladder is designed to work. The step from Starter to Professional is not incremental: at list prices a three-seat team goes from $60 a month to $890 plus $3,000 once, which is roughly fifteen times the monthly cost. Whatever you build on Free, build it knowing where the next rung is.
tools.best_for: teams that want marketing, sales, service and content on one contact database and will actually use more than one hub — that shared database is the real product, and it is what makes the price defensible when you use the breadth
tools.skip_if: you need one job done well and cheaply, because a dedicated tool will almost always beat the equivalent HubSpot hub on price; or your contact list is growing fast and your budget is not, since contacts are the meter that moves without you touching anything
compare_with: the honest comparison is not feature-for-feature but shape-for-shape. Pipedrive and Close are sales tools that do one job and publish a per-seat price you can multiply in your head. HubSpot is a database with hubs bolted around it, priced on two meters at once — seats and contacts — with a mandatory onboarding fee at the Professional rung. If you want a CRM, the dedicated tools are cheaper and simpler. If you want marketing, sales and service reading from one contact record, that is the thing HubSpot sells and they do not really compete. Verify all current price lists yourself; ours were read on 18 August 2026.

tools.name: Hubstaff
tools.what_it_does: Time tracking with screenshots, activity levels, GPS and payroll integration for distributed teams.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced per seat. Their own worked example puts the Team plan at $10 per seat per month. Their FAQ is explicit about what a seat means: 'Hubstaff charges per seat. This means that even if only two out of your three team members are using its tracking features, you will still have to pay for all three members.' Seats added mid-term on an annual plan are prorated — their example is $60 for a seat added in July on a January-to-December plan. Monthly and annual options exist, with different proration rules, and add-ons are available on lower tiers.
tools.honest_knock: The seat definition is the whole story and they state it plainly, which deserves credit: you pay for every seat you have created, not every person actually being tracked. So an account that grew with your headcount and never got tidied up is billing you for people who left. Audit your seat list before renewal, not after. The second thing is that features on the lower tiers are add-ons rather than inclusions, so the plan you priced and the plan that does what you watched in the demo may not be the same one. And be clear with yourself about why you are buying it: screenshots and activity levels change how a team feels about their work, and that cost does not appear on any pricing page.
tools.best_for: agencies and distributed teams that bill clients for hours and need defensible time records — the proof is the product, and per-seat is fair when every seat is a person you invoice for
tools.skip_if: you want to know whether your team is working — that is a management problem and surveillance software makes it worse; also skip it if seats churn a lot, since you pay for every seat you forget to remove
compare_with: the direct time-tracking peers — both are cheaper and neither takes screenshots by default, so decide first whether you actually need the monitoring

tools.name: Iconosquare
tools.what_it_does: Social analytics, reporting and competitor benchmarking, deepest on Instagram and the core networks. Free for one user and two profiles, then Launch around €33/month and Scale €69. Tiers gate on seats and profiles, so agencies managing many brands climb faster than the entry price suggests.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, in euros, quoted at the default of 5 social profiles) Launch €33/mo billed yearly or €39 billed monthly (1 user, 100 posts a month, email support, 1 year of data retention); Scale €69 yearly or €83 monthly (3 users, unlimited posts, 1 group, chat support, 2 years of retention); Excel €116 yearly or €139 monthly (6 users, unlimited groups, white-label reporting, API access, dedicated CSM, unlimited retention). Yearly billing is advertised as two months free, and every plan starts with a 14-day trial. Custom pricing begins at 20 social profiles. The price scales with the number of profiles you manage, so these are entry figures rather than the whole ladder. There is a free tier at €0 (2 profiles, 1 user, 10 posts per month per profile, basic analytics), but Iconosquare frames it as free access after your trial rather than as a plan you sign up for.
tools.honest_knock: Its depth is strongest on Instagram and the core networks; if your priority platform sits outside its best-supported set, coverage thins. Analytics is where it shines — scheduling and community features exist but aren't always as deep as dedicated publishers. And the per-seat, per-profile tiering means agencies managing many brands climb toward the Excel tier quicker than the headline Launch price suggests.
tools.best_for: agencies and brands that want deep social analytics, reporting and competitor benchmarking alongside scheduling, especially Instagram-first teams
tools.skip_if: you need a heavy-duty publishing workhorse across many niche platforms, or a single free native analytics view already answers your questions
compare_with: Sprout is a pricier all-in-one, Later is scheduling-first — Iconosquare's edge is analytics depth per dollar

tools.name: iContact
tools.what_it_does: Straightforward email marketing for growing businesses. Build campaigns and automations with drag-and-drop design and deliverability support.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) No permanent free plan — a 30-day free trial, then paid tiers by contact count, with 15% off for paying yearly. At 500 contacts Standard is $9/mo and Premium $16/mo; the ladder then climbs with list size, with Standard running $14, $28, $45, $73, $110, $180, $250 and $350 a month at successive contact bands and Premium starting from $16 and $27 at the equivalent steps. Standard covers templates, landing pages and automations; Premium adds unlimited users, social posting and the AI content assistant. Larger lists are quoted.
tools.honest_knock: Pricing feels a touch high for what you get, and the Standard plan's hard caps on automations and landing pages push growing teams to upgrade sooner than expected. It's also less cutting-edge on automation than ActiveCampaign — its real edge is simplicity, strong deliverability and the included human support.
tools.best_for: small businesses and nonprofits who want a simple, reliable email tool with strong deliverability and a real marketing advisor included on every paid plan
tools.skip_if: you need advanced multi-branch automation (ActiveCampaign does more) or you're chasing the rock-bottom cheapest option

tools.name: IDrive
tools.what_it_does: Cloud backup across many devices, with versioning, snapshots and physical seed-and-restore shipping. Personal is 5 TB at $9.99/month, shown at $6.99 on annual billing — but that discount is first-year only and the renewal step is about 43%, so budget on year-two rates.
tools.pricing: (2026, re-verified 26 Jul 2026) Free 10 GB Basic tier. IDrive Mini is $0.25/month for 100 GB ($0.83/month for 500 GB). IDrive Personal is $9.99/month for 5 TB, shown discounted to $6.99/month with annual billing (save 30%), scaling up to $99.99/month ($69.99 discounted) at 100 TB. Team starts at the same $9.99/month ($6.99 discounted) for 5 computers and 5 users on 5 TB; Business starts at $19.99/month ($13.99 discounted) for 500 GB with unlimited users. Add-ons: server backup $5/month/server, and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace backup at $20/seat/year. The honest catch is on the pricing page in IDrive's own words: the discounted price applies to the first year, standard pricing applies from year two.
tools.honest_knock: The first-year price is a teaser and the renewal is the price — IDrive says so itself under the plan table, and on the current numbers the step from discounted to standard is about 43% (Personal 5 TB goes from $6.99 to $9.99 a month). Budget on year-two rates, not the banner. Beyond that, the honest backup fundamentals apply: a backup you never test-restore is a hope, not a backup, and the first full backup of multi-TB data takes weeks over the wire unless you use their physical Express seed shipping.
tools.best_for: individuals and small businesses that want cheap multi-device cloud backup with versioning, snapshots and physical seed/restore shipping
tools.skip_if: you need real-time sync-and-collaborate storage (that's Drive/Dropbox territory, not backup), or you won't tolerate the year-two renewal jump
compare_with: Backblaze is simpler flat-rate per computer; Acronis adds security suites — IDrive wins on multi-device flexibility per dollar, as long as you price in the year-two step-up

tools.name: InboxAlly
tools.what_it_does: Email deliverability tool that trains your sender reputation: engagement-based signals keep your campaigns and cold outreach out of spam and in the primary inbox — works alongside any ESP or email platform.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Starter about $149/mo (100 seed emails/day, 1 sender profile), Plus about $645/mo (500/day, 5 profiles), Premium about $1,190/mo (1,000/day, 10 profiles, strategy sessions); Enterprise custom. 10-day free trial, no card.
tools.honest_knock: This is a premium, seed-list-based deliverability tool, and the price reflects it — Starter alone is well above casual warm-up apps, so it only makes sense if inbox placement is genuinely costing you real revenue. It improves sender reputation through engagement signals, but it's not a magic fix for bad content or a purchased list: deliverability still depends on how you actually send. Buy it when the math (lost revenue from spam-foldering) clearly beats the monthly fee.
tools.best_for: serious senders — email marketers and cold-outreach teams — whose deliverability problems are costing measurable revenue and who need active reputation repair
tools.skip_if: you're a small sender who just needs basic list hygiene (cheaper warm-up tools suffice), or your inbox issues stem from content and list quality you haven't fixed
compare_with: lower-cost warm-up alternatives — InboxAlly is pricier and more hands-on; justify it by the revenue your spam-foldered mail is losing

tools.name: Increff
tools.what_it_does: Warehouse management plus algorithm-driven merchandising and inventory optimisation for omnichannel retail. There is no public pricing and no flat fee — every deal is quoted case by case against warehouses, users and modules, so budget for an enterprise implementation.
tools.pricing: No public pricing, re-verified 2026-08-17 and consistent across every reading we have. Increff's own /pricing URL returns a 404, and our monthly captures of the site in July and August 2026 produced no amount at all. Increff prices every deal case by case, scaled to the operation — warehouses, users and which modules you take (WMS, merchandising) — which their partnership team confirmed to us directly on 28 Jul 2026. There are no published tiers to compare, so budget for an enterprise implementation and ask for a tailored quote.
tools.honest_knock: This is enterprise omnichannel supply-chain software, and the opaque, quote-based pricing signals the target customer: retail brands with real scale, not small stores. The value — algorithmic merchandising and inventory optimization — only pays off at a catalog and volume large enough for those optimizations to move money. For a small or mid seller, it's likely more platform (and cost and implementation) than the problem warrants. For a scaling omnichannel brand, it's built for exactly that.
tools.best_for: retail brands and omnichannel sellers at real scale needing warehouse management plus algorithm-driven merchandising and inventory optimization
tools.skip_if: you're a small or single-channel store where simpler inventory software suffices, or you can't commit to an enterprise implementation
compare_with: comparable inventory/warehouse platforms — Increff leans algorithmic merchandising for scaled retail; get quotes and weigh implementation

tools.name: Insightful
tools.what_it_does: Workforce analytics and productivity monitoring — time tracking, workflow optimization and insider-threat detection, priced per seat.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Per-seat, billed annually. Workforce Analytics $8/seat/mo, Workflow Optimization $12/seat/mo, or both bundled at $16/seat/mo (saves 20%). Add-ons: Insider Threat Detection $4/seat/mo, advanced BI/API $0.50/seat/mo (talk-to-sales). A free audit is offered instead of a self-serve free tier.
tools.honest_knock: This is employee-monitoring software, so weigh the culture cost, not just the price: the advertised $8-16 rates are per seat AND assume annual billing, security features like insider-threat detection are a paid add-on, and monitoring tools can damage trust if rolled out without transparency.
tools.best_for: operations leaders who want transparent, consent-based workforce analytics — time tracking, productivity insight and workflow data — across in-office and remote teams
tools.skip_if: you value a low-surveillance culture, run a tiny team, or want month-to-month billing — the headline rates are annual and per seat
compare_with: Time Doctor is the established time-tracking incumbent; Insightful leans into workforce analytics and workflow optimization — similar per-seat model, so decide on features and how much monitoring your culture can carry

tools.name: Instapage
tools.what_it_does: Enterprise landing-page and conversion platform: build, personalize and A/B-test post-click landing pages at scale, with ad-to-page mapping, heatmaps and fast AMP pages — built for paid-ads and demand-gen teams.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 16 Jul 2026) Instapage no longer publishes plan prices: the pricing page now only offers ‘Try for free’ (14-day trial) and ‘Get a demo’. Last published rates (2026) were Create from $99/mo (~$79 annual, ~15k visitors) and Optimize $199-299/mo with visitor caps and overage fees; Convert was custom. Budget on a sales conversation for current numbers.
tools.honest_knock: It's premium-priced and only justified by serious ad spend — small budgets will feel it. Visitor caps mean overage fees, there's no 24/7 support, and like Unbounce it still can't generate a full landing page from one prompt. And the ownership question the feature list does not raise: publishing to your own domain means pointing a CNAME at Instapage — their help centre carries a per-registrar guide for exactly that — so the page is served by them and lives as long as the subscription does. Their own docs add a second catch worth knowing before you standardise on it: “we lock domains under the first Instapage account that uses them”. Treat these pages as rented campaign infrastructure, not as part of your site, and keep the copy somewhere you control.
tools.best_for: marketing teams running significant paid ad campaigns who need post-click optimisation — AdMap ad-to-page personalisation, A/B testing and heatmaps
tools.skip_if: you run limited ad campaigns or want budget pricing — at $99+/mo it's overkill below real paid-traffic volume
compare_with: the other premium and the budget landing-page builders

tools.name: InVideo
tools.what_it_does: Turns a prompt or script into a first-draft video with AI voiceover, templates and stock footage. AI minutes are metered and do not roll over: Plus is around $28/month for roughly 50 minutes, Max $50–60 for 200. The free tier is watermarked, so it serves as evaluation only.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free plan (limited AI minutes, watermarked); Plus around $28/mo (removes watermark, ~50 AI minutes, commercial rights); Max around $50–60/mo (~200 AI minutes, 4K); a higher generative tier about $100+/mo. Roughly 20% off annual. Unused credits don't roll over.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is the credit model — AI minutes are metered and don't roll over, so heavy users burn an allowance faster than the flat monthly price implies, and the free tier's watermark makes it evaluation-only. AI video is fast but generic by default: templated output needs real editing and brand direction to not look like everyone else's. Treat it as a first-draft engine, not a finished-studio replacement.
tools.best_for: marketing teams and creators who want to turn a prompt or script into a publish-ready first-draft video fast, using templates, AI voiceover and stock
tools.skip_if: you need frame-level creative control, long-form or highly bespoke production, or your usage would blow past the monthly AI-minute allowance
compare_with: Pictory is a close text-to-video peer; Synthesia leans avatar/presenter video — pick by whether you need a talking head

tools.name: involve.me
tools.what_it_does: Interactive funnel builder: quizzes, calculators, assessments and payment pages with built-in email sequences — free tier to start, paid tiers priced by live-funnel count from $19/mo annual.
tools.pricing: (verified 17 Jul 2026) Free tier to start; Start $19/mo billed annually ($29 month-to-month) with 3 live funnels and 1 user; Grow $49/mo annual ($69 monthly) with 5 funnels and 2 users; Scale $119/mo annual ($139 monthly) with 25 funnels, A/B testing and lead verification; Enterprise from $399/mo on annual contracts only. Extra seats $10/user/mo.
tools.honest_knock: The tier ladder is really a funnel-count ladder — 3 live funnels on Start evaporates once you run campaigns in parallel, and the advertised prices are annual: month-to-month runs $10-20 higher per tier. And the honest fundamental for any interactive-funnel tool: quizzes and calculators convert traffic you already have — they don’t create it, so validate on the free tier before the subscription outruns the pipeline.
tools.best_for: marketers building interactive lead-gen — quizzes, calculators, assessments and payment funnels with built-in email sequences — who want a free tier to validate the concept first
tools.skip_if: you just need a simple form (lighter tools do that free), or you don’t yet have the traffic to feed an interactive funnel
compare_with: FlexiQuiz is the graded-quiz specialist — exams, certificates, question banks; involve.me plays the marketing game with funnels, lead capture and payments. Pick by whether you’re testing knowledge or generating pipeline

tools.name: Jibble
tools.what_it_does: Time and attendance tracking with facial recognition, GPS and payroll-ready timesheets.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Their own claim on that page is a free forever plan with unlimited users, described as '100% free', with no credit card required. Paid tiers exist above it but their prices are rendered in the browser and were not visible in the page we could read, so we are not quoting them. The page leads with a savings calculator rather than a price table.
tools.honest_knock: Free forever with unlimited users is a real claim and unusual in this category, where per-seat pricing is the norm — that alone makes it worth a look for a team on a tight budget. Two things to establish before you rely on it. First, what the free tier actually excludes, because 'unlimited users' and 'unlimited features' are different promises and the paid tiers exist for a reason. Second, note that their pricing page leads with a calculator showing what you supposedly save rather than what you pay: that is a marketing choice, and the number it produces rests on assumptions about payroll leakage that are theirs, not measured in your business.
tools.best_for: teams that need attendance records without a per-seat bill — if the free tier covers your case it is genuinely free, which nothing else in this category offers
tools.skip_if: you need the paid features, because you will have to get those prices from them directly; also skip facial recognition without checking your local rules on biometric data, which is a legal question rather than a pricing one
compare_with: the direct time-tracking peers — both have free tiers too, so compare on what each free plan excludes rather than on the headline

tools.name: Joiin
tools.what_it_does: Financial consolidation and group reporting for multi-entity, multi-currency organisations — connects Xero, QuickBooks and Sage, with unlimited users and reports on every plan.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Joiin's own machine-readable pricing page) 14-day free trial, no credit card; unlimited users and reports on every plan. Priced by the number of companies you consolidate, and the page shows both columns — monthly against annual (per month): 1 company $28 / $23, 2 $36 / $29, 5 $70 / $57, 10 $111 / $92, 20 $167 / $139, 50 $217 / $174, 100 $336 / $252. Above 100 companies it starts from $336/mo plus $2.80 per additional company. Paying monthly runs roughly 20% above the annual rate at every step.
tools.honest_knock: The $23 headline covers a single company on annual billing — but consolidation is the whole point of Joiin, and a real group of 10-20 entities lands at $92-139 a month. Month-to-month billing adds roughly two months per year, and it consolidates what its integrations reach: Xero, QuickBooks and Sage, plus spreadsheet imports for everything else.
tools.best_for: finance teams and accountants consolidating multi-entity, multi-currency group reporting from Xero, QuickBooks or Sage without hand-built spreadsheets
tools.skip_if: you run a single entity (your accounting platform's own reports cover it), or your ledgers live outside the supported integrations and you'd be importing spreadsheets anyway
compare_with: Fathom leans into analysis and presentation-grade reporting; Joiin is the leaner consolidation specialist with per-entity pricing and unlimited users

tools.name: Jotform AI Agents
tools.what_it_does: Build AI chatbots and customer-service agents in minutes — no code required. Handles leads, support tickets and bookings 24/7. Integrates with your existing forms and CRMs.
tools.pricing: (2026) A free Starter tier (5 agents, ~100 conversations/mo); paid plans Bronze ~$34/mo, Silver ~$49/mo (2,500 conversations) and Gold ~$129/mo (10,000 conversations), scaling by conversations, voice minutes, SMS and knowledge-base size. Enterprise is custom.
tools.honest_knock: The gating detail is conversations, not features — the free and lower tiers cap monthly conversations quickly, so an agent that actually gets used will push you up a tier, and voice minutes and SMS are metered separately on top. It's also tightly bound to the Jotform ecosystem: brilliant if you already live in Jotform forms, less compelling as a standalone chatbot if you don't. For form-driven support and lead capture, it's a fast, low-code win.
tools.best_for: teams already using Jotform (or wanting no-code) that need AI chatbots and service agents to handle leads, support and bookings tied to their forms
tools.skip_if: you need a deeply customizable, standalone conversational-AI platform, or your conversation volume would make the per-tier caps expensive
compare_with: dedicated AI-support platforms — Jotform's edge is no-code and form integration; compare on conversation limits at your real volume

tools.name: Jubilee
tools.what_it_does: Bankruptcy petition preparation, document automation and case management for legal practices. $95 per case pay-as-you-go, or annual plans from $995 for up to 36 filings to $4,995 for 500. Size the tier to your real filing volume; sporadic filers do better per case.
tools.pricing: Pay As You Go at $95 per case, or annual subscriptions billed by yearly filing volume: Jubilee 36 $995/yr (up to 36 filings, 2 users, $34.99/case over), Jubilee 150 $2,495/yr (up to 150, 3 users, $26.99 over), Jubilee 300 $3,995/yr (up to 300, 3 users, $17.99 over), Jubilee 500 $4,995/yr (up to 500, 5 users, $12.99 over). Prices are for annual billing (re-verified 2026-07-19).
tools.honest_knock: It's a focused vertical tool — bankruptcy petition preparation and case management — so its whole value is bounded by that practice area; a general legal practice won't get much from it. The case-count tiers are the thing to size correctly: pick 36 vs 300 by your real annual filing volume, and check whether the pay-per-case option is cheaper if you file sporadically. For a bankruptcy practice, the automation and court-form handling are exactly the point.
tools.best_for: bankruptcy attorneys and legal professionals who want streamlined petition preparation, document automation and case management for filings
tools.skip_if: you don't practice bankruptcy law, or you file so few cases that a general practice-management tool plus manual forms is enough
compare_with: Best Case (Stretto) or general practice-management software
the established bankruptcy-software peer — Jubilee competes on price and cloud access; size the case tier to your volume

tools.name: Kartra
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one platform for selling online: landing pages, email automation, funnels, memberships and checkout in one tool — no plugins to stitch together.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) Four tiers, monthly against yearly: Essentials $59 / $52, Growth $119 / $99, Advanced $229 / $189 and Professional $549 / $429, with yearly billing advertised as saving up to 22% and a 14-day trial. The line that changes the arithmetic and is missing from most summaries: Essentials charges a 5% transaction fee on your sales, and the tiers above it charge 0%. On $10,000 a month of sales that fee is $500, which makes the $60 step from Essentials to Growth trivially worth taking. Essentials also sends 10,000 emails and texts a month against unlimited above it, and includes 1 custom domain.
tools.honest_knock: If your core need is polished course delivery, Kajabi's creator features are stronger; Kartra wins on all-in-one breadth, not course depth.
tools.best_for: creators and coaches who want funnels, email, checkout, memberships and scheduling under one roof instead of five subscriptions
tools.skip_if: you only need one of those pieces — a dedicated tool does that piece better and cheaper than an all-in-one

tools.name: Katana MRP
tools.what_it_does: Cloud manufacturing and inventory platform for product businesses. Live inventory control, production scheduling and order syncing across your sales channels — know exactly what to make and when.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A Free plan covering 30 SKUs with unlimited users, integrations and locations plus full features and API, then Core starting at $299/mo with unlimited SKUs and users and 24/7 support, and an Advantage tier on custom pricing. The add-ons are where the real cost sits and they are priced separately: manufacturing routings and insights $199/mo, end-to-end traceability via batch or serial numbers $249/mo, warehouse management with bin locations and pick-and-pack $149/mo, plus an optional $2,000 item on the page. Higher monthly sales-order volume also raises the effective cost.
tools.honest_knock: The $299 headline is the floor, and the features most manufacturers actually need — production routings and traceability — are paid add-ons on top, which is why real bills often land two to three times higher. Cost also rises with sales-order volume, so a busy month is a bigger month. It's genuinely capable manufacturing software; just price the add-ons you need, not the base plan.
tools.best_for: product makers and small manufacturers who need live inventory, production scheduling and multi-channel order sync in one cloud platform
tools.skip_if: you're a simple reseller who doesn't manufacture (a plain inventory tool is cheaper), or your volume is too low to justify the add-on-driven real cost
compare_with: comparable manufacturing/inventory platforms — weigh by which add-ons you'd actually enable and your order volume

tools.name: Keap
tools.what_it_does: CRM, sales and marketing automation built for small businesses. Capture leads, automate follow-up and manage your pipeline in one place.
tools.pricing: Starting at $299/mo billed monthly for the whole platform — no feature-based tiers and no free plan; users and contacts are added on top via the calculator on their pricing page, and Keap requires paid implementation services (strategy consulting, data import and migration) that are quoted separately before you go live (re-verified 2026-07-21).
tools.honest_knock: Cost is the big one (56% of reviewers flag it), the interface feels dated, and there's a real 2–4 week learning curve on the automation builder. Billing and cancellation complaints are common, and email design is thinner than dedicated email tools.
tools.best_for: service-based small businesses, coaches and solopreneurs who want CRM, email, payments and automation in one tool — and will invest the time to learn it
tools.skip_if: you're price-sensitive, want a modern UI, or only need simple email — the cost and learning curve bite
compare_with: the more modern all-in-one and the automation specialist

tools.name: Keeper Security
tools.what_it_does: Password manager and privileged access management for teams, with a zero-knowledge architecture.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own business pricing page) No per-user prices are shown for any business tier. Three plans are listed — Business Starter, Business and Enterprise — all billed annually, with Business Starter stated as 5 to 10 users. A long list of capabilities is sold separately rather than included: Secrets Manager, Advanced Reporting & Alerts, Compliance Reporting, remote access and privileged session management, endpoint privilege management and threat detection. KeeperPAM is described as available through sales only, priced to organisation size, and KeeperMSP requires contacting sales.
tools.honest_knock: The business pricing page does not price the business plans. What it does do is list, at length, what is not included — Secrets Manager, compliance reporting, session management, endpoint privilege management are all separate purchases — so the tier you pick is a base and the security posture you were sold on is an assembly. Annual billing is stated on every tier, so there is no month-to-month option to test with, and Business Starter has a floor of five users. Ask for the per-user price of the base plan and each add-on you need as separate lines, because a bundled quote here hides which part is actually costing you.
tools.best_for: teams that need shared credentials with real admin control and audit, and that will genuinely use the provisioning and role-based access that separate this from a consumer password manager
tools.skip_if: you are under five people wanting a shared vault, since Business Starter has a five-user floor and consumer or small-team plans elsewhere are cheaper and published
compare_with: the direct team password-manager comparison — both publish per-user prices, so use those as the anchor for Keeper's quote

tools.name: Kinsta
tools.what_it_does: Managed WordPress hosting on Google Cloud, with free migrations and 24/7 support. From about $35/month for one site (25,000 visits, 10 GB), or roughly $29 billed annually. Exceeding the visit cap bills per 1,000 extra visits, and Kinsta confirms it offers no partner-only discount codes.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own plans page, USD, tax excluded) Managed WordPress hosting from $35/mo for a single site, or $30/mo billed annually $350 a year, with the first month free on top — Kinsta advertises annual as two months off. That entry plan carries one WordPress install, 10GB storage, 125GB CDN bandwidth and 14 days of backup retention, and you choose whether it is metered on bandwidth (20GB) or on visits (35,000), which is a real change from the visit-only plans older reviews describe. Multi-site plans start at $59/mo $700 a year for two installs, and agency plans start at $340/mo, or $284/mo billed annually at $3,400 a year. It is a premium tier — cheaper shared hosts exist. There is no exclusive discount code to look for: Kinsta confirmed to us on 28 Jul 2026 that it gives no partner-only or affiliate-only discounts.
tools.honest_knock: You're paying a premium for managed speed, Google Cloud infrastructure and expert support — worth it if performance and hands-off management matter, wasteful on a low-traffic hobby site a $5 shared host would carry fine.
tools.best_for: business-critical WordPress sites where speed, uptime and expert support directly affect revenue
tools.skip_if: you run a small, low-traffic site on a tight budget — entry-level shared hosting or a caching plugin gets you most of the way for a fraction of the price

tools.name: Kit
tools.what_it_does: Email marketing built for creators (formerly ConvertKit). Grow your list with landing pages and forms, then automate newsletters and sell digital products from one place; a beta Kit MCP connects AI assistants like Claude directly to your account. Recent additions: a new landing-page editor, Dynamic Content, Newsletter Sponsorships, and App Store integrations on paid plans — SMS via SlickText, Patreon member sync (tier and support data in automations), Luma/Eventbrite event sync, and two-way HubSpot CRM sync on Pro.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-09) The free Newsletter plan is $0/mo and covers 1,000 email subscribers, with one basic Visual Automation plus unlimited landing pages, forms and broadcasts. Creator is $39/mo billed monthly, or $33/mo billed yearly ($390 a year, saving $78). Pro — the tier that adds subscriber scoring, engagement analytics and deliverability reporting — is $79/mo billed monthly, or $66/mo billed yearly ($790 a year, saving $158). Paying yearly saves 17%. Every price on the page is quoted for 1,000 email subscribers and Kit bills by list size, so read the tier for your own list before you budget. Paid plans open with a 14-day free trial without a card, and migrations are free.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest notes. Subscriber-based pricing counts everyone on your list — cold subscribers cost the same as fans, so prune before you price. And the free plan is smaller than Kit's reputation suggests: it stops at 1,000 subscribers (re-verified 2026-08-09), so the month your list outgrows that number you are on Creator at $39/mo, or $33/mo if you pay a year up front. The creator-first features (tip jars, paid newsletters, recommendations) remain the real differentiator.
tools.best_for: creators, writers and coaches building an audience-first business who want email, landing pages, digital products and a creator network in one
tools.skip_if: you're an e-commerce store (commerce-native email tools fit better) or your list is big-but-cold — clean it before paying per subscriber
compare_with: the creator-email rivals — Beehiiv leans newsletter-growth mechanics, MailerLite undercuts on price; Kit wins on creator-commerce maturity

tools.name: Kixie
tools.what_it_does: Power dialer with SMS and CRM integration for outbound sales teams. Kixie publishes no seat price: three tiers separated by how many lines they dial, with the multi-line AI voice detection, ConnectionBoost, Conversation Intelligence and DNC compliance all sold as add-ons on top.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-18, read on their own pricing page) No seat price is published. Three plans are listed — Professional, Single-Line PowerDialer and Multi-Line PowerDialer — with a quarterly/yearly toggle but no amount rendered anywhere on the page. The core phone system is identical on all three; what separates them is dialling: no PowerDialer on Professional, one line on Single-Line, up to four simultaneous lines on Multi-Line, which is also the only tier offering AI human voice detection and offers it as a premium add-on. ConnectionBoost, Conversation Intelligence and DNC compliance are add-ons at every tier. The plan cards claim unlimited US/Canada minutes while the FAQ prices unlimited US and Canada minutes at $30 a month per user, so which of the two applies belongs in writing in your quote. First US/Canada number free, extra local numbers $5.00 a month, porting in free. Texts from $0.011 each on a registered 10DLC number, inbound free. 7-day trial, no credit card.
tools.honest_knock: Plan for 30-60% above the sticker: minutes, the multi-line dialer and AI human-voice-detection all bill separately, and the quarterly auto-renewing contract only allows downgrades in its final 30 days — read that clause before signing. The dialer itself is genuinely fast and CRM-native; just buy it with the full basket priced and the calendar reminder set (our Renewal Radar exists for exactly this).
tools.best_for: outbound sales teams living in their CRM that want a serious power dialer with local presence, SMS and automation
tools.skip_if: low call volumes (per-seat + minutes math won't pay back), or you want monthly flexibility without contract fine print
compare_with: dialer peers with simpler pricing — compare all-in per-seat including minutes, and the contract terms

tools.name: KrispCall
tools.what_it_does: Virtual numbers across 100+ countries with a shared dashboard, dialer and CRM hooks, from about $12/user/month on annual billing. Calls and SMS are pay-as-you-go from a separate credit balance, so compare per-country call rates at your volume rather than the seat price.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against the vendor's own pricing page) Essential $12 per user/mo billed annually or $15 monthly, for solo agents and teams up to 5 people; Standard $32 per user/mo annually or $40 monthly, for teams scaling up to 50 users; Enterprise custom. Annual saves 20%, which the page puts at $36 per user a year on Essential and $96 on Standard, and each plan comes with $1 of free calling and SMS credit. Calls and SMS are otherwise pay-as-you-go from a separate credit balance, and numbers carry their own one-off and monthly charges (from $4.50 one-off and $1.50 a month at the time of reading).
tools.honest_knock: Same honest math as most budget VoIP: the plan buys the platform, the meter buys the conversations — per-minute and per-SMS charges land on top of every seat, so the comparison that matters is call-rate-per-country at your volume. The 100+ country number coverage is genuinely the draw; verify number availability and local regulations for your specific target countries before committing.
tools.best_for: sales and support teams that need virtual numbers across many countries with a shared dashboard, dialer and CRM hooks at a budget seat price
tools.skip_if: your calling is domestic-only at low volume (simpler tools suffice), or you need enterprise reliability guarantees over price
compare_with: the direct budget-VoIP set — differences live in per-country rates and number availability, so price your actual destinations

tools.name: Landingi
tools.what_it_does: Landing page builder with 400+ templates, from $29/month for unlimited pages and 5,000 visitors; A/B testing and pop-ups start at $49. Roughly half what Unbounce and Instapage charge, and the trade is no AI traffic routing, no real-time collaboration and thinner technical control.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17; the English page quotes USD while the same page served from a Dutch address quotes euros at the same numerals, so check your own currency) Four plans, billed annually: Build $24/month, Optimize $119/month, Scale from $229/month and Enterprise from $1,199/month. Annual billing includes two months free against monthly. Custom domains are metered: 1 on Build, 3 on Optimize, 10 on Scale and 100 on Enterprise, with extras at $5 a month each. AI credits come with the plan (2,500, 10,000, 20,000 and 60,000 a month) and top-ups are pay-as-you-go at $15 for 5,000, $25 for 10,000 and $40 for 20,000. A promotional rate roughly half the Build price appears periodically — it is a limited-time offer rather than the standard rate.
tools.honest_knock: You trade away the high-end optimisation: no AI traffic routing like Unbounce's Smart Traffic, no real-time collaboration, and thinner technical control (script containers). Excellent value, but not the conversion-optimisation powerhouse.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious teams, international businesses and anyone needing bulk or programmatic page generation across 29 languages
tools.skip_if: you need AI traffic routing, real-time collaboration or deep technical control — that's where Unbounce earns its higher price

tools.name: Later
tools.what_it_does: Visual social media scheduler and planner. Plan, preview and auto-publish posts across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and more from one calendar.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Starter $18.75/month, Growth $37.50 and Scale $82.50, all billed yearly, which Later advertises as three months free and 25% off against monthly. There is a limited free plan and a 14-day trial. The add-ons are where a growing team pays more: extra Social Sets are $11.25 a month each, extra users $3.75 a month each, and extra AI credits $3.75 a month per 100 credits. Starter covers casual scheduling; Growth adds the inbox, approvals and longer analytics; Scale is aimed at enterprise-level analytics without an enterprise contract.
tools.honest_knock: The Starter caps are where the price really lives: 30 posts per profile and 3 months of analytics run out fast for an active brand, pushing real users toward Growth — so compare at the tier you'll actually need, not the entry price. Later's visual-first planning (born from Instagram) is still its strength; if your world is link-in-bio commerce and grids, that focus earns its seat.
tools.best_for: creators and visual-first brands (Instagram/TikTok-centric) that want drag-and-drop visual planning, link-in-bio and scheduling in one
tools.skip_if: you need deep multi-network publishing, listening and team workflows at agency scale (suite-class tools fit), or the post caps chafe immediately
compare_with: Buffer is the lean generalist, Vista undercuts on breadth — Later wins on visual planning UX for Instagram-first work

tools.name: Leadfeeder
tools.what_it_does: Website visitor identification for B2B sales. See which companies visit your site and what they viewed, and turn anonymous traffic into a warm pipeline.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Lite €0 forever, after a 14-day full-access trial: the last 100 identified companies, 7 days of visitor history, 20 credits a month. Discover from €79/month billed annually, or €113 month-to-month. Activate from €369 annually, or €527 monthly. Scale €599, annual billing only. Enterprise quote-only. Users are unlimited on every tier. Credits are consumed by enrichment and activation actions, not by identifying a company. The identified-company allowance per paid tier is shown only as 'Tiered', with no numbers.
tools.honest_knock: The words doing the work are 'starting at'. What actually sets your price is how many companies you identify a month, and the page shows that allowance as 'Tiered' with no figures at any level — so €79 is the floor of the smallest bucket and you cannot tell from the page which bucket your traffic puts you in. Get that table before you talk price. Two other things: month-to-month costs 43% more than annual on the same plan (€113 against €79), and Scale is annual-only, so the tier most growing teams land on cannot be tried for a month.
tools.best_for: B2B teams with real website traffic and a sales team that will actually work the list — the free tier is enough to find out whether your traffic contains anyone worth calling
tools.skip_if: your traffic is mostly consumer or very low volume, because company identification needs business networks to match against and thin traffic produces a thin list
compare_with: the direct visitor-identification peers — compare the identified-company allowance at your traffic level, since that is the number that sets the bill

tools.name: Leadpages
tools.what_it_does: Landing pages, pop-ups and alert bars, with unlimited traffic on every Leadpages plan where metered rivals count visitors. Conversion plans run $99 (Grow) to $399 (Scale), alongside a separate HTML Pub publishing line at $10–49. The value pick rather than the optimisation pick.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Leadpages' own machine-readable pricing file, which they last updated 2026-07-10; USD) Two lines, six paid plans, no free plan, and a 7-day free trial that requires a credit card and converts unless you cancel. Publishing plans: Starter $10/mo or $8 billed annually ($96 a year), 5 pages, 1 site, no third-party integrations; Pro $29/mo or $23 annually ($276), 25 pages, 1 blog, API access; Business $49/mo or $39 annually ($468), 50 pages, 2 sites. Optimization plans add testing and personalisation: Grow $99/mo or $79 annually ($948), unlimited pages, 4 sites, manual A/B testing; Optimize $199/mo or $159 annually ($1,908), 6 sites, multivariate testing and Smart Traffic; Scale $399/mo or $319 annually ($3,828), 10 sites, heatmaps, auto-personalisation and 10 seats. Annual billing is 20% off across the board. No plan has a traffic cap. Add-ons: $20 a month per extra seat or extra custom domain, $40 per extra client workspace on Scale, and AI credit top-ups from $2.50 for 2,000 credits down to $0.60 per thousand at the largest pack.
tools.honest_knock: It's the value pick, not the optimisation pick — if you're spending big on ads, Unbounce's Smart Traffic and Instapage's 1:1 personalisation go deeper.
tools.best_for: small businesses building landing pages and simple funnels who want unmetered traffic — no per-visitor anxiety, unlike metered rivals
tools.skip_if: you need deep A/B experimentation or enterprise features — the Conversion tier jumps to $299/mo fast

tools.name: LearnWorlds
tools.what_it_does: Create, sell and scale online courses. Build a branded school with interactive video, assessments, certificates and a built-in checkout.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Starter $29/mo (or $24 annually) but with a $5 fee per enrollment — confirmed on the page today and the single most important number in this ladder; Pro Trainer $99/mo with no transaction fee; Learning Center $299/mo; High Volume and Corporate quoted. Annual billing saves 20% and there is a 30-day trial. A branded mobile app is a separate add-on at roughly $149/mo, and your payment gateway (Stripe at about 2.9% + $0.30) charges on top regardless of tier. The plan prices themselves render client-side; the enrollment fee and uptime commitments are what the page publishes in plain text.
tools.honest_knock: The detail most people miss is Starter's $5-per-enrollment fee — at any real sales volume it quietly makes Starter more expensive than the flat Pro Trainer plan, so the "cheap" tier often isn't. The genuinely powerful interactive-video and assessment features live higher up, and the branded mobile app is a steep separate add-on. Price it against your expected enrollment volume, not the sticker.
tools.best_for: course creators and training businesses that want a branded school with interactive video, assessments, certificates and a built-in checkout
tools.skip_if: you sell only occasional courses (a lighter or transaction-fee-only platform may cost less) or you just need to host a few videos behind a paywall
compare_with: close course-platform peers — LearnWorlds leads on interactivity and branding; compare transaction-fee structures at your volume

tools.name: Leavo
tools.what_it_does: Team time-tracking, attendance and overtime banking with transparent per-user pricing and a 30-day free trial.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against leavo.com) (2026) 30-day free trial with unlimited members (a trial, not a permanent free plan). Professional $2.49/user/mo billed yearly (about $448/yr for 15 users) adds unlimited features and overtime banking; Premium $4.15/user/mo yearly (about $747/yr for 15). Priced per user, annual billing.
tools.honest_knock: The tidy per-user numbers are annual-billed, and it's priced per seat — every employee you track adds to the bill, with no volume break shown. And the “free” is a 30-day trial, not a permanent free tier: budget for the paid plan from day 31.
tools.best_for: teams that want straightforward time-tracking, attendance and overtime banking with transparent per-user pricing
tools.skip_if: you need a permanent free plan (this is a 30-day trial), or you're a tiny team where a shared spreadsheet already covers hours
compare_with: Toggl is the established time-tracker with a genuinely free tier for small teams; Leavo leans into attendance and overtime banking — richer there, but per-seat and trial-only at the free end

tools.name: lemlist
tools.what_it_does: Cold email outreach and sales engagement. Build personalized multichannel sequences (email, LinkedIn, calls) with built-in deliverability tools, and trigger them off buying-intent signals its agents surface.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17; the page served us DOLLARS today where our previous reading was in euros, with the same numerals — check your own checkout) No free plan, 14-day trial. Email is $69/month, or $55/month on yearly billing, covering unlimited users and 50,000 emails a month. Multichannel is $109/month per user, or $87/month yearly, with unlimited emails and messages and 5 senders per user. Quarterly billing saves 10% and yearly 20%. Enterprise (5+ users) is quote-only. Contact data is billed separately through rechargeable credits where 1 credit = $0.01: a 1,000-credit pack is $10 and buys roughly 200 email lookups or 50 phone numbers, with a phone number costing 20 credits.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat plus per-email-account model makes total cost unpredictable as you scale, and reviews flag support response times and the LinkedIn Chrome-extension's reliability.
tools.best_for: outbound teams that live in cold email and want multichannel sequences, warm-up and a big template community in one per-seat tool
tools.skip_if: you send occasional one-off campaigns — the entry plan starts at 69€/month and only pays off with steady outbound volume

tools.name: LettrLabs
tools.what_it_does: Automated direct-mail marketing: design, personalise and send physical mailers — handwritten letters, postcards — at scale, synced with your digital campaigns and tracked for ROI.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) Robotically handwritten pieces start around $0.49 each including postage (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Direct mail only pays off with a tight list and a real offer — it's a leverage channel, not a cheap thing to test blindly.
tools.best_for: local businesses and e-commerce brands using robotically handwritten mail (~$0.49/piece incl. postage) to stand out where email gets ignored
tools.skip_if: your audience or offer doesn't justify ~$0.49 per contact — direct mail only pays at decent response rates and order values

tools.name: Lindy.ai
tools.what_it_does: An AI teammate that lives in Slack: @mention it and it works across your other tools, sits in meetings for shared context and runs jobs on a schedule. Sold per user — Plus $29.99/month for 3k credits, Pro $99.99 for 15k — so cost tracks headcount, and a removed seat runs to the end of the cycle.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-12, read on their own pricing page) Now sold per user, and the credit allowance is published again: Plus $29.99/mo per user (3k credits per user per month), Pro $99.99/mo per user (15k credits, 5x Plus) or Max $199.99/mo per user (35k credits, ~12x Plus). Enterprise is quote-only. Every seat's credits pool into one workspace balance, refresh each billing cycle and do not roll over; the page sizes work as 2-250 credits for an everyday ask, 250-1,000 for deep work and 1,000-2,500 for a big build. Anyone who uses Lindy takes a paid seat, including colleagues who only @mention it in Slack — those who join that way get a 7-day free trial first, direct signups are billed straight away. All four tiers connect up to 5 inboxes, and computer use, model selection and MCP support are no longer tier-gated.
tools.honest_knock: Cost tracks headcount rather than output: every colleague who so much as @mentions Lindy in Slack takes a paid seat, and a seat you remove runs to the end of the cycle with no mid-cycle proration. Credits are published now, but as ranges — an everyday ask is 2-250, a big build 1,000-2,500 — so a month is still an estimate, and when the shared pool runs dry there is no top-up: Lindy pauses credit-using actions until the reset unless an admin moves the workspace to a bigger plan.
tools.best_for: teams that live in Slack and want one shared teammate that sits in their meetings, runs scheduled routines and drafts replies inside the tools they already use
tools.skip_if: you want flat, predictable automation costs across a large team — Lindy charges for every seat that touches it and the credits expire each cycle, so you pay for people whether or not they used their allowance
compare_with: trigger-based automation tools with flatter pricing

tools.name: Livestorm
tools.what_it_does: Browser-based webinars with registration, automated emails, polls and analytics. There is no plan price: Pro sells attendee credits at €2.50 each, bought a year up front, and one credit is spent per unique participant per session — a four-part series to 200 people costs 800 credits.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) There is still no plan price. Pro is sold as attendee credits at €2.50 each, bought as a yearly pack up front, with sessions up to 4 hours and unlimited team members; Enterprise is quote-only with sessions up to 12 hours. Their own definition, worth reading twice because it decides your bill: one credit is spent for each unique participant, per session, over a 12-month period. Someone attending two different sessions costs 2 credits; the same person joining live and later watching the replay of that session counts once. Registrants who never show up cost nothing, and your own team members never consume credits.
tools.honest_knock: This is a bet on attendance that you place a year in advance. You buy credits up front at €2.50 each, and a credit is spent per unique participant per session — so a four-part series to the same 200 people is 800 credits, not 200, which is €2,000. A webinar that does better than expected runs you out; one nobody attends still cost you nothing back. The page will not show you a total: the slider moves but the price does not appear until you engage. Before you commit, count sessions times expected attendees for the whole year, and ask what happens to unused credits at the twelve-month mark, because the page does not say.
tools.best_for: teams running a predictable programme of webinars to a known audience size, where buying a year of attendance up front is cheaper than a per-seat platform
tools.skip_if: your webinar schedule is irregular or experimental, because paying a year ahead for attendance you cannot forecast is the wrong shape; a per-month platform is safer while you find out what works
compare_with: the usual alternatives — both price per host per month, so compare that against your credits divided across a year

tools.name: Logome.ai
tools.what_it_does: Generates a logo and basic brand assets from a prompt. Designing and previewing is free, but downloading requires a paid plan — Basic at around $29/month gives one file without a transparent background. Their public site including pricing returned 404 at last check, so verify what you are charged.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, with a caveat) The pricing page did not return figures we could read, and neither of our monthly captures retrieved an amount, so today's prices are not independently confirmed. Our dated reading: design and preview are free with no signup, but downloads require a paid plan — Basic about $29/mo ($19 annually) for one logo file, Premium about $99/mo ($49 annually) for five logos with transparent backgrounds and high-resolution formats, and a Logo + Brand Kit tier about $199/mo ($99 annually) for a full identity package. All paid plans include commercial rights, which is the part that matters for a business logo.
tools.honest_knock: Update, 21 Jul 2026: Logome's public website, including its pricing page, is currently returning 404 and only the app itself still loads, so we cannot verify any price or plan detail right now. Treat the figures below as last-known rather than confirmed, and check what you are actually charged before you commit. The honest catch is the free-to-design, pay-to-download model — you can fall in love with a logo before you learn that using it costs a subscription, and the Basic tier gives just one file without a transparent background, which pushes most real users to Premium. AI logos are also a starting point, not a trademark: they can resemble common templates, so check distinctiveness before you build a brand on one. For a fast, cheap first identity, it's genuinely handy.
tools.best_for: founders and small businesses that want a professional-looking logo and basic brand assets generated fast and cheaply, without hiring a designer
tools.skip_if: you need a truly bespoke, trademark-safe brand identity (hire a designer), or the single-file Basic tier won't give you the formats you actually need
compare_with: close AI logo generators — compare download formats, ownership terms and how much the transparent-background/brand-kit features cost

tools.name: Lucrovox
tools.what_it_does: AI phone agent for local service businesses — answers missed calls, books jobs and captures leads 24/7 for trades like HVAC, plumbing and roofing.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Careful with any figure here, including ours: the pricing page now leads with a missed-call ROI calculator rather than a plan table, and the only numbers our reading retrieved were that calculator's outputs (a $500 average job value producing $750 a week and $39,000 a year of 'lost revenue'), not prices. Our dated reading of the plan table gives Starter $199/mo for up to 100 AI-handled calls, Pro $499/mo for up to 500 calls with CRM integration and lead qualification, and Enterprise $999/mo for up to 2,000 calls with white-label and multi-location, with higher volume custom and a 14-day trial on every plan (30 days on Enterprise). Treat those as our record rather than as today's page.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is AI-handled calls: Starter’s 100 calls a month is roughly three a day, so a genuinely busy shop outgrows it quickly — and the steps are steep ($199 → $499 → $999). The ‘callers can’t tell it’s AI’ claim is the vendor’s own: they offer a live demo number, so test that before you commit.
tools.best_for: local service businesses — HVAC, plumbing, roofing, med spas — losing revenue to missed calls who want a 24/7 AI receptionist that books jobs straight into Google Calendar, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan or Jobber
tools.skip_if: your call volume is tiny (100 Starter calls is the whole point) or your callers expect a human — ring their live demo line first and judge the voice yourself
compare_with: Ruby is the established human-receptionist service; Lucrovox is the AI route with published per-plan pricing from $199/mo — cheaper per call at volume, so decide how much ‘human’ your callers actually need

tools.name: ManyChat
tools.what_it_does: Comment-to-DM and chat funnels for Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and SMS. Flows are button-and-script based, so an unexpected reply falls back. The free tier holds 25 active contacts and paid plans are banded by list size — $14/month at 250 contacts, $139 at 25,000.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-04, read on their own pricing page) Paid tiers are banded by active contacts: $14/mo for 250, $29/mo for 2,500, $69/mo for 7,500 and $139/mo for 25,000, each with that allowance included and per-contact billing above it, and 18-30% off on annual billing. The free tier is now 25 active contacts after the March-2026 change, with two channels and one user. Inactive contacts still count toward your band unless you remove them, so the bill tracks audience size rather than engagement — the reason a viral Reel can move you up a band. Two channels on the lower tiers, unlimited from $69.
tools.honest_knock: Flows are button-and-script based, not natural language — type something unexpected and the bot falls back. The AI add-on is closer to keyword-matching than real conversational AI, billing scales with contacts (a viral Reel can spike your bill), and support is email-only and slow.
tools.best_for: creators and brands running comment-to-DM and multi-channel (Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp) marketing funnels — its killer feature works reliably
tools.skip_if: you want true conversational AI support, or you have a fast-growing contact list — the flow logic is rigid and contact-based billing climbs fast

tools.name: MarketerHire
tools.what_it_does: Hire pre-vetted expert marketing talent on demand: growth marketers, paid ads specialists, email pros and more — matched to your business within days.
tools.pricing: Retainer-based (2026). Reported tiers roughly Starter ~$5,000/mo, Pro ~$10,000/mo, Elite ~$15,000/mo, with hour-based options too (senior talent ~$100–$200/hr, minimums ~10–20 hrs/week). A fully refundable two-week trial and free rematch if the fit is off.
tools.honest_knock: This is expert freelance talent at expert prices — the value is speed and vetting (a matched senior marketer in days, not a months-long hire), but it is a real five-figure-a-month commitment for serious engagements, not a cheap gig marketplace. Because it's talent, not software, outcomes depend on the individual and how well you brief them; the rematch guarantee helps, but you still own the strategy. Right when a great marketer would pay for themselves, wrong as a budget stopgap.
tools.best_for: companies that need a vetted senior marketer (growth, paid ads, email, more) matched quickly, without the time and risk of a full-time hire
tools.skip_if: you need cheap, task-level help (a freelance marketplace fits) or you can't yet brief and direct a senior marketer toward a clear goal
compare_with: raw freelance marketplaces are cheaper but unvetted; agencies bundle teams — MarketerHire's edge is fast, pre-vetted individual senior talent

tools.name: Marketing 360
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one marketing platform for small business. Websites, CRM, ads, email and reputation management under one roof, with a unified reporting dashboard (their 'Intelligence' analytics) that pulls every channel, lead and sale into one view — and real humans to help run it.
tools.pricing: Quote-based, not listed publicly (2026-08-15, verified on their own site). Reported core software runs around $395–$419/mo with marketing consultations, but design and custom website work are separate and can run from $2,000 into five figures, and managed ad services layer on top. We could not capture a page showing prices on 15 August 2026 — the pricing and plans routes did not resolve to one — so this review carries no pricing screenshot rather than a placeholder. Get a full written quote.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest cautions. Pricing is hidden and quote-driven, and reviewers repeatedly flag that the real cost — software plus design plus managed services — climbs well above the headline, sometimes with recurring fees for features you don't use. And it's an all-in-one "we'll do it for you" model, which is great if you want a single vendor and a human team, but it can mean less flexibility and more lock-in than assembling best-of-breed tools. Ask exactly what's included before signing.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want one vendor handling website, CRM, ads, email and reputation with real humans to help, and prefer done-for-you over DIY
tools.skip_if: you're comfortable assembling your own stack (it'll cost far less), or you need transparent, predictable pricing you can budget upfront
compare_with: HubSpot plus a freelance marketer, or a local agency
best-of-breed or agency routes — Marketing 360 bundles software and services, but compare the all-in quote against a self-assembled stack

tools.name: MeetGeek
tools.what_it_does: Meeting recorder and note-taker: transcription, summaries and searchable meeting history.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Basic is free. Pro $9.99 per user per month with 20 hours of transcription. Business $17 per user per month with unlimited transcription, aggregated analytics, exports and admin user management. Enterprise is quote-only with API and MCP access. Extra transcription hours are $0.50 each. A 14-day free trial runs on the paid tiers.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is transcription hours and Pro gives you twenty a month, which is about an hour a working day. That sounds generous until you count the meetings you would actually record — a sales rep on four calls a day passes it in the first week, and the overage is $0.50 an hour. Unlimited transcription is the real reason to be on Business at $17, so treat Pro as a plan for occasional recording rather than a cheaper version of the same thing. Worth checking before you buy: consent. A recorder that joins every meeting changes what people say in them, and that is a policy decision rather than a pricing one.
tools.best_for: people who run many external meetings and need a searchable record — the summaries earn their keep when you cannot remember which of four calls a detail came from
tools.skip_if: your meetings are internal and few, because the note-taking in your existing conferencing tool covers that; also skip Pro if you record daily, since twenty hours will not last
compare_with: the direct meeting-recorder peers — compare the transcription-hour allowance at your real meeting load, since that is the only meter that moves

tools.name: Melio
tools.what_it_does: Bill payments for small businesses by bank transfer or card, syncing with your accounting tools. The free Go plan covers five ACH transfers a month, then $0.50 each; Core is about $25/month. Card payments carry a flat 2.9%, which only pays off when you are deliberately floating cash.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) A free Go plan, $0 forever, with 5 free ACH payments a month and $0.50 for each one after that. Core is $25/mo, or $20 billed annually, with 20 free ACH a month; Boost $55/mo, or $44 annually, with 50 free ACH; Unlimited $80/mo. The detail our earlier note missed: every paid plan adds $10 a month per additional user, or $8 on annual billing, so a three-person finance team on Core is $45 a month rather than $25. Card payments carry a flat 2.9% fee and check and wire payments have their own charges. There is a 30-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: The free plan is genuinely useful for low bill volume, but the value case narrows as you scale into paid tiers — and the 2.9% card fee only makes sense when you're deliberately floating cash on a card for rewards or timing.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want to pay bills by bank transfer or card and get paid, starting free with no subscription
tools.skip_if: you already run AP through robust accounting software with bill-pay built in — a second tool adds little
compare_with: the per-seat AP platform for bigger finance teams

tools.name: MindStudio
tools.what_it_does: Visual builder for AI agents and workflows across 200+ models, with model usage passed through at provider cost and no markup. The real bill is therefore subscription plus model spend: Individual is about $20/month, and a looping agent burns provider credits until you set caps.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 on mindstudio.ai/pricing) The subscription is a floor, not the bill: every tier reads “+ usage”, so model calls are charged on top. Free is $0/month plus usage and caps you at one agent and 1,000 runs a month. Individual is $20/month plus usage, or $16/month plus usage billed yearly, and lifts both caps to unlimited agents and unlimited runs. Business is quote-based. Because the metered part is uncapped, the tier you pick says little about what you will actually pay - the run volume does.
tools.honest_knock: The no-markup model pass-through is genuinely fair — but it also means your real cost is subscription PLUS model spend, and an agent that loops or processes big documents burns provider credits invisibly until you set limits. The honest build discipline: start every agent with usage caps, and treat 'no-code' as no-code for the plumbing — the logic design and prompt quality are still entirely on you.
tools.best_for: operators and teams that want to build and deploy real AI agents and workflows visually, across many models, without engineering time
tools.skip_if: you need one simple chatbot (simpler tools exist) or deeply custom logic that ends up easier in actual code
compare_with: adjacent agent-builders — MindStudio's edge is the multi-model router and transparent model pricing; compare on the integrations you need

tools.name: Miro
tools.what_it_does: Visual collaboration platform: an infinite online whiteboard for brainstorms, diagrams, workshops and planning — with templates, voting and AI that generates diagrams and summaries, built for real-time and async teamwork.
tools.pricing: (2026) A free plan (3 editable boards workspace-wide, unlimited members, 10 AI credits/mo); Starter about $8/member/mo billed annually ($10 monthly), Business $20/member/mo annual ($25 monthly), Enterprise custom from 30 seats. Annual saves roughly 20%; Miro AI runs on monthly credit allowances per plan.
tools.honest_knock: Per-member pricing charges for every member added to the workspace, so an org-wide rollout multiplies at full headcount — and the free plan's 3-board cap is workspace-wide, not per person, so real teams outgrow it in days. Model who truly needs to edit before you buy seats.
tools.best_for: teams that think visually — brainstorms, flowcharts, retros, workshops and planning on an infinite shared canvas with strong templates and facilitation tools
tools.skip_if: your work is mostly documents or task tracking (a doc or PM tool fits better) or most of your company would only ever need to view, not edit
compare_with: FigJam wins if your designers already live in Figma, Lucidspark on diagram-heavy work; Miro wins on breadth: templates, integrations and workshop facilitation

tools.name: Mktg.ai
tools.what_it_does: Always-on AI marketing analyst: unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over your own spend data — no public pricing, demo-first.
tools.pricing: No public pricing (verified 17 Jul 2026): the pricing page returns a 404 and the site funnels everything to ‘Book a Demo’. The affiliate program pays per paid subscription, so subscriptions exist — but rates require a sales conversation. Budget accordingly.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest cautions. First, the pricing is fully hidden — no tiers, no ranges, a 404 where the pricing page should be — which for a tool that promises spend transparency is an irony worth noticing. Second, the ROI story on the homepage (‘on a $5M media budget, teams typically recover over $100K’) is the vendor’s own illustration, not an audited benchmark — ask for verified case numbers on the demo call.
tools.best_for: marketing teams with real media spend across channels who want an always-on AI analyst — unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over their own data. It layers on top of your existing platforms rather than replacing them, with setup the vendor puts at under 30 minutes
tools.skip_if: your ad spend is modest (the value scales with budget waste, and yours is small), or you want transparent self-serve pricing before a sales call
compare_with: Diginius manages PPC and e-commerce performance hands-on with published pricing; Mktg.ai sells the always-on AI-analyst layer on top of your channels — but with no public prices, you’re comparing a sticker against a sales call

tools.name: Modelize
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that generates on-model, lifestyle, studio and flat-lay product photos in bulk from your existing catalogue images, using Google's Gemini image models. Free tier is 3 one-off images; Starter $19 a month buys 100 images, Pro $49 buys 250 at up to 4K, Enterprise $99 buys 500 with extras at $0.20 each.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/modelize, listed as “Modelize: AI Product Photos”) Free plan available, then Starter $19, Pro $49 and Enterprise $99 a month. The free tier is 3 AI images once, not per month. Starter covers 100 images a month with 3 AI custom presets and 3 custom models, at standard 2K resolution and email support. Pro at $49 covers 250 images, 10 custom presets and 10 custom models, resolution up to 4K and priority support. Enterprise at $99 includes 500 images with $0.20 per additional image, unlimited custom presets and models, maximum 4K and dedicated support. On modelize.studio the same tiers are also sold annually at two months free, but only on Free, Starter and Pro — Enterprise is monthly billing only. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 5.0 from 13 App Store reviews. Developer Optify, Lyon, France; the app launched 20 April 2026 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock: The economics are flat: at roughly $0.19 to $0.20 an image on every tier, moving up the ladder buys resolution, custom presets and support, never a cheaper image. Read it that way and the pricing is honest; read it as a volume discount and you will overbuy. Two other things deserve a clear head. The output quality rides on Google's Gemini image models rather than on anything Modelize owns, so results and consistency can shift when Google ships a new version, and that is outside the vendor's control as much as yours. And the app is genuinely new — launched 20 April 2026, 13 reviews at the time of writing — so the five-star average is a small sample, not a track record. Finally, an on-model photo generated by AI shows a person who does not exist; check what your ad platforms and marketplaces require you to disclose before you build a catalogue on it.
tools.best_for: Shopify fashion, jewellery and homeware sellers who need consistent on-model, lifestyle or flat-lay imagery across a large catalogue and cannot justify a photographer per drop
tools.skip_if: you need art direction a preset cannot express, photography of the actual physical item in its real texture, or a vendor with a long public track record — this app is four months old

tools.name: Momence
tools.what_it_does: Booking and business management for class-based businesses — yoga and fitness studios, gyms, salons and schools: scheduling, memberships, payments, marketing automations and a member app in one place.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, verified on their own pricing page) Last published tiers, and we can no longer confirm them: Basic at $0/mo but with a 5% Momence fee on every transaction (plus ~4% passed to clients), Pro about $60/mo with a 2.5% fee, and Custom around $199/mo with no Momence fee — all plus standard card processing (~3.9% + $0.30 in the US). Those come from their published pricing after the 2025 restructure. On 15 August 2026 every pricing route we tried landed on a contact form asking for name, company, region and number of locations before it will discuss cost. On 19 August we looked closer, and the wording matters: the tiers are not missing from the page. Four pricing cards are rendered in full and then covered — a lead form on top and a blur filter over the cards beneath it — so the numbers exist in the page and are deliberately made unreadable until you hand over your details. We did not strip that blur, and we publish no screenshot of one. Treat the figures as last-known and get the quote in writing.
tools.honest_knock: The 'free' plan is the most expensive one once you have real volume: a 5% commission on every sale overtakes Pro's $60 flat fee around $30k/year in processed revenue. Pick your tier by volume, not by sticker.
tools.best_for: class-based businesses — studios, gyms, salons, schools — that want scheduling, memberships, payments and marketing in one system with a member app
tools.skip_if: you only need a simple calendar-booking link (a lightweight scheduler is cheaper) or you won't accept platform fees on top of card processing
compare_with: Mindbody wins on marketplace reach for fitness, Acuity on cheap simple scheduling; Momence wins on modern all-in-one value for class businesses

tools.name: monday.com
tools.what_it_does: Work management platform with boards, automations and views — plus separately-priced CRM, Dev and Service products.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own pricing page; first read 2026-08-01) Work Management: Free €0 (max 2 seats), Basic €9, Standard €12, Pro €19 per seat/month; Enterprise quote-only. Automations and integrations are capped per tier: 250 actions/month on Standard, 25,000 on Pro, 250,000 on Enterprise. API calls 1,000/day on Standard, 10,000 on Pro. monday CRM is a separate subscription (Basic €12 annual / €18 monthly, Standard €17/€25, Pro €28/€41, minimum 3 seats), and monday Dev and monday Service are separate again (Service starts at €31/seat/month).
tools.honest_knock: The seat price is not the product price. monday sells four products — Work Management, CRM, Dev and Service — each on its own subscription, and the €9 you see first is the cheapest tier of one of them. A sales team that wants the CRM pays €12 to €28 a seat on top of whatever Work Management costs, with a three-seat minimum of its own. The second number to find before you commit is the automation cap. Standard allows 250 automation actions a month across the whole account; if you are buying monday because of the automations you saw demoed, 250 is roughly one workflow running a few times a day, and the next step up is Pro at €19 a seat against Standard's €12. Free is capped at two seats and three boards, which makes it a preview rather than a plan.
tools.best_for: teams who want one visual system for projects and work, and who will actually use the automations and views that justify the per-seat price at Standard or above
