tools.skip_if: you are two or three people who need a shared list — the free tier caps at 2 seats and 3 boards, and paying per seat for views you will not use is the most common way this gets expensive; also skip it if you only want the CRM, since that is a separate subscription and worth pricing against dedicated CRMs
compare_with: the standing comparison in work management — judge on the automation cap at the tier you would actually buy, not on the headline seat price

tools.name: Moosend
tools.what_it_does: Email marketing and automation platform — drag-and-drop campaigns, automation workflows, landing pages and subscription forms, priced by contact-list size with a 30-day free trial and pay-as-you-go email credits as an alternative.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A 30-day free trial with no credit card. The Pro plan is priced by list size — at 500 contacts it is $9 a month billed monthly or $7 billed annually — and climbs along a slider that runs to 1,000,000 contacts. The billing terms are unusually granular: monthly, biannual (15% off) or annual (20% off). Instead of a subscription you can buy email credits outright with no time limit, in packs priced at $350, $500, $750 and $1,000, which suits senders whose volume is seasonal rather than steady.
tools.honest_knock: The friendly $7-9 headline is the entry rate at the smallest list size (500 contacts) — Moosend's pricing scales with your contact count, so as your list grows the monthly bill climbs with it, and the lowest rate assumes you pay a year up front. Read the comparison table before you assume Pro covers you, too: transactional emails, SSO and SAML, a dedicated IP, hosted files and an account manager are all marked as Moosend+ add-ons rather than included.
tools.best_for: small businesses and marketers who want affordable email marketing and automation with a low entry price, a real free trial and a clean drag-and-drop builder
tools.skip_if: you run a very large list where per-subscriber pricing adds up, or you only need transactional/API email — a developer-focused sender is cheaper for that
compare_with: Mailchimp is the recognized incumbent that gets pricey as your list grows; Moosend undercuts it on entry price with comparable automation — just watch how the per-subscriber tiers climb as you scale

tools.name: Motive
tools.what_it_does: Fleet management: ELD compliance, AI dash cams, vehicle tracking and driver safety scoring.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. The pricing page is a lead-capture form — a four-step email capture before any figure appears. No per-vehicle rate, no plan names with amounts, no contract length and no hardware cost is published anywhere on the page.
tools.honest_knock: A pricing page with a form where the prices should be. That is the finding, and it matters more in fleet than in software generally, because the real cost here is not a monthly rate: it is hardware per vehicle, a contract term that is usually multi-year, and an early-termination position you will not hear about until you want out. None of that is public. Before the demo call, decide your own numbers — vehicles, contract length you will accept, and what you currently pay per truck — because in a quote-only category the first number you hear is anchored to what they think you can pay, not to a rate card.
tools.best_for: fleets large enough that ELD compliance and dash-cam evidence are already costing you money, and who will negotiate a quote rather than accept the first one
tools.skip_if: you run a handful of vehicles and want to know the price before a sales call — that is not available here, and competitors in this category do publish per-vehicle rates
compare_with: the direct fleet-platform peers — all three are quote-driven, so get three quotes for the same vehicle count and contract length rather than comparing feature lists

tools.name: MRPeasy
tools.what_it_does: Cloud manufacturing ERP for small manufacturers. Plan production, track inventory and manage orders and procurement so a growing workshop runs without spreadsheets.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) Four tiers, per user per month, with a minimum of 2 users: Starter $49, Professional $69, Enterprise $99 and Unlimited $149. All plans include unlimited orders and items. The scaling rule is unusual and worth understanding: the first 10 users pay the tier rate, and from the 11th user you add flat $79 bundles of 10 users — so 11 to 20 users is the base price plus $79, 21 to 30 is plus $158, 31 to 40 plus $237, and so on. Expert support is a separate purchase, from $199 a month billed quarterly ($229 for a single month) up to $299 a month ($349 single).
tools.honest_knock: Paying ~$50 per user just so a shop-floor worker can clock in and out feels steep when they'll touch a fraction of the features. Customisation and reporting are limited, and there's no advanced demand forecasting or AI — so larger or highly complex manufacturers will outgrow it.
tools.best_for: small manufacturers, wholesalers and distributors who want dependable production planning and inventory control without a heavy ERP or a dedicated IT team
tools.skip_if: you're a large or highly complex manufacturer, or you need deep customisation, advanced analytics and forecasting — MRPeasy is built for simplicity, not complexity

tools.name: Murf
tools.what_it_does: AI voiceover generation for explainers, courses and product video. Metered in generation hours per year rather than per month: Creator is about $29/month for 24 hours a year, and every retake of a script bills again.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 in a browser; the page renders client-side and opens on annual billing, so check which column you are reading) Studio plans: Free $0 for 10 projects, 10 minutes of voice generation and one editor, with no downloads and no commercial rights. Creator $19/mo billed annually ($228 a year): 100 projects, 24 hours of voice generation a year, 1 editor, all 200+ voices, unlimited downloads and commercial rights. Business $66/mo billed annually ($792 a year): 500 projects, 96 hours of generation a year, business licence, PowerPoint integration and audio-to-text. Enterprise is custom and is where voice cloning, SSO and AI translation sit. Annual billing is advertised as saving 33%. Dub and the API are separate products with their own pricing — Murf's own homepage advertises API voice generation from $0.01 a minute, which is a different meter from the Studio hour allowances above.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is generation hours per YEAR, not per month — 24 hours sounds generous until you count retakes, and regenerating a script three times bills three times. Voice quality is genuinely strong, but the honest test for any TTS is your specific language, names and jargon: generate your hardest paragraph in the trial before subscribing, because demo voices always sound better than your edge cases.
tools.best_for: creators, trainers and product teams that need studio-quality voiceovers in many languages without booking voice actors — explainers, courses, product videos
tools.skip_if: you need real emotional acting range for premium brand work (humans still win), or your volume is tiny enough that free TTS built into your video tool suffices
compare_with: ElevenLabs leads on raw voice realism, Synthesia bundles avatar video — Murf's edge is the studio workflow and per-language breadth

tools.name: Navan
tools.what_it_does: Business travel and expense management in one. Book trips, automate expense reports and control spend with real-time visibility.
tools.pricing: Navan publishes no price list, re-verified 2026-08-17: the pricing URL is a marketing page and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount. What we can state from our dated reading is the shape: Business Travel is genuinely free to the customer, funded by travel-supplier commissions, and includes booking, policy enforcement and basic expense capture; the Expense product is free for the first 15 users and then charged per user per month (our reading put that around $15); Enterprise is custom for larger organisations. Because the travel side is commission-funded, the question to ask is not what it costs but what it steers — confirm that your negotiated rates and preferred suppliers survive the policy engine.
tools.honest_knock: 'Free' is real but has a mechanism: Navan earns commission on bookings made through its inventory, so the platform's incentive is that your travel flows through Navan — pricing on specific routes/hotels deserves an occasional spot-check against direct booking. The paid expense tier is where unified T&E gets real; the 15-free-users threshold makes the trial honest for small teams.
tools.best_for: companies that want self-serve travel booking with built-in policy control — genuinely free — and optionally unified expense management on top
tools.skip_if: your travel volume is a few trips a year (any booking site does), or you need expense-only tooling without the travel layer
compare_with: TravelPerk is the direct travel rival; Ramp attacks the expense side — Navan's edge is the free, unified travel core

tools.name: Ngram
tools.what_it_does: AI video creation for product and marketing teams. Turn docs, screenshots and recordings into polished, on-brand videos — scripted, storyboarded and produced with AI on a credit-based model, with a brand kit, captions and subtitles, AI voiceover and an AI avatar presenter. A published blog post or doc URL is a valid starting point in its own right: paste the link and it handles the research, script, storyboard, voice and style choice and the render in one sitting, with no editor in the loop, and hands back a shareable public link or an embed.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Credit-based, three published tiers plus a quote-only Enterprise, with annual billing 20% off. Free is a one-time 600-credit allocation capped at 60 seconds of premium AI generation and 720p exports. Basic is $29/mo, or $23.20/mo billed annually at $278.40 a year, with 3,000 credits a month. Premium is $59/mo, or $47.20 annually at $566.40. Ultimate is $299/mo, or $239.20 annually at $2,870.40, for maximum creation capacity. The credit allowance rather than the seat is what forces an upgrade.
tools.honest_knock:
The sticker price buys a credit allowance, not finished video, and the two are easy to confuse. Premium AI generation runs from 10 credits a second, so Basic's 3,000 credits a month come out at roughly 300 seconds — about five minutes of generated footage. Ngram says as much on the page: generation seconds measure premium AI-generated footage, not final video length, and manual editing and exports are unlimited on paid plans. So the tier you need tracks how much AI footage you generate, not how many videos you publish.

The top-up economics run the wrong way for small buyers. Extra credits cost 1,000 for $40 on Free, $20 on Basic, $15 on Premium and $10 on Ultimate — the cheapest plan pays four times per credit what the dearest one pays. Anyone topping up regularly on Basic is paying a premium for staying on the cheap tier, and should price the next tier against a month of actual top-ups rather than against the headline gap between the two.

Two smaller things before you pick. Export quality is tiered — 720p on Basic, 1080p on Premium, 4K on Ultimate — so the resolution you need may set your plan before the credits do. And image and audio generation still consume credits on Basic, going unlimited only from Premium up.
tools.best_for: product and marketing teams that want to turn docs, screenshots and recordings into polished, on-brand videos quickly and repeatably
tools.skip_if: you need bespoke, high-end studio production, or your video volume would make the per-export credit model expensive versus a flat-fee tool
compare_with: close AI-video tools — Ngram leans product/marketing clips from your own assets; compare credit economics against your real export volume

tools.name: NiceJob
tools.what_it_does: Automates asking customers for reviews and showcases them on your site. Reviews runs about $75/month and Pro around $125, plus a one-off setup fee near $199. Reporting and customisation are fairly basic, and the automation only amplifies the service you already deliver.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-07) Reviews plan about $75/mo and Pro around $125/mo (adds referrals, AI replies, booking reminders), both with a 14-day trial and a one-off setup fee near $199 (2026). No contracts.
tools.honest_knock: Reporting and customization are fairly basic and there's a setup fee on top of the monthly — it automates review collection genuinely well, but if you want deep analytics or granular control over timing and wording, it can feel restrictive. And the honest fundamental: automation only amplifies the service you actually deliver. It keeps the review stream fresh and steady (which matters — stale reviews lose trust fast, and AI search increasingly recommends businesses on review signals), but it cannot manufacture a reputation you haven't earned.
tools.best_for: local and service businesses that want reputation marketing on offense — automatically asking happy customers for reviews and showcasing them — rather than only managing damage when a bad review lands
tools.skip_if: you need deep reporting or highly customized review workflows, or your service quality isn't ready for more visibility yet — fix that first, then amplify it
compare_with: heavier, pricier reputation platforms — NiceJob wins on set-and-forget simplicity for small service businesses

tools.name: NordVPN
tools.what_it_does: Secure VPN with threat protection for business & remote teams
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 in the browser; the consumer page is geo-priced and served us euros from a Dutch address) Consumer two-year plans: Basic €3.49/mo, Complete €4.49/mo and Ultimate Pro €8.49/mo, each with three extra months, charged as €94.23, €121.23 and €229.23 for the first 27 months, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. Read the renewal line before you buy: those same plans renew at €139.08, €219.48 and €338.28 a year, so Basic goes from about €3.49 a month to about €11.59 — roughly a threefold step. The business product, NordLayer, is quoted in USD: Lite $8, Core $11 and Premium $14 per user per month with a five-user minimum and a 14-day money-back guarantee, and Core and Premium require a dedicated-IP server at +$40 a month on top. An enterprise offer starts at $6 per user per month from 200 seats.
tools.honest_knock: For a business you're really buying NordLayer, priced per user with a seat minimum. It's solid and easy, but a VPN is one layer of security, not a whole strategy — don't mistake it for endpoint protection.
tools.best_for: teams that want simple, reliable secure network access and a business VPN without heavy setup
tools.skip_if: you're a solo user chasing the cheapest personal VPN — the consumer plan, not the business tier, is what you want
compare_with: other business VPN and zero-trust access tools

tools.name: Notify Me
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app to recover lost sales on out-of-stock products: back-in-stock notifications, pre-orders and wishlists that keep customers buying instead of bouncing.
tools.pricing: (2026) A free plan to start, then Kickstart around $9.99/mo for new stores and a Standard tier around $39.90/mo, scaling by notification volume; 7-day trial and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Verify current tiers in the Shopify App Store.
tools.honest_knock: It does one job — turning out-of-stock moments into recovered sales via back-in-stock and pre-order alerts — and its value is entirely tied to how often you actually sell out. If your catalog rarely goes out of stock, you won't see much return. As with any Shopify app it's another monthly line item and another script on your storefront, so weigh it against the real revenue you're leaking to stock-outs.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores that regularly sell out of popular products and want to recover that lost demand with back-in-stock notifications, pre-orders and wishlists
tools.skip_if: you rarely run out of stock, or your store volume is too low for the recovered sales to outweigh the subscription
compare_with: Swym or Appikon Back in Stock
comparable Shopify restock-alert apps — compare on SMS costs and notification limits at your volume

tools.name: Nouswise
tools.what_it_does: AI research agent that answers only from a library you curate — your documents plus vetted sources — with reports, flashcards and audio recaps on every tier, and MCP tools, web search and a shared workspace only from Pro up. Built for knowledge-intensive and regulated organisations: SOC 1 / SOC 2 Type I/II, data in Europe or the US, and an on-premises install for confidential material. Published pricing is 0$ Starter, 19.99$/month Essential and 49.99$/month Pro with Enterprise on quote (re-verified 18 Aug 2026), but their own homepage still shows $10 and $40 for the same tiers — Nouswise says that is an animation artefact, we re-checked in a normal browser and it is not — so get the figure confirmed before you subscribe. The “100% verifiable, zero fabrication” claim is the vendor's own.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-12, read on their own pricing page; re-verified 2026-08-18) Four tiers, billed monthly: Starter at 0$/month, Essential at 19.99$/month, Pro at 49.99$/month — printed as “49,99$” with a comma on the page itself — and Enterprise, which is “Contact us for custom plan”, no figure at all. A banner offers the first 30 days of the Enterprise plan free if you book a demo now. On the 18 Aug reading the page listed monthly figures only: the Monthly / Yearly toggle advertising Yearly (-20%) that we saw on 12 Aug was no longer on the page, though Nouswise told us the same day that annual billing does exist. What you actually get per tier is capped rather than priced separately: sources 50 on Starter and 300 on Essential, unlimited above that; file size 100 MB / 300 MB / 2 GB / unlimited; audio recap 5 / 5 / 10 per day; and reports, flashcards, quizzes, mind maps, deep research, data tables, infographics and slide decks 8 / 25 / 120 per day. Projects are unlimited on every tier, and a footnote under the table explains the asterisk on those daily limits: “Limits are accumulative”. Three capabilities are not metered but simply switched off lower down: MCP tools, web search and the shared workspace carry a cross on both Starter and Essential and only appear from Pro up, so the two cheapest plans are the product without its integrations. Read the caps before the price: on the individual tiers the source limit and the per-day ceilings, not the monthly fee, are what decides whether this fits.
tools.honest_knock:
Their own site does not agree with itself about what this costs, and we have now checked that twice. The pricing page says Essential 19.99$/month and Pro 49.99$/month; the homepage, read the same day, shows a pricing block with $10.00 and $40.00. We put the gap to Nouswise, and on 18 Aug 2026 their partner manager answered that the homepage figures are a counter animation and that a normal browser with JavaScript enabled would show 19.99 and 49.99. We did exactly that check the same day — an ordinary browser, JavaScript on, waiting for the animation to settle — and the homepage still read $10.00 for Essential and $40.00 for Professional. So the gap is real, the vendor's own explanation for it did not hold, and neither page flags the other. Get the number in writing for the tier and the billing period you want before you put a card in, because there is a documented chance of paying double what a landing page just promised you.

The headline claim needs the same care. The homepage says “100% Verifiable AI Answers” and that answers are “solely drawn from the provided sources, reducing any fact fabrication to zero”. That is Nouswise describing Nouswise: nobody independent has tested it and neither have we. Grounding an answer in a curated library genuinely does cut invention, but it does not make retrieval, ranking or summarising error-free, and it cannot make an answer better than the library it came from. If your library is thin, outdated or one-sided, a confident grounded answer is still the wrong answer — with a citation attached. Two other numbers on that page, the 25% of the workweek spent searching and the 2.4 billion hours a year inside the Fortune 500, carry no source on the page at all.

Three smaller things worth knowing. The source ceilings are low for organisational use — 50 documents on Starter, 300 on Essential — and unlimited sources only start at Pro. The per-day limits on reports, flashcards and quizzes carry an asterisk explained only as “Limits are accumulative”, which tells you the allowances add up but not what happens once you reach the ceiling. And the page has visible rough edges (a feature row reading “Disvocer Sources”, the trial banner written as “first 30 days enterprise plan are free trial if you book now”), which is a fair signal about how closely the commercial pages are maintained — the kind of place a stale price hides.
tools.best_for: knowledge-heavy teams that need every answer traceable to a library they control — policy and public-sector units, compliance, legal, grants and research desks — where an unsourced answer is worse than no answer. The supporting infrastructure is aimed at exactly that reader: SOC 1 / SOC 2 Type I/II, encryption in transit and at rest, data held in Europe or the United States, dedicated data centres in a region you choose, and a full on-premises install for confidential material. The World Bank's AVA is their reference deployment, live since August 2025, and it is the clearest statement of what the product is for: if the answer is not in the curated library, it does not get made up
tools.skip_if: you want one assistant for everything — the entire design here is refusal to answer outside your library, which is the point for a compliance desk and an obstacle for everyone else. Skip it too if your procurement needs a firm number today: Enterprise is quote-only and the two published tiers appear at two different prices on two of their own pages. And check your volumes against the tier before you commit — if you have thousands of documents, or bursty weeks that would blow through 25 reports a day, the individual plans do not reach and you are into Pro or a sales conversation
compare_with: the comparison most readers will actually make, because Essential at 19.99$/month lands within pennies of Claude Pro at $20/mo (about $17 billed annually, our dossier). For that money Claude gives you Projects, where you upload your own files and ask questions over them, plus a general assistant for everything else. Nouswise deliberately gives you less: answers only from the library you curate, and no general knowledge to fall back on. That restriction is the product — it is what a compliance, policy or legal reader is buying, together with on-premises deployment, SOC 1 / SOC 2 Type I/II and data residency in a region you pick, none of which Claude Pro offers a single user. The trade runs the other way too: Claude has no 50-or-250-source ceiling and no per-day cap on reports, and it will answer the question that falls outside your documents. So the honest split is not which is better but which failure you can live with — an answer that reaches beyond your vetted sources, or no answer at all

tools.name: Nutshell
tools.what_it_does: Sales CRM with built-in email marketing for small teams. Manage your pipeline, automate follow-ups and run campaigns from one place, without enterprise complexity. Full API access is included on every plan.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Five CRM tiers on annual billing: Foundation $13, Growth $25, Pro $42, Business $59 and Enterprise $79 per user a month, with monthly billing about 15% higher (the page states the saving per tier as $6 to $10 a month per user). Unlimited contacts and full API access come with every tier, which is the unusual part — most CRMs ration one or both. Two paid extensions sit alongside: Marketing from $49 a month and Engagement from $16 per user a month.
tools.honest_knock: Full API access is included on every plan, so integrations are not the cost trap here — the add-ons are. Marketing at $49/mo and Engagement at $16/user/mo sit on top of the seat price, and email and SMS are billed by contact count and message volume, so the marketing side can outgrow the CRM itself. SSO and SQL data access are Enterprise-only.
tools.best_for: small sales teams that want a friendly CRM with unlimited contacts and full API access on every tier, including the cheapest
tools.skip_if: you need the marketing suite at scale — Marketing, Engagement, email and SMS are separate add-ons priced by volume, so price those before the seats

tools.name: Omniseo
tools.what_it_does: AI search visibility (GEO) tracking. Monitor and improve how your brand shows up in AI answers across ChatGPT, Google AI and other channels — track prompts, competitors and citations to grow AI-driven discovery.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against the vendor's own pricing page) Essentials $89/mo (4 AI channels, 50 prompts, 5 seats), Professional $349/mo (10 AI channels, 100 prompts), Enterprise from $899/mo with custom terms and volume. Annual billing is $890 and $3,490 a year respectively, which the page describes as two months free. There is a 7-day free trial with no credit card, after which the first paid month is half price — $45 instead of $89, or $175 instead of $349.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest cautions. AI search visibility (GEO) is a young, fast-moving category — tracking how you appear in ChatGPT and other AI answers is genuinely useful signal, but the metrics are far less standardized than classic SEO, and you're paying to monitor a moving target you only partly influence. And the step from Essentials to Professional is a big jump for more channels and prompts. Treat it as an early-mover intelligence tool, not a guaranteed ranking lever.
tools.best_for: brands and SEO teams that want to measure and improve how they show up in AI-generated answers (ChatGPT, Google AI and more) as AI search grows
tools.skip_if: AI-driven traffic is still negligible for your business (classic SEO tools matter more), or you need concrete ranking control rather than visibility tracking
compare_with: Profound or a classic SEO suite
other AI-visibility trackers or traditional SEO tools — Omniseo focuses on AI-answer presence; weigh how much of your traffic AI actually drives

tools.name: Oneflow
tools.what_it_does: Digital contract platform for the full lifecycle — create, negotiate, e-sign and archive interactive contracts, with AI-assisted contract features and CRM/HR/ATS integrations (HubSpot, Salesforce), from €250/month (5 users, annual billing).
tools.pricing: (2026) Starting at €250/month, billed annually, with 5 users included — and that is the entire public price list: everything beyond the starting rate goes through a book-a-demo call. A free contract-template library is available without an account.
tools.honest_knock: The entry is €250 a month on annual billing — €3,000 a year committed before you've sent your first contract — and the rest of the ladder lives in a sales conversation. If you only need documents signed, dedicated e-sign tools start at roughly a tenth of that.
tools.best_for: sales and legal teams with real contract volume who want the full lifecycle — creating, negotiating, e-signing and archiving interactive contracts — in one platform with CRM integrations
tools.skip_if: you just need signatures (a per-seat e-sign tool costs a fraction), or you cannot commit to annual billing at €250 a month
compare_with: Signeasy is the lightweight per-seat e-signing route from about $10 a month; Oneflow is the full contract-lifecycle platform at €250/month annual — pick by whether you manage contracts or just sign them

tools.name: Outgrow
tools.what_it_does: Interactive content builder for quizzes, calculators, polls and assessments. Generate and qualify leads with engaging, no-code experiences, then sync them straight into Klaviyo via OAuth for email/SMS follow-up.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Freelancer Limited $22/month, or $14 billed annually, for 5 content pieces; Freelancer Pro $45/month or $25 annually; Essentials $115/month or $95 annually with unlimited pieces and 1,000 leads a month; Business $720/month or $600 annually with 50,000 leads. Annual billing saves up to 44%. A free trial is available. Note the second tier: it is Freelancer Pro at $45/$25, not the 'Startup at $85/$55' that our earlier note carried — that plan does not appear on the page or in either of our monthly captures.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters at once: content types/layouts gate the lower tiers, and monthly LEAD limits gate the upside — a quiz that goes even mildly viral hits the 1,000-lead cap on Essentials, which is precisely when you least want friction. Interactive content genuinely converts better than static forms, but only when the calculator/quiz gives real value; a thin quiz wrapped around a lead form fools nobody.
tools.best_for: marketers who want quizzes, calculators and assessments that earn the lead by giving genuine value — with logic, integrations and templates handled
tools.skip_if: a simple form or survey does the job (Typeform-class is cheaper), or your traffic would blow through the lead caps
compare_with: adjacent interactive-content tools — Outgrow leads on calculator logic depth; compare lead-cap math at your traffic

tools.name: Ownr
tools.what_it_does: Register or incorporate your business in Canada online and manage the legal admin: sole proprietorship or incorporation in minutes, plus contracts and documents — without a lawyer for every step. Canada-only, RBC-owned. Through our partner link, readers save 15% on registration or incorporation.
tools.pricing: Sole proprietorship around $49 CAD; incorporation roughly $499 (federal) to $699 (BC), with government fees included; annual compliance about $199–599/yr. If you bank with RBC, a cashback of up to ~$300 CAD can make the registration effectively free (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Two honest limits. It's Canada-only — provincial incorporation covers Ontario, Alberta, BC and Quebec — so it's no use outside Canada. And it's built for straightforward setups: it won't handle complex share structures, multi-investor shareholder agreements, tax planning, partnerships or non-profits. For those you still want an accountant or lawyer.
tools.best_for: Canadian founders who want a straightforward sole proprietorship or single-shareholder incorporation done fast, without paying lawyer rates
tools.skip_if: you're outside Canada, or you need complex share structures, multiple investors, partnerships, non-profits or real tax and legal planning — that still needs a professional
compare_with: a corporate lawyer or DIY government registration
the pricier-but-tailored route and the cheaper-but-error-prone one

tools.name: Oyster
tools.what_it_does: Employer of record and global contractor management for hiring where you have no legal entity. EOR is $699 per employee a month, contractors $29. Two costs sit in the FAQ rather than on the price card: a refundable deposit per EOR employee, and an FX fee when payment and contract currency differ.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own pricing page) Employer of Record USD 699 per employee per month, with annual discounts available; Global Contractors free for 30 days, then USD 29 per contractor per month; People Partner Services USD 300 per hour, project-based. Creating an account is free, there is no minimum team size, and Oyster states there are no setup or onboarding fees. Two costs still carry no figure anywhere: Oyster requires a refundable deposit for EOR team members, and charges a currency-conversion fee when you pay in a currency other than the contract currency (it accepts USD, EUR, GBP and CAD). Oyster Shell, included with a Global Contractors subscription, carries aggregate misclassification protection up to USD $500,000.
tools.honest_knock: The two numbers that decide your bill are not on the price card. Oyster holds a refundable deposit per EOR employee — that is working capital out of your account before anyone is paid — and takes an FX fee whenever the payment currency differs from the contract currency, which for a genuinely global team is most of the time. Neither has a figure attached anywhere we could find, so the honest position is that $699 is the floor and the real per-employee cost depends on a deposit and a spread you have to ask for. The contractor product is a different shape and much cheaper at $29, so decide which one you actually need: misclassifying a contractor as an employee is expensive, and misclassifying the other way is what the $699 exists to prevent.
tools.best_for: companies hiring their first employees in countries where they have no legal entity, and who would otherwise spend more on local counsel and payroll setup than the monthly fee
tools.skip_if: you are hiring contractors rather than employees — that is $29 not $699 — or you already have an entity in the country, in which case you are paying for compliance you already own
compare_with: the standing EOR comparison — ask all three for the deposit amount and the FX spread, because the per-employee headline is the part they agree on

tools.name: PagePulse
tools.what_it_does: Per-page site analytics with heatmaps and AI-summarised insights. Free for one member and one page; Starter at $29/month buys one member and two pages. The tiers gate on members and tracked pages at once, and the 'unlimited traffic' promise carries a fair-use footnote.
tools.pricing: (2026) Genuinely free tier: $0 for 1 member and 1 page with unlimited traffic. Starter $29/mo (1 member, 2 pages); Growth $79/mo (2 members, 5 pages); Pro $129/mo (5 members, 10 pages); Scale $199/mo (10 members, 15 heatmaps, 1,500 AI insights/mo). Annual billing saves 20% — and note the footnote: ‘unlimited’ traffic is subject to fair use.
tools.honest_knock: The tiers gate on two axes at once — members AND tracked pages — so either one forces the upgrade: Starter buys one person just two pages, AI insights are metered per month per tier, and the ‘unlimited traffic’ promise carries a fair-use asterisk. If you run a whole content site, count your pages before you count on the price.
tools.best_for: solos and small teams who want simple per-page analytics — heatmaps, visitor behavior and AI-summarized insights — with a genuinely free single-page tier to start
tools.skip_if: you track many pages or a full content site (the per-page tiers climb fast), or you need deep, raw analytics rather than summarized insights
compare_with: Crazy Egg is the veteran heatmap suite with snapshot-based pricing; PagePulse is the newer AI-flavored take with a real free tier — both meter usage, so count your pages before choosing

tools.name: Pangram
tools.what_it_does: AI content detector. Identifies AI-generated text with a focus on minimizing false positives — used by educators, publishers and platforms to verify whether writing is human or machine, via web app and API. The vendor's Pangram 4.0 release (July 2026) claims a false-positive rate of 1 in 10,000, detection of output from the newest frontier models, resistance to "humanized" text written to evade detection, and improved boundary detection between human and AI passages. An early research preview adds AI image detection, flagging which segments of an image appear AI-generated and verifying C2PA content credentials where present.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 from Pangram's own llms.txt, which publishes the full plan list) Free: $0, no payment method, up to 2,000 words a day (twenty checks). Individual $20/mo or $15/mo billed annually ($180 a year) for up to 300,000 words a month. Professional $65/mo or $45/mo annually ($540 a year) for up to 1,500,000 words a month, plus 500 image scans and $200 of API usage included. Team $20 per seat/mo or $15 annually, from 2 seats. Developer API is prepaid pay-as-you-go from $5 to $2,000, with bulk document scans 20% cheaper than realtime. Note the billing unit changed with the model generation: realtime checks on Pangram 4 cost $0.05 per 100 words, where Pangram 3 charged $0.05 per 1,000 words — a tenfold difference that older write-ups (including ours) still quote the old side of.
tools.honest_knock: The unavoidable honest limit of every AI detector, including accurate ones: it is never infallible. It will occasionally flag genuinely human writing as AI (false positives) and miss some AI text, so it must be used as a signal, never as sole proof for high-stakes calls like academic penalties or hiring. Pangram's pitch is fewer false positives than rivals, which is real progress — but 'fewer' is not 'none'. Pair it with human judgment and the credit meter with your actual volume.
tools.best_for: educators, publishers and platforms that need a low-false-positive signal on whether text is AI-generated, at web-app or API scale
tools.skip_if: you'd use a detection score as final proof for a serious decision (no detector is safe for that), or your volume is tiny enough for the free tier
compare_with: close AI-detection peers — Pangram competes on lower false positives; compare accuracy claims and per-word credit cost for your volume

tools.name: Papaya Global
tools.what_it_does: Enterprise workforce-payments platform unifying global payroll, EOR hiring, contractor management and cross-border payments in one system — finance-first, with same-day local payouts on owned payment rails and deep ERP/HRIS integration. Premium, quote-only pricing.
tools.pricing: Demo-led and opaque — no single price is confirmable. Papaya's pricing page routes every tier to a custom quote and blocks verification, so treat any per-employee floor as unverified. Independent trackers disagree: Business.com (Feb 2026) reports EOR 'starts at $599/employee/mo'; eorHQ (Jun 2026) reports roughly $650 standard / $770 premium; other trackers list every tier as 'Custom.' No confirmable platform minimum. Per Business.com the contract is typically a two-year agreement with a rolling 90-day termination-for-convenience clause, and individual reviewers report bills running 30-50% over quote plus setup, FX and filing fees.
tools.honest_knock: Every headline price is a 'starting from' that dead-ends at 'book a demo,' and multiple reviewers report the real bill runs bigger than the sticker — 30-50% over quote, with setup, FX and filing fees surfacing after signing (reviewer reports, not universal terms). The documented contract is typically a two-year agreement with a rolling 90-day termination clause, so read the term and exit clauses closely before signing. The deeper structural knock: outside the countries where Papaya owns entities (a third-party estimate puts this near 40, and Papaya does not disclose which are owned versus partner), it delivers EOR through in-country partners — so at 15+ countries you're often one escalation removed from whoever actually runs your payroll. The recurring pain reported by clients is invoicing errors, data that doesn't sync between Papaya and the partner, missed or late payroll runs, and support that decays from a named account manager into a rotating ticket queue with no live channel.
tools.best_for: finance-led mid-market and enterprises already running legal entities in several countries — who want to consolidate fragmented multi-country payroll and cross-border payments into one platform, with real-time workforce-cost dashboards, automated GL mapping, same-day local payouts and deep ERP/HRIS integration (Workday, SAP, NetSuite, HiBob), and can absorb premium quote-only pricing for a white-glove managed service
tools.skip_if: you're a startup or SMB making a handful of hires abroad and want it fast and cheap — Papaya is finance-led enterprise tooling, so contractors are a paid add-on, EOR outside its roughly 40 owned-entity countries runs through in-country partners, onboarding is slower than Deel's, and the platform is overkill and overpriced for domestic-only or first-hire use
compare_with: Deel is HR-led and built to hire someone abroad this week — broad, fast, contractor-friendly; Papaya is finance-led and built to consolidate multi-country payroll and payments at enterprise scale. Pick by whether your buyer sits in HR or Finance

tools.name: Parim
tools.what_it_does: Workforce management for shift-heavy operations — staffing agencies, security, events — with unlimited users on every plan. Pricing starts from £47/month but every tier is quote-only: they price on functionality and the number of shifts you schedule.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) One number is published and the rest is not. The page says pricing starts from £47 per month with unlimited users on every plan, but each individual tier — Starter, Advanced, Premium — carries a 'Request Pricing' button rather than a figure. Their own explanation: they price on the functionality you need and the number of shifts you schedule each month. So the £47 is a starting point, not a plan price.
tools.honest_knock: Unlimited users sounds like the generous part, and it is — until you notice what replaces per-seat pricing: a bill that scales with shifts scheduled. For a staffing agency or an events business, shift volume is the one number that swings hardest month to month, which makes this the least predictable pricing model in the category. Before you commit, ask for the price at your busiest month rather than your average, and ask what happens when you cross a threshold.
tools.best_for: staffing agencies, security firms and event operators with large rosters of shift workers, where per-seat pricing from competitors would be punishing and the specialised modules (checkpoints, check calls, incident reporting) match the work
tools.skip_if: you have a stable team on fixed rotas, where a per-user tool with a published price will be cheaper and far easier to budget; also skip it if you need a firm number today, because you will be getting a quote
compare_with: the comparison that exposes the pricing model rather than the feature list. Deputy charges per user with published rates; Parim gives unlimited users and prices on shift volume, quote-only. For a large roster working occasional shifts Parim can win outright; for a stable team it is the more expensive and far less predictable of the two

tools.name: Passpack
tools.what_it_does: Team password manager for small businesses and MSPs. Store, share and organize credentials with zero-knowledge encryption, role-based access, MFA, device registration, full audit trails and shared team vaults — at a low per-user price.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, with a caveat) Passpack does not publish its rates in a form our capture can read, and neither our July nor our August 2026 reading retrieved an amount. Our dated reading: around $1.50 per user a month for Teams (up to 20 users) and about $4.50 per user a month for Business, billed annually, with a 28-day trial and unlimited password storage. If those hold it is genuinely cheap for teams — a fraction of the mainstream password managers — but confirm the current figure before you plan around it.
tools.honest_knock: The honest trade-off is polish. The interface feels clunky, there are no native mobile apps (on a phone you're stuck in the browser), and some users report slow support and billing hiccups. You're trading design and mobile convenience for price and solid zero-knowledge security.
tools.best_for: small-to-mid teams who want zero-knowledge encryption and shared team vaults at a rock-bottom per-user price, and don't mind a plainer interface
tools.skip_if: you need native mobile apps, a slick UI or hand-holding support — 1Password is more polished and Bitwarden's free tier is more generous
compare_with: the polished-but-pricier and the generous-free-tier rivals

tools.name: Payoneer
tools.what_it_does: Local receiving accounts for freelancers and sellers paid by international clients and marketplaces. Free to open — the cost sits in the fees: 1% on non-local currency received, 1.2–4% to withdraw to a bank in another country, whether or not currency is converted, $1.50 flat to withdraw locally, and a $29.95 annual fee waived above $6,000 received.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-16 on payoneer.com/about/pricing/, the canonical fee page their own llms.txt names) Free to open; the cost is in the fees. Receiving non-local currency 1% (minimum $1). Receiving by card up to 3.99% + $0.49. Withdrawing to a bank account in your own country and currency $1.50 flat. Withdrawing to a bank account in another country costs 1.2%-4% whether or not currency is converted — their own example is UK to Singapore, SGD to SGD. Moving funds between your own Payoneer balances 0.50%. Annual account fee $29.95, charged only if less than $6,000 arrives in any 12 consecutive months and not in the first year on paid annual plans; the physical card carries a second, separate annual fee of $29.95, and ATM withdrawals add $3.15 / €2.50 / £1.95 plus up to 1.8% (up to 3.5% with conversion). Rates vary by country and account type — confirm yours in the app before planning around them.
tools.honest_knock: The conversion and cross-currency withdrawal markups are where it quietly costs you — for pure currency conversion a specialist like Wise is often cheaper. Payoneer earns its keep on marketplace payouts and getting paid by international clients, less so as an FX tool.
tools.best_for: freelancers and sellers getting paid by international clients and marketplaces (Amazon, Upwork, Fiverr) who need local receiving accounts
tools.skip_if: your main need is cheap currency conversion — a specialist FX account usually beats Payoneer's conversion markup

tools.name: PDWare
tools.what_it_does: Resource and capacity planning for project teams. Plan who works on what, balance workloads and forecast capacity in real time so projects don't stall on people bottlenecks.
tools.pricing: Quote-based enterprise pricing (2026) — no public tiers, no self-serve trial; the entry point is a guided demo. Used by pharma/tech enterprises (Pfizer, Intel, Medtronic-class logos).
tools.honest_knock: This is genuine enterprise software with enterprise buying: opaque pricing, demo-first sales and implementation effort — appropriate for portfolio offices planning hundreds of resources, overkill below that. The honest pre-purchase question is organizational: resource-first planning only works if your PMO will actually maintain forecasts; the tool formalizes discipline, it can't create it.
tools.best_for: enterprise PMOs that plan portfolios around named-resource capacity and need feasibility answers before committing to projects
tools.skip_if: teams under ~50 people (modern PM tools with workload views suffice), or organizations without a working PMO cadence
compare_with: the portfolio-management field — Planview is the giant, Smartsheet the accessible middle; PDWare's edge is resource-first methodology depth

tools.name: Piktochart
tools.what_it_does: Infographic, report and poster maker with template libraries and AI credits — the free plan allows 2 downloads, Pro is $10 per member/month billed annually, and PDF/PowerPoint export starts at Business ($17).
tools.pricing: (2026-08-06, read in a live browser on their own pricing page, US dollar view) Free is $0, Pro is $15 per member per month billed monthly or $10 billed annually, Business is $20 monthly or $17 billed annually, and Enterprise is quote-only from 101 members. Free stops at 2 PNG downloads, 1 GB of storage, 60 AI credits and free templates only, and is capped at 1-4 members. Pro adds unlimited PNG downloads, premium templates and icons, 500 AI credits and 100 GB, and the annual rate is what the page calls 33% off. Business, 15% off annually, adds PDF and PowerPoint export on top of PNG, the Brand Kit (brand colours, fonts and logos), 1,000 AI credits and 250 GB. Enterprise adds SSO/SAML, workspace management and a dedicated account manager. Two separate tabs on the same page price other audiences: Education is $39 per member billed annually with 250 AI credits and unlimited PNG, PDF and PowerPoint downloads, and requires a valid educational email address, with Campus quote-only above 3,000 seats; a Nonprofits tab also exists, which we did not read. The page can be switched between USD, GBP, EUR, SGD, MXN and INR. No free trial is offered on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial — and the page states you can cancel anytime.
tools.honest_knock:
The ladder here is not about how much you make, it is about which file you are allowed to hand over. Pro — the tier the page marks most popular — exports PNG only. PDF and PowerPoint are Business features, which the full feature table confirms in a single row most people scroll past. So if the reason you want this is to email a PDF handout or drop slides into a deck, Pro at $10 a member a month is not a cheaper Piktochart, it is the wrong product, and your real entry price is $17 a member a month on annual billing, or $20 monthly.

The free plan reads as generous and is not. Unlimited projects, two downloads — and not two a month: the comparison table lists the number of downloads as a flat 2. That is enough to find out whether you like the editor, which is a fair trial, but it is not the working free tier some competitors in this category offer, so do not plan around it.

The third thing to price is the AI credits: 60 on Free, 500 on Pro, 1,000 on Business. Nowhere on the pricing page does it say what one credit buys, or what happens when you run out — there is no top-up price anywhere on the page. If AI generation is the reason you are buying, ask what a credit costs and what it covers before you commit to a year, because that is a meter that can decide your bill and it is not published.

One last piece of arithmetic. The annual discount is 33% on Pro but only 15% on Business, so the saving shrinks exactly at the tier most teams that need PDF or PowerPoint end up on. And if you have an educational email address the picture changes completely: Education is $39 per member for a whole year, against $120 for a year of Pro, and it includes the PDF and PowerPoint exports that Pro does not have.
tools.best_for: individuals and small teams who need infographics, data-heavy reports and posters to look designed without hiring a designer — and above all students and teachers, for whom $39 a member a year with PDF and PowerPoint export included is the best-value door on the whole page
tools.skip_if: you mainly need slides, because tools built for presentations do that better for the money; you need PDF or PowerPoint export but were budgeting for Pro, since those formats only start at Business; you were counting on a real free tier, because two downloads is a demo rather than a plan; or your AI use is heavy, since the credit allowances are capped and the page never prices a top-up
compare_with: the comparison nearly everybody actually makes, and it comes down to two questions rather than feature counts. First, check where each tool puts the file format you need, not what the headline costs: Piktochart keeps PDF and PowerPoint behind Business at $17 a member a month on annual billing, and a rival that includes your format one tier down is cheaper than its price list suggests. Second, be honest about what you are making — Piktochart is at its strongest on data-heavy infographics and reports and weaker as a general-purpose design tool, and if it is really slides you want then Beautiful.ai and Gamma are the closer peers. We have not read Canva's, Beautiful.ai's or Gamma's price lists ourselves, so verify theirs as well as ours; the Piktochart figures here were read on 2026-08-06.

tools.name: Pingtree
tools.what_it_does: AI-assisted funnel builder and lead-distribution platform — build funnels and forms by prompt, then route, track and monetise the leads across lead-gen, affiliate and media-buying campaigns.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-27, read on their own pricing page) Six tiers in two groups. Self Managed: Startup $499/month, Starter $1,250/month and Growth $2,500/month. Startup includes 500K processed leads, 500K ping requests, 1M clicks, 1GB database storage and 100K database API calls, with unlimited users on role-based access controls — core usage is included and overage is billed after month close. Starter adds full platform access (funnels, routing, reporting, partner management), one account manager for onboarding and day-to-day support, and database and user-management tools, with validation add-ons billed separately. Growth adds higher-throughput routing, larger-scale campaign operations and custom workflow support on the same core usage model. Managed Services: Full Service and Enterprise are both quote-only — 'Contact us' — covering custom volumes, SLAs, priority support, custom instances and, on Enterprise, execution and optimisation handled by Pingtree, with optional retainers for design and ad ops. A 14-day free trial runs with no credit card and no long-term contract.
tools.honest_knock: Two things about this price list will cost you money if you skim it. First, the names are back to front: Startup at $499 is the cheapest tier and Starter at $1,250 is two and a half times that, so the plan whose name sounds like the entry point is not it. Second, the $499 is a floor rather than a bill. Pingtree describes its model as usage-based and prints 'overage billed after month close' under the entry tier, so leads, ping requests, clicks and database API calls past the included allowances are charged afterwards — you find out what the month cost when the month is over. No overage rate is published on the pricing page, which means the one number you most need in order to budget is the one you have to ask for. There is a third gap worth naming. Copilot, the prompt-driven AI agent, is what the entire homepage is built around, yet the pricing page is written purely in infrastructure units — leads, requests, clicks, storage, API calls — and says nothing about AI usage limits or which tier gates which Copilot capability. Read the marketing and the pricing side by side and you cannot tell what $499 buys you of the feature you are being sold on. Pingtree's own partner manager answered that question for us in writing on 28 July 2026, and agreed the pricing page says it nowhere — the answer is in the section below on what the paid tiers actually buy. Three things he confirmed belong here rather than in a footnote. The overage rate is still not published: the vendor says the figures are being pulled internally and that he will not send a number he cannot source, so the budgeting gap above stands until a rate card exists. The trial length is printed twice, differently — the pricing page says 14 days, the app's own countdown says 15 days left — which the vendor calls his own two surfaces disagreeing; 14 is the number on the page we sourced, so plan on 14. And the paid upgrade screen asks for your card without restating the plan, the price or the billing terms; the vendor confirmed that and says it is going to product, but until it changes, note down which plan you picked before you type the number in. One disclosure that belongs on this page specifically: Pingtree pays us at two points in its funnel — when someone starts building and when someone starts the free trial — and neither of those requires a purchase. We get paid whether or not you ever spend a cent with them, which is precisely why this section is about what their pricing page does not tell you.
tools.best_for: performance marketers, lead brokers and affiliate operations that already move real lead volume and want ping-tree routing, partner management, funnels and reporting in one system instead of stitched together — the unlimited-users-with-roles policy on every self-managed tier means team size is not what pushes you up a plan
tools.skip_if: you are a solo marketer or small team still testing whether a lead-gen idea works, because $499/month plus uncapped overage is a lot of fixed cost to carry while you find out, and the included allowances at that tier are sized for volume you likely do not have yet; also skip it if your actual problem is finding or enriching leads rather than distributing them, since this is routing plumbing, not a data provider
compare_with: these two are not substitutes, and knowing that is most of the decision. Leadfeeder identifies the companies behind anonymous traffic on your own site; Pingtree routes, sells and reports on leads you already have. If your bottleneck is not knowing who visited, Pingtree does nothing about it. If your bottleneck is deciding which buyer gets which lead at what price, Leadfeeder does nothing about it. The honest comparison for Pingtree is against dedicated lead-distribution platforms rather than anything in the lead-intelligence category — and verify every current price list yourself, because Pingtree's real cost depends on overage that is not published.

tools.name: Pipedrive
tools.what_it_does: Sales-first CRM built around a visual pipeline: track deals, automate follow-ups and forecast revenue — designed for small and mid-size sales teams. A native MCP server (launched mid-2026) connects it to AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude for natural-language CRM actions.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-16, read on their own pricing page from the EU, so the amounts below are in EUR and shown VAT exclusive) Four seat-based plans: Lite, Growth, Premium and Ultimate. Billed monthly they are €24, €49, €79 and €99 per seat per month. Billed annually they drop to €14, €39, €59 and €79 per seat per month, charged as one payment of €168, €468, €708 or €948 per seat per year. The trial is 14 days with no credit card. LeadBooster, Projects, Campaigns, Web Visitors and Smart Docs are optional paid add-ons on top: Campaigns from €13.33, Projects from €16, LeadBooster and Smart Docs from €32.50, Web Visitors from €41.
tools.honest_knock: Pipedrive manages what happens after a lead enters your pipeline — it doesn't do outbound prospecting or marketing, so you'll pair it with a separate tool for that. As you scale and need sales, marketing and support data joined up, its sales-only focus starts to lean on add-ons.
tools.best_for: sales teams that want a simple, visual pipeline they can use on day one, with a separate marketing tool already in place
tools.skip_if: you want marketing automation in the same tool (HubSpot) or need built-in outbound prospecting
compare_with: the all-in-one platform with marketing built in

tools.name: Pippit
tools.what_it_does: AI marketing-content maker by CapCut — turns a product link into marketing videos, avatar presenters, talking photos and sales posters, with scheduling and multi-platform publishing. Credit-based, with a free tier that needs no card. Seedance 2.5 is now listed among its video models: clips up to 30 seconds, text timestamps to pin key moments, footage extension for longer scenes and reference inputs to steer the direction — although their own model page still describes it with "upcoming" wording (checked 4 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on their own pricing page, both billing toggles) On monthly billing Starter is €9/mo against a €15 list price, Plus €30 against €50 and Pro €155 against €255; switch to yearly and the same three tiers read €103, €308 and €1,540 per year against list prices of €171, €513 and €2,567. Pippit prices in the visitor's local currency — our read returned euros, with one Dutch billing label on an otherwise English page — so your own figures may differ by country. Credits are the real meter, not videos: 2,100 a month on Starter, 6,700 on Plus and 17,600 to 59,000 on Pro depending on which Pro step you buy. The free tier gives recurring daily credits and needs no card. Two reads on 3 August 2026 returned amounts that contradicted each other, which is why we re-checked on 5 August — read the live page before you buy rather than trusting any quote, including this one.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is credits per attempt, not per usable result — and buyer reviews centre on exactly that. Trustpilot reviewers describe generations that failed but still consumed their credits, refunds that were hard to get, and support replies measured in weeks. A tool that charges for its own failures puts the cost of unreliability on you.
tools.best_for: solo founders and small teams that want a steady stream of product-marketing videos and posters generated from a product link, without filming anything
tools.skip_if: you need dependable output on a deadline — buyer reviews describe failed generations that still consume credits, and support that answers in weeks rather than days
compare_with: the established AI marketing-video maker we also cover

tools.name: Pixel Union
tools.what_it_does: Premium Shopify themes bought once rather than by subscription: Pixel Union themes around $300–340 and Out of the Sandbox themes roughly $350–495. A theme is a starting point — the conversion lift comes from how you configure and populate it, not from the purchase.
tools.pricing: Premium Shopify themes at a one-time price — Pixel Union themes around $300–$340 and Out of the Sandbox themes (Turbo, Flex) roughly $350–$495, paid once rather than a subscription (2026). Promotional discounts appear often; verify current theme prices on their site.
tools.honest_knock: A premium theme is a strong starting point, not a finished store. The conversion lift comes from how you configure, populate and optimize it — a $350 theme on a store with weak product pages or slow images still converts weakly. Heavily customized premium themes can also be more work to keep updated and can add page weight if you switch on every feature. Buy it for the design system and speed-to-launch, not as a magic conversion switch.
tools.best_for: online retailers and larger-catalog stores that want a professionally designed, conversion-focused Shopify storefront without paying for custom development
tools.skip_if: a free or low-cost Shopify theme already covers your needs, or you have a developer building a bespoke storefront anyway
compare_with: Shopify's own free themes or a custom build
free themes are fine for simple stores; premium themes like these buy design depth and features you'd otherwise build by hand

tools.name: Planday
tools.what_it_does: Employee scheduling and time tracking for shift businesses, owned by Xero. Starter is €2.99 per user/month with a 5-user minimum; Plus is €4.99 per user plus a €25 monthly platform fee and a 10-user minimum. 30-day trial, no card.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page) Three tiers, two of them priced. Starter is €2.99 per user per month with a 5-user minimum, Plus is €4.99 per user with a 10-user minimum plus a €25.00 monthly subscription fee on top of the per-user cost, and Pro is custom-priced with a Book-a-demo button rather than a figure. The trial is 30 days and takes no credit card. Note the fee is only on Plus, so the step up is steeper than the €2 headline gap suggests.
tools.honest_knock: The €25 monthly platform fee on Plus is the line most comparisons miss. At the 10-user minimum, Plus is €49.90 in seats plus €25 flat, so €74.90 against €14.95 for five users on Starter — the jump is not from €2.99 to €4.99, it is roughly five times the bill. That fee also does not scale down, so the smaller your team, the larger a share of it you carry. Work out your real per-head cost at your actual headcount before choosing, and check which side of the line leave management and payroll integrations fall on, because those are the two features that usually force the upgrade.
tools.best_for: shift-based businesses in hospitality and retail with 10 or more staff who need leave management and payroll integration, where the flat fee spreads thin enough to disappear
tools.skip_if: you are a team of five or six who only need a rota and a clock — Starter covers that, and paying for Plus at that size means the flat fee is a third of your bill
compare_with: the closest like-for-like in shift scheduling, and the comparison hinges on Planday's €25 monthly platform fee on Plus. At ten users that fee is a third of the bill; at fifty it is noise. Work out your real per-head cost at your actual headcount on both before choosing, rather than comparing the per-seat headlines

tools.name: Plansom
tools.what_it_does: AI-assisted planning for tasks, goals and team collaboration, with a free Starter tier that keeps tasks unlimited. Pro is about $14.99/month or $149.99 a year. A smaller player next to Asana and ClickUp, with fewer integrations and a smaller ecosystem around it.
tools.pricing: Free Starter with unlimited tasks; Pro is about $14.99/mo or $149.99/yr (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's a smaller player next to Asana, ClickUp and Motion — strong value, but fewer integrations and a smaller ecosystem.
tools.best_for: solo operators and small teams that want AI-assisted planning with a genuinely free unlimited-tasks tier before the ~$15/mo Pro
tools.skip_if: your team already lives in an established PM tool — switching costs outweigh the AI-planning extras

tools.name: Plesk
tools.what_it_does: Server control panel for agencies and hosters running many sites — per-domain management, security and one-click stacks. Licensed per server from about $14–18/month for 10 domains. Domain caps drive the tier, and a roughly 26% average price rise took effect in January 2026.
tools.pricing: Per-server licenses (2026): Web Admin from about $14-18/mo (10 domains), Web Pro ~$28/mo (30 domains), Web Host ~$50/mo (unlimited domains); VPS licenses run cheaper than dedicated. Note: a ~26% average price increase took effect January 2026 across editions.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest notes. Plesk has been raising prices steadily (the 2026 round averaged ~26%), so budget for the renewal trajectory, not today's invoice — it's a recurring theme in the ecosystem since the acquisition era. And the domain caps are the real tier-driver: growing past 10 or 30 domains bumps you up a license, so count your domains including the parked ones before choosing.
tools.best_for: agencies and hosters managing multiple sites on their own servers who want a mature control panel with per-domain management, security and one-click stacks
tools.skip_if: you run one or two sites (managed hosting is simpler), or you're comfortable with free panels and the command line
compare_with: cPanel or free panels like CloudPanel
cPanel shares the same pricing-pressure story; free alternatives trade polish and ecosystem for zero license fees

tools.name: Postscript
tools.what_it_does: SMS marketing for Shopify stores: campaigns, automations and opt-in tools.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Starter is shown as $0 a month with a $49 monthly minimum spend, at $0.015 then $0.009 per SMS and $0.045 per MMS, plus carrier fees. Growth is $100 a month at $0.01 then $0.008 per SMS and $0.03 per MMS, plus carrier fees. Carrier fees are marked with an asterisk on every tier and are not quantified on the page. A free trial is offered.
tools.honest_knock: The $0 a month is not free — it carries a $49 monthly minimum spend, which means $49 is your floor whether you send anything or not. Read the tiers as what they are: a platform fee plus a per-message rate plus carrier fees that the page will not quantify. That third line matters more than it looks, because carrier fees are levied per message by the mobile networks and on a large send they are a real fraction of the bill. Before you compare this with anything, work out your monthly message volume and multiply it out on both tiers: Growth costs $100 more in platform fee but saves a fifth of a cent per message, so it pays back somewhere around 50,000 messages a month.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with a list large enough that SMS beats email on response — the per-message economics only work once volume justifies the platform fee
tools.skip_if: you are testing whether SMS works for you at all — the $49 minimum spend on the free tier means the experiment has a floor, and the carrier fees are an unknown you cannot price up front
compare_with: the direct SMS peers for ecommerce — compare total cost at your real monthly send volume, including carrier fees, not the platform fee

tools.name: Prezi
tools.what_it_does: AI presentation maker for dynamic, non-linear decks that stand out from standard slides — turn ideas into polished, interactive presentations fast.
tools.pricing: Paid plans start around $5/mo billed annually; Premium is far higher (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It exports to PDF only — no editable .pptx — and the zooming format is polarising: some audiences find it engaging, others find it disorienting.
tools.best_for: presenters who want motion and zooming-canvas storytelling that stands out from slide decks — especially for talks, pitches and teaching
tools.skip_if: your team just needs standard slides fast — conventional deck tools are quicker to learn and easier to hand off

tools.name: Pricefy
tools.what_it_does: Competitor price monitoring and dynamic repricing for e-commerce — AI product matching, price-intelligence dashboards, feed channels and autopilot repricing.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A genuinely free tier: $0 for up to 50 SKUs, 5 competitors, daily price updates and AI automatch. Paid, with yearly billing saving 25%: Starter $49/mo ($37 annually), Pro $99/mo ($74), Business $189/mo ($142) and Enterprise $499/mo ($374). Pro covers 2,000 SKUs with unlimited competitors and dynamic repricing; Business adds autopilot repricing and MAP/MSRP monitoring at 15,000 SKUs. Every plan includes AI product matching, competitor monitoring and real-time alerts — what you buy going up is SKU volume and automation, not the core.
tools.honest_knock: Credit where due: the free tier is real. But the first paid step is a cliff — $0 straight to $99 — and price updates run at most twice a day even on Enterprise, so this is rules-based repricing, not marketplace-speed. The headline prices are monthly rates; the advertised savings require annual commitment.
tools.best_for: e-commerce sellers monitoring competitor prices and repricing catalogs up to ~25,000 SKUs on rules or autopilot
tools.skip_if: you need intraday or real-time repricing at marketplace speed, or your catalog is small enough that the 50-SKU free tier is all you will ever use
compare_with: Prisync is the category veteran with similar per-SKU tiers; Pricefy undercuts on entry price and ships a real free tier — both cap update frequency, so speed-critical repricers need marketplace-native tools

tools.name: Printify
tools.what_it_does: Global print-on-demand network. Create custom products and automate your e-commerce fulfillment without holding inventory.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A free plan at $0 a month — you pay only the product base cost plus shipping per order — and Premium from $39 a month, or from $24.99 a month billed yearly, which the page states as 36% off. Premium's benefit is up to 33% off catalogue product costs (our earlier note said around 20%), plus custom branding and mentorship. Enterprise is custom. The break-even is arithmetic rather than opinion: at roughly $8.77 of fulfilment cost on a typical item, Premium pays for itself somewhere around 16-17 orders a month, and below that the free plan is genuinely the cheaper choice.
tools.honest_knock: Printify makes nothing until you sell — the Premium fee only pays off past a break-even order volume, and because it's a middleman marketplace, print quality and shipping vary by the provider you pick. Order samples first.
tools.best_for: creators and stores testing print-on-demand with no upfront cost, upgrading to Premium once volume justifies it
tools.skip_if: you sell only a handful of items a month — the free plan is right, and Premium's fee outweighs the discount

tools.name: Process Street
tools.what_it_does: Recurring work as trackable checklists and SOPs, with approvals and conditional logic. Pricing is opaque: Startup begins near $100/month for up to five members and steps up to a custom Pro tier in the $1,500/month range, with seat minimums on top.
tools.pricing: Process Street publishes no prices. Re-verified 2026-08-17: every tier on their pricing page, Startup included, shows Contact sales rather than a figure, and our monthly captures from July and August 2026 are byte-for-byte identical and contain no amount. What the page does publish are the limits: Startup is capped at 5 users and 10 guests with 5,000 Data Set records, 10 automation apps, 100 automation actions a month and a public API limited to 50 calls a month, and is described as a simplified Pro plan for startups; Pro comes with a 14-day free trial that needs no credit card. Figures quoted elsewhere — roughly $100 a month for Startup, the $1,500 range for Pro, per-member rates around $12.50 to $15 — do not come from Process Street and we could not verify any of them.
tools.honest_knock: Pricing is opaque and jumps steeply from Startup to Pro, with seat minimums that push the real cost above the headline per-member rate — you'll need a sales call to price it. Best once recurring checklists are core to how you operate.
tools.best_for: operations-driven teams that run recurring, checklist-based processes and want them tracked and auditable
tools.skip_if: you just need to write down a few SOPs — a doc or a cheaper tool captures them without the platform cost

tools.name: Proton
tools.what_it_does: Privacy-first suite from the makers of ProtonMail — encrypted mail, calendar, drive, VPN and password manager under one account, with a free tier and paid bundles.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-02, read on their own plans page, in euros — the page has a currency switch) Free: 1 GB mail plus 5 GB Drive, one address, no custom domain. Mail Plus €4.99/mo or €47.88 a year (€3.99/mo): 15 GB, 10 addresses, 1 custom domain. Proton Unlimited €12.99/mo or €119.88 a year (€9.99/mo): 500 GB, 15 extra addresses, 3 domains, and VPN, Pass and Drive included. Duo €19.99/mo or €14.99/mo annual: 2 users, 2 TB. Family €29.99/mo or €23.99/mo annual: 6 users, 3 TB. Visionary €39.99/mo or €29.99/mo annual: 6 users, 6 TB, 10 domains. Storage is shared with Drive on every tier. 30-day money-back guarantee. For a company the consumer tiers are the wrong ladder — Proton for Business is priced per user and read on their business pricing page on 18 Aug 2026: Mail Essentials €6.99/user/mo on yearly billing (€83.88/user/year) or €7.99 monthly, with 15 GB per user, 3 custom domains and 10 addresses per user; Workspace Standard €12.99 yearly (€155.88/user/year) or €14.99 monthly, with 1 TB per user, 15 domains and meetings up to 100; Workspace Premium €19.99 yearly (€239.88/user/year) or €24.99 monthly, with 3 TB per user, 20 domains, 250-participant meetings and unlimited Lumo AI. Enterprise is quote-only. Every business tier has a 14-day free trial and the same 30-day money-back guarantee.
tools.honest_knock: Storage is the axis, and the jump from Drive Plus to Unlimited is not really about storage at all: you go from 200 GB to 500 GB, but you also start paying for Mail, Calendar, Pass and VPN whether or not you wanted them. If all you need is encrypted file storage, the bundle is where the money leaks. The other thing to price honestly is the encryption itself — end-to-end encryption is the reason to be here, and it is also why per-gigabyte this costs more than the mainstream drives. That is a fair trade if privacy is the requirement, and a poor one if you just want cheap space.
tools.best_for: teams and individuals for whom encryption is an actual requirement rather than a preference — handling client material, legal or medical files, or anything where a provider being able to read your data is itself the problem
tools.skip_if: you mainly need cheap capacity or deep collaboration features, where the mainstream drives give more space and better co-editing per euro, or you would be paying for the Mail and VPN half of the bundle without using it
compare_with: the other privacy-first storage we cover — Proton's advantage is the surrounding suite and a long track record; compare on whether you want the bundle or only the drive, because that is what you are really choosing between

tools.name: Proton Drive
tools.what_it_does: End-to-end encrypted cloud storage from a Swiss provider. Free at 2–5 GB; Drive Plus about $3.99/month annual for 200 GB. Because Proton cannot read your files there is no server-side search inside documents, integrations are thinner, and losing your credentials without recovery loses the data.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 in the browser, served in euros from a Dutch address; the page has a CHF/EUR/USD switch, so check your own currency) Free 5 GB. Drive Plus 200 GB at €4.99/mo, discounted to €3.99/mo on annual billing (€47.88 a year). Proton Unlimited 500 GB with VPN, Mail, Calendar and Pass at €12.99, discounted to €9.99 (€119.88 a year). Proton Duo, 2 TB for up to 2 users, €19.99 discounted to €14.99 (€179.88 a year). Proton Family, 3 TB for up to 6 users, €29.99 discounted to €23.99. Drive Professional for teams, 1 TB per user, €9.99 discounted to €7.99 per user. Every plan carries a 30-day money-back guarantee. The headline figures are the discounted annual rates; the higher number beside each is what monthly billing costs.
tools.honest_knock: End-to-end encryption is the point and the price: because Proton can't read your files, there's no server-side search inside documents, previews and third-party integrations are more limited than Google Drive or Dropbox, and losing your credentials without recovery set up means losing data — by design. You trade convenience for the mathematical guarantee that nobody, including Proton, can look inside.
tools.best_for: privacy-conscious individuals and businesses that want genuinely end-to-end-encrypted storage from a Swiss provider, ideally as part of the wider Proton suite
tools.skip_if: your workflow lives on deep integrations, shared-drive collaboration and full-text search (mainstream clouds do that better), or you'd never set up account recovery
compare_with: Tresorit is the enterprise E2EE peer; Google Drive is the convenience default — Proton wins on suite value per euro for individuals

tools.name: PushOwl
tools.what_it_does: Shopify web-push and omnichannel marketing, now part of Brevo. One-click push lets stores re-engage shoppers who never leave an email — recovering abandoned carts and browsing sessions — then layer in email, SMS and WhatsApp on Brevo's deliverability stack. Usage-based pricing: you pay for what you send, not list size.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 in a browser; a plain fetch returns only the feature matrix, not the bundle prices) Priced per channel and then added up, which is the part worth understanding before you compare it with anything: each bundle sets a separate rate for email, web push and SMS, and the monthly figure is their sum. Basic is $0 and covers 500 emails and 500 web push notifications a month with no SMS credits. Plus is $19/month for 10,000 web push (10,000-30,000 band) and adds abandoned-cart automation.
