Power is $79/month for 25,000 up to unlimited web push, with flash-sale and browse-abandonment triggers, segmentation and custom attribution windows. Yearly billing is advertised at 10% off, and 20% on the web push side of Plus. It is Shopify-only.
tools.honest_knock: The bundles are push-first: every paid tier still caps included email at 500 a month, so 'omnichannel' email at any real volume means buying separate credits — and consumption-based pricing gets harder to predict as your sends climb. It's also Shopify-exclusive, so it becomes a dead end the day you move platforms.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores that want to win back abandoned carts and browsing sessions with one-click web push — reaching shoppers who never handed over an email — and then layer in email and SMS, starting on a free tier that genuinely does something
tools.skip_if: you're not on Shopify (it's built exclusively for it), or you need a full standalone email platform — the 500-email bundle cap means heavy senders keep paying extra per credit
compare_with: the deeper Shopify email and SMS marketing platforms — PushOwl's edge is web push and a free tier that actually works; Klaviyo goes further on email flows and segmentation but costs more as you grow

tools.name: Pylon
tools.what_it_does: B2B customer support platform built for Slack and Microsoft Teams. Manage tickets, track issues, and deliver white-glove support directly where your clients chat.
tools.pricing: (2026) Per-seat with minimums: Starter about $59/seat/mo (3-seat min ≈ $177/mo), Professional ~$89 (3-seat min), Enterprise ~$139 (7-seat min ≈ $973/mo), billed annually. AI modules are separate: AI agents from ~$100/mo scaling with volume, premium AI assistant ~+$50/seat, phone ~+$35/seat.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat sticker is the entry ticket; the AI that makes the platform sing is metered separately, so a realistic modern deployment (seats + AI agent + phone) lands well above the tier price — model your full basket. That said, its B2B-native design (Slack/Teams-first support, account-based views) is a genuine fit gap that classic ticket tools fake with workarounds.
tools.best_for: B2B SaaS teams supporting customers in shared Slack/Teams channels who want tickets, accounts and AI in one B2B-native platform
tools.skip_if: you run classic B2C email/chat support (Zendesk-class tools are cheaper at volume), or the seat minimums exceed your team
compare_with: the incumbent support suites — Pylon's edge is B2B-native Slack/Teams workflows; compare full-basket cost including AI add-ons

tools.name: Pythago
tools.what_it_does: AI analytics and ROI tracking for dropshippers — real-time ROAS optimization, product research and competitor tools across one or more Shopify stores.
tools.pricing: (2026) Cancel anytime, per-store pricing. 1 Store $59/mo; 2 Stores $49/store/mo; 3+ Stores $39/store/mo. Every tier includes full ROI/ROAS tracking, AI product research and competitor tools. The advertised “from $39/month” is the per-store rate you only reach at three or more stores.
tools.honest_knock: The $39 headline is the per-store price once you run three-plus stores — a single store is actually $59 a month. And because it is priced per store, every store you add adds a full subscription: scaling your operation scales the bill linearly, with no volume break below three stores.
tools.best_for: dropshippers running multiple Shopify stores who want real-time ROAS and ROI tracking plus AI product research in one dashboard
tools.skip_if: you run a single small store (the real entry is $59, not the $39 headline) or you are still validating a product idea with little ad spend
compare_with: Triple Whale is the established e-commerce analytics heavyweight for bigger brands; Pythago is the dropshipping-focused, per-store-priced alternative — leaner, but the per-store model adds up across a portfolio

tools.name: Qoyod
tools.what_it_does: Saudi accounting and e-invoicing platform built around ZATCA compliance, used by 25,000+ businesses. From 1,200 SAR a year (~$320) for one user and one location — but ZATCA Phase 2, the part most businesses actually need, starts on the Pro tier.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-18 in-browser on app.qoyod.com/home/select_plan_en; the marketing site returns 403 to plain fetches) Billed in Saudi riyal, which is pegged to the dollar at 3.75, so the conversion is exact rather than approximate. Annual pricing: Basic 1,200 SAR (~$320) for 1 user and 1 location covering ZATCA Phase 1, invoices, payments and credit notes; Pro 1,800 SAR (~$480) for 3 users and 3 locations, adding ZATCA Phase 2, quotations and the full procurement cycle; Advanced 2,211 SAR (~$590, shown struck through from 3,300 SAR / ~$880 under a “33% off for a 3-year term” banner) for 5 users and 5 locations with fixed-asset management, depreciation and accounting dimensions; Enterprise is quote-only with unlimited users, custom API integrations and a dedicated account manager. A free trial is offered, and the monthly toggle costs more — the site advertises “save up to 20%” on annual. Add-ons are priced per year on top: payroll 120 SAR per active employee (~$32), POS 600 SAR per user (~$160), extra system users 240 SAR each (~$64) and extra locations 480 SAR each (~$128).
tools.honest_knock: The entry tier does not do the thing the product is sold on. Qoyod's pitch is surviving Saudi e-invoicing, but Basic covers ZATCA Phase 1 only — Phase 2 is the integration phase, where invoices are cleared with the tax authority in real time, and that starts at Pro. If Phase 2 applies to you, your actual floor is 1,800 SAR and not 1,200. The second thing to price before you sign: Basic is genuinely one user and one location, and every extra seat is 240 SAR a year, which is a fifth of the whole Basic plan per person. A four-person shop on Basic pays 1,200 + 3×240 = 1,920 SAR, more than Pro costs while still sitting on Phase 1. Add a single POS user at 600 SAR and the arithmetic tips further. Work out your seat and location count first, then pick the tier — doing it the other way round is how the add-on line becomes the biggest number on the invoice.
tools.best_for: Saudi businesses that need ZATCA-compliant e-invoicing from software built for that regime rather than retrofitted to it, and who have counted their users, locations and POS terminals before choosing a tier
tools.skip_if: you operate outside Saudi Arabia — the entire value proposition is ZATCA compliance and Arabic-first accounting — or you are a single operator whose invoicing needs are met by a general tool at a fraction of the price

tools.name: Quartile
tools.what_it_does: Retail media optimisation across Amazon Sponsored Ads and Amazon DSP, Walmart, Instacart, Criteo, Google, Meta and Microsoft, sold as a platform plus a dedicated account team rather than a self-serve tool. Demo-led with no public pricing of any kind: no tiers, no entry rate, nothing on the pricing page (read 7 Aug 2026). The 41% average ROAS uplift on their homepage is the vendor's own claim.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-07, read on their own site) There is no public pricing. quartile.com/pricing serves the same page as the homepage — no tier, no rate card and no entry figure anywhere on it, and the only call to action is Request Demo. The dollar amounts the site does show are volume claims about their customer base rather than prices: over $2B in annual retail advertising spend managed and over $25B in annual managed revenue, across 5,300+ customers in more than 32 countries. Two audiences are named, Small Business and Mid-Market/Enterprise, with no rate attached to either. Budget for this one from a written quote, because nothing else exists.
tools.honest_knock:
Everything about the sales motion here is a conversation. The product is sold as a platform plus a dedicated account team, and there is no self-serve entry: the only route in is Request Demo. That carries a cost which never appears on the page — you cannot size this against your ad budget before you talk to someone, and you cannot put it next to a competitor on paper. It matters more than usual in this category, because the direct peers do publish. Our own dossiers have Teikametrics at $149 a month billed annually for up to $10K in monthly ad spend, plus 3% of spend above that (read 2026-08-01), and BidX at €495 a month for its self-service Amazon tier (read 2026-08-06). Against those two, Quartile is an unknown until you have a quote in hand.

The introductory offer runs into the same wall. New customers arriving through a referral link get 40% off their first three months, which is a real discount — but it is forty per cent of a number nobody publishes, on the first three invoices only, with the normal rate from month four. Treat it as a reason to ask for the quote, not as a saving you can put in a spreadsheet.

One more figure to handle carefully: the 41% average increase in ROAS on their homepage is Quartile's own number, measured by Quartile on Quartile's customers. Nobody independent has checked it and neither have we, so ask what the sample was and over what period before you let it weigh on the decision.
tools.best_for: brands and sellers already running paid media across several retail networks at once — Amazon Sponsored Ads and Amazon DSP, Walmart, Instacart, Criteo, Google, Meta and Microsoft — who would rather hand the whole set to one team than wire together a tool per channel. The fixed account team is the actual product here, not a support tier, and if you were going to hire an agency anyway then a platform with people attached is a fair shape for the money
tools.skip_if: you want to know what something costs before you take a sales call — nothing on this site will tell you, and two of its direct competitors will. Skip it as well if your spend sits on one marketplace and you are comfortable running the bids yourself: the multi-network reach and the account team are what you would be paying for, and neither does much for a single-channel seller with a routine that already works
compare_with: the useful comparison, because it is broadly the same job with the opposite pricing posture. Teikametrics publishes: $149 a month billed annually for up to $10K in monthly ad spend, $179 billed monthly, and above that threshold a custom base plus 3% of ad spend (our dossier, read 2026-08-01). Quartile publishes nothing at all and sells through a demo. What Quartile offers in exchange is reach and people — Instacart, Criteo, Google, Meta and Microsoft alongside Amazon and Walmart, with a fixed team on the account — where Teikametrics is Amazon and Walmart software you run yourself. Get a written quote from Quartile at your real monthly spend and hold it against the Teikametrics arithmetic at that same number; that is the only comparison here that means anything.

tools.name: QuickBooks UK
tools.what_it_does: Intuit's accounting platform for the UK market — bookkeeping, VAT and Making Tax Digital submissions, invoicing and payroll as a paid add-on. Annual plans run from £108 for sole traders to £604.80 for the five-user tier, excluding VAT, with a 30-day trial.
tools.pricing: Read in a live browser on their own UK pricing page, 31 Jul 2026, on the annual toggle and in pounds. List prices per year, all excluding VAT at 20%: Sole Trader Plus £108, Simple Start £172, Essentials £410.40 for three users and Plus £604.80 for five. At the time of reading a 90% first-year discount was running, which showed those same tiers as £10.80, £17.20, £41.04 and £60.48 — the page states plainly that the full rate returns after one year. There is a 30-day free trial. Payroll is a paid add-on rather than part of any tier.
tools.honest_knock: The 90% offer is the number to be careful with, because it is the one you will see everywhere and it is not what you will pay. Sole Trader Plus reads as £10.80 and renews at £108; Plus reads as £60.48 and renews at £604.80. That is a tenfold step in year two, on a tool you will by then have your entire bookkeeping inside — which is precisely when switching is hardest. Add 20% VAT on top of every figure, and add payroll separately if you need it. Budget from the list price and treat the discount as a one-off rebate, not as the price.
tools.best_for: UK sole traders and small businesses that need Making Tax Digital submissions handled and would rather their accountant worked in the same system they do — the accountant access on every tier is the practical reason most people land here
tools.skip_if: you are outside the UK, where this specific product and pricing do not apply, or your bookkeeping is simple enough that a spreadsheet plus your accountant's own software costs nothing extra
compare_with: the other small-business accounting tools we cover — QuickBooks' advantage in the UK is HMRC recognition for Making Tax Digital and how many accountants already work in it; compare on the renewal price rather than the first-year offer

tools.name: QuickSigner
tools.what_it_does: Legally-binding e-signatures with unlimited documents and no per-envelope caps: send a secure link and recipients sign from any device without creating an account. ISO/IEC 27001-certified, AATL signatures, valid across the US, UK and EU — a fair-priced DocuSign alternative.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against QuickSigner's own machine-readable pricing page) Personal is free: 5 documents a month, 3 signers and 1 document per request, 5 MB maximum, PDF only, with signature and stamp fields and AATL sealing. Business is $5 per user a month ($48 a year) and is where documents become unlimited — 10 signers and 3 documents per request, 10 MB, Word files, 10 saved templates, reminders and signing order. Professional is $15 per user a month ($144 a year): 50 signers and 10 documents per request, 15 MB, OTP phone verification, bulk send, teams and the eSign API. Annual billing saves 20% and paid plans carry a 14-day trial. The API has a free developer account with unlimited test requests; production costs from $0.30 per signed document and requires Professional. ISO/IEC 27001:2022-certified and AATL, legally binding in the US, UK and EU.
tools.honest_knock: A few users report occasional email-deliverability hiccups — otherwise it does exactly what it says (recipients even sign without an account) for a fraction of enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: cost-conscious teams that want certified e-signing (ISO 27001, AATL) with unlimited documents from ~$5/mo and a real free tier
tools.skip_if: you need advanced workflow features and integrations of the big suites — this wins on price, not on ecosystem depth

tools.name: QuillBot
tools.what_it_does: Paraphrasing, grammar, summarising and plagiarism checking in one box of writing utilities. The free tier caps paraphrasing at 125 words and two modes, and the advertised $4.17/month assumes a year paid up front — no month-to-month rate is published.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free: $0 — paraphrasing capped at 125 words and 2 modes. Premium is listed at $4.17/mo, billed annually. The pricing page quotes no month-to-month rate and the Team plan is an "explore" enquiry rather than a published price, so the annual commitment is the real entry point (re-verified 2026-07-22 on quillbot.com/premium).
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is deliberately narrow — 125 words per paraphrase and two of the modes — and the honest framing is that this is a box of writing utilities (paraphraser, grammar, plagiarism, AI detection) rather than somewhere you actually write, with general AI chat tools now overlapping much of it. Note the sticker too: the advertised $4.17 assumes you pay for a year up front, because no month-to-month rate is published.
tools.best_for: students, non-native writers and anyone who wants quick paraphrasing, grammar and summarizing help
tools.skip_if: you already use a general AI assistant that paraphrases and edits — QuillBot may be redundant
compare_with: Grammarly or a general AI assistant

tools.name: Quo
tools.what_it_does: Shared business numbers, texting and AI call summaries for small teams, formerly OpenPhone. About $15/user/month on annual billing, plus telecom taxes and surcharges in 16 US states. Call reliability off Wi-Fi is the recurring complaint, and there is no video conferencing.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) Starter ~$15/user/mo (annual) or $19 monthly; Business ~$23 (annual) or $33 monthly — plus telecom taxes and surcharges in 16 US states, so a 5-person team lands nearer $100/mo than the sticker (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Call reliability is the recurring complaint — G2 logs hundreds of connection and disconnection reports, and calls get shaky the moment you're off Wi-Fi. There's also no video conferencing, no 24/7 support on lower tiers, international calling costs extra, and the CRM integrations are shallow (the HubSpot app scores ~3.3/5).
tools.best_for: micro-teams of 2–5 people working mostly on Wi-Fi who want a clean, modern phone app built around a shared inbox, with AI call summaries (Sona)
tools.skip_if: you're scaling past ~10 users and need rock-solid call infrastructure, you make lots of calls off Wi-Fi, or you need video — Nextiva or RingCentral fit better
compare_with: the fuller, more reliable but pricier phone systems

tools.name: Rank Math
tools.what_it_does: WordPress SEO plugin with schema, on-page analysis and rank tracking. The free version is generous enough that many sites never need to upgrade; PRO, from about $6.99/month billed annually, earns its keep once you want rank tracking, Content AI credits or many client sites.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17; the storefront served us euros from an EU address) A genuinely capable free version, then three paid tiers whose first-year price is lower than the renewal, which is the thing to budget for. PRO €7.99 a month billed annually and renewing at €8.99 plus taxes: unlimited websites you own (client sites excluded), rank tracking for 500 keywords, Content AI and advanced schema. Business €24.99 renewing at €27.99: 100 client websites and 10,000 tracked keywords. Agency €54.99 renewing at €64.99: 500 client websites and 50,000 keywords. There is also a Rank Math + WP Rocket bundle at €11.99 renewing at €13.99. Note the personal-versus-client distinction on PRO: unlimited only applies to sites you own yourself.
tools.honest_knock: The free version is so generous that many sites never need to upgrade — PRO mainly earns its keep once you want built-in rank tracking, Content AI credits or to manage many sites. Don't pay until you hit those.
tools.best_for: WordPress site owners who want a powerful, feature-rich SEO plugin — the free version alone beats most paid rivals
tools.skip_if: your SEO needs are basic and the free version covers them — there's no rush to PRO until you need tracking or Content AI
compare_with: Yoast SEO or The SEO Framework

tools.name: Readymode
tools.what_it_does: Predictive dialler with compliance tooling and supervisor monitoring for high-volume outbound floors. Starter is $239 per license/month and iQ $299 for teams of five or more, both with free outbound minutes under a fair-use policy (prices read on their own pricing page on 17 Aug 2026, after a vendor price change effective 1 Aug 2026). Premium per seat, and predictive dialling carries real TCPA compliance responsibility.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page, after the vendor announced a price change effective 1 Aug 2026) Two published plans, priced per license per month: Starter $239 for 1+ licenses and iQ $299, which the page calls ideal for 5+ licenses. Both waive the set-up fee and the phone-number (DID) activation fee, both give free outbound minutes subject to a fair-use policy, and both charge inbound at $0.02/min. Starter includes up to 30 DIDs per license; iQ includes up to 75 and adds caller-ID reputation monitoring, assisted remediation, call cadencing, Autopilot and unlimited integrations, none of which Starter has. Implementation and training are included from 3 licenses. One complimentary Admin license comes with every plan, and the page is explicit that it is not an agent license — no floor plan, no web phone. Voicemail Drop is available only to those who qualify and costs extra per drop. The older $199/$249 pair, and the ~$200 admin fee for sharing a license, are withdrawn: neither appears on the page today.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat price is premium, and the model rewards scale — the predictive dialer, compliance tools and supervisor monitoring earn their keep on a 5-plus-agent floor, but for one or two reps it's expensive for what a lighter dialer would do. Predictive dialing also carries compliance responsibility (TCPA and similar): the speed is only an asset if your calling practices stay compliant. For high-volume outbound teams, it's a genuine efficiency engine.
tools.best_for: high-volume outbound call teams (insurance, real estate, collections) with 5+ agents that need predictive dialing, compliance tools and supervisor monitoring
tools.skip_if: you're a one- or two-rep operation (a simpler, cheaper dialer fits) or your outreach doesn't justify predictive-dialer speed and its compliance overhead
compare_with: other dialer/contact-center platforms — Readymode targets high-volume outbound; compare per-seat cost and compliance features at your team size

tools.name: Reclaim.ai
tools.what_it_does: Auto-schedules tasks, habits and meetings around your stated priorities. Google Calendar-first, so Outlook-heavy teams are out, and the free tier is limited. Paid seats run about $8–10/month on Starter and Plus, roughly 29% cheaper on annual billing.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Free forever with limits; Starter $10 per seat a month and Business above it, with Enterprise custom and yearly billing saving 20%. The mechanism most reviews miss is Attendee Units: AUs are attendees without a paid Reclaim seat in Smart Meetings of 3 or more people (two-person meetings do not need them), and they accumulate. Extra AUs are bought in packs on top of the seat — on Starter, $8/month for 3, $16 for 6, $24 for 9 and $32 for 12; on Business, $12 for 6, $24 for 12, $36 for 18 and $48 for 24; Enterprise packs run $18 for 10 and $36 for 20. If you schedule across people who do not have seats, the AU packs rather than the seat price are what determines your bill. Discount codes appear on the page periodically.
tools.honest_knock: The magic only works if your team lives in Google Calendar — it's Google-first, so Outlook-heavy shops are out, and the free tier is quite limited. A genuine time-saver for the right setup, useless for the wrong one.
tools.best_for: Google Calendar teams that want AI to auto-schedule tasks, habits and meetings around their priorities
tools.skip_if: you're on Outlook or don't overbook your calendar — the auto-scheduling has little to optimize

tools.name: Reditus
tools.what_it_does: Affiliate-program software plus marketplace for B2B SaaS: launch, manage and scale a partner program with tracking, automated payouts and affiliate discovery.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) 14-day free trial, no credit card. The published entry plan is Growth at $99/mo billed annually ($1,188 once a year, which the page presents as 34% off and four months free) covering up to $60K of tracked ARR; the tier above covers up to $360K ARR, and larger plans and Enterprise sit above that, annual-only. Payout processing is charged on top on every plan at 5% for card and 2% for invoice. Note the tier names have shifted since our earlier reading, so match on the ARR ceiling rather than on the plan name.
tools.honest_knock: The advertised $99 is the annual-commitment rate — month-to-month is $149. The affiliate-marketplace listing, often the very reason teams pick Reditus, only unlocks at Scale Up: $4,788 per year, annual-only. And payout processing fees of 5% (card) or 2% (invoice) sit on top of every plan.
tools.best_for: B2B SaaS teams with a product-led motion that want to launch an affiliate program and tap an affiliate-discovery network, and are comfortable committing annually
tools.skip_if: you are pre-product-market-fit, need month-to-month flexibility on a small budget, or expected marketplace exposure on the entry tiers
compare_with: PartnerStack is the bigger, enterprise-depth network; Reditus is leaner and cheaper to start, but its marketplace exposure gates behind the annual-only Scale Up tier

tools.name: Remote People
tools.what_it_does: Employer of Record and global hiring in 150+ countries. EOR from $199 per employee a month with no setup fee, no deposit and no minimum headcount; contractor management from $29, US PEO from $99. Recruitment is charged separately at 20-25% of annual salary.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-07, read on their own pricing page) Priced per service rather than per plan, and every figure is a floor. Employer of Record: EOR Flex from $199 per employee a month, billed monthly with no commitment, no setup fee and no minimum headcount; EOR Plus from $399 with an annual commitment, a dedicated account manager and a minimum of 5 employees. Contractor of Record from $199 a month including misclassification cover; plain contractor management from $29. US PEO from $99 per employee a month and US payroll from $29. Global payroll from $25 per employee a month, with volume discounts quoted above 50 employees. Recruitment is charged on salary instead: Recruit + EOR is 2% of annual salary spread over twelve months, Global Recruitment 20% payable on the candidate’s first day, and Executive Search 25%. Legal help is $199 an hour with no retainer. Benefits, equity, incorporation, entity management and visas are all quote-only.
tools.honest_knock:
The monthly rates are the cheapest we have on file for this category, and that is worth saying plainly — our Deel dossier has EOR from $599 per employee a month against Remote People’s $199, contractor of record $325 against $199, US PEO $125 against $99 and contractor management $49 against $29. If those hold at your headcount and in your country, the gap is large enough to matter.

Two things stop that from being the whole picture. First, every figure on the page carries a ‘from’ and not one country-level rate is published. EOR pricing moves with statutory employer cost, which varies enormously between, say, Portugal and Brazil, so the number you are quoted for your actual hire is the only one that counts. Ask for it in writing before you compare anything.

Second, and larger: the recruitment services are priced as a share of salary, and that dwarfs the subscription. Global Recruitment at 20% of annual salary on an $80,000 hire is $16,000 due on day one — more than six years of EOR Flex for the same person. Executive Search at 25% is more again. Recruit + EOR at 2% over twelve months is a different animal entirely and is the one worth understanding, because it is the only route where the fee is spread rather than paid up front. Nothing on the pricing page puts these side by side, so it is easy to read the $199 and miss where the money actually goes.

One structural note: EOR Plus needs a minimum of five employees and an annual commitment, so a small team comparing tiers is really only choosing Flex.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size teams hiring a handful of people abroad who want to pay monthly, keep the option to stop, and not carry a five-employee minimum. EOR Flex is genuinely unusual on those terms: no setup fee, no deposit, no minimum headcount and no commitment, at a third of the EOR floor we have on file for Deel. The $29 contractor tier is a reasonable entry too if all you need is compliant contracts and payment in 120+ currencies.
tools.skip_if: your hiring runs through their recruitment desk rather than your own, because at 20 to 25% of annual salary that fee decides the total cost and the monthly rate becomes a rounding error. Skip it as well if you need a firm budget before committing: with no country-level rates published, a like-for-like comparison against another provider is not possible from public information — you have to get quotes from both. And if you are already at scale with a dedicated account manager elsewhere, the Flex tier is not aimed at you and Plus removes much of the flexibility that makes Flex interesting.
compare_with: the comparison worth doing, and our Deel dossier makes it checkable. On published floors: EOR $199 against $599 a month, contractor of record $199 against $325, US PEO $99 against $125, contractor management $29 against $49. Remote People is cheaper on every line we can compare. What Deel has is scale and a product surface that goes well beyond employment — and, in fairness, both are demo-led at the point where it matters, so neither publishes what your particular hire will actually cost. Get a written quote from both for the same country and the same salary; that is the only comparison that survives contact with reality. Our Remote People figures were read on 2026-08-07, the Deel figures are dated in that dossier.

tools.name: Replit
tools.what_it_does: Browser-based coding environment with instant deploys and an AI agent. Billing is effort-based: Core is $20/month including $25 of credits, Pro $95/month billed annually including $100. Credits expire monthly and a complex agent session burns them fast, which makes production costs hard to budget.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 on their own pricing page) Starter is free, with daily Agent credits, a built-in database and the slides/video/animation tools. Core is $25/month, or $20/month billed annually (Replit advertises 20% off), and includes $25 of monthly credits, up to 5 collaborators and up to 2 agents working in parallel. Pro is $100/month, or $95/month billed annually, and includes $100 of monthly credits, up to 15 collaborators and up to 50 viewers. Enterprise is separate. The number to watch is not the seat but the credits: since Replit moved to effort-based pricing the Agent decides how much work a request is worth, so the monthly credit allowance is a starting balance rather than a budget.
tools.honest_knock: The credit model on AI-heavy building is unpredictable — a complex agent session can burn credits fast, and they expire monthly, so heavy AI users hit surprise costs. Great for learning and prototyping; watch the meter for production work.
tools.best_for: developers, learners and tinkerers who want a zero-setup, browser-based coding environment with AI assistance
tools.skip_if: you need a stable, cost-predictable production environment — the expiring-credit model makes AI-heavy usage hard to budget
compare_with: GitHub Codespaces or a local IDE

tools.name: Reply.io
tools.what_it_does: AI-driven sales engagement platform. Automate your cold outreach across email, LinkedIn, and calls while keeping the human touch. Now includes a mobile app (Jason AI) for iOS and Android to run outreach on the go.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 against Reply's own machine-readable plan breakdown) Three separate tracks, and the one you pick changes the arithmetic completely. Email Volume is pay-as-you-go by active contacts: 1,000 for $49/mo, 2,000 for $59, 3,000 for $69, 5,000 for $89, 10,000 for $159, 25,000 for $259 and 50,000 for $459, with 100,000+ quoted. Multichannel is all-inclusive from $89/month billed annually ($99 monthly) with unlimited active contacts, adding LinkedIn, SMS, calls and WhatsApp, 10 mailboxes (5 on monthly) and 50 live data credits. AI SDR (Jason) runs $500 to $1,000 a month billed annually at Starter (1,000-3,000 contacts) and $1,500 to $3,000 at Growth (5,000-10,000), with Enterprise quoted. Agency Core starts at $210/month and Agency AI SDR at $500 per client. Add-ons on top of the Email track: LinkedIn automation $69/month per account, calls and SMS $29/month per account, AI/live-data credits from $39/month and email validation from $20/month.
tools.honest_knock: The advertised $89 is the lobby, not the building: use LinkedIn and calling — the whole point of multichannel — and the real per-seat price roughly doubles. Budget 1.5-2x the sticker, plus sending infrastructure (domains, warmup) that any cold-outreach stack needs. The platform is genuinely capable; the pricing just rewards reading this paragraph before the demo call.
tools.best_for: sales teams running structured multichannel outbound (email + LinkedIn + calls) who want sequences, warmup and a B2B database in one platform
tools.skip_if: you only send plain email sequences (cheaper single-channel tools exist), or your list is too small to justify per-seat-plus-add-ons math
compare_with: Instantly is cheaper email-first, Apollo bundles a bigger database — Reply's edge is mature multichannel sequencing; compare real per-seat totals

tools.name: respond.io
tools.what_it_does: Shared inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS, email and live chat, with workflow automation, broadcasts and AI agents on top. Priced per monthly active contact rather than per seat: $79 Starter, $159 Growth and $279 Advanced, around 20% off paid yearly, with a 7-day trial and no card. The catch is where the line sits: automation, broadcasts, AI agents and the API all start at Growth, so the entry plan is the inbox without the engine (read 13 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026-08-13, read off respond.io/pricing) Four tiers, billed on monthly active contacts rather than seats: Starter $79/month, Growth $159, Advanced $279, and Enterprise on quote. Paying yearly takes roughly 20% off — $948, $1,908 and $3,348 a year against $1,188, $2,388 and $4,188 monthly. The trial is 7 days and takes no card. What separates the tiers is not volume but capability, and the line matters: Starter buys team and custom inboxes, the mobile app, AI Prompt, AI Assist, basic reports and 2FA. **Workflows automation, broadcasts, AI Agents, advanced reports, the developer API and the Zapier and Make integrations all start at Growth.** Advanced adds multiple workspaces, SSO, webhooks, HTTP requests in workflows and phone-number masking, and although a figure is shown its button says “Talk to Sales”. One thing we could not pin down: the page carries a selector for 1,000 / 2,500 / 5,000 / 10,000 / more than 10,000 monthly active contacts under the heading “pay only for the contacts you talk to”, but the prices we read did not move between those settings. Ask what your contact volume actually costs before you sign — that is the meter you are buying.
tools.honest_knock: The entry plan is the inbox without the engine. At $79 you get shared inboxes across WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, SMS and live chat, and that alone solves the “five people answering from one phone” problem. But workflow automation, broadcasts, AI Agents and the API — the things most people picture when they read “omnichannel platform” — begin at $159, so the real entry price for an automated setup is double the headline. Work out which side of that line you sit on before comparing it with anything else. And note the meter: you pay per active contact per month, so cost follows how many people message you, not how many staff you add. That is kinder than per-seat pricing for a small team fielding a lot of chats, and harsher if you have a big list you talk to often.
tools.best_for: a small team that already lives in WhatsApp and Instagram DMs and has outgrown a shared phone — retail, clinics, travel, local services. Per-contact pricing suits you if headcount grows faster than conversation volume, and the seven-day trial without a card lets you check that before committing
tools.skip_if: you only need one channel: a plain shared inbox or a helpdesk will cost less than an omnichannel platform you use a fifth of. Skip the Starter plan specifically if automation is the reason you are looking — you will be on Growth within a month. And if your monthly active contacts run into the tens of thousands, get the number in writing first, because that is the meter and the published ladder stops being informative
compare_with: the comparison most WhatsApp-first teams will make, and one we have already researched. Both put a shared team inbox on top of the WhatsApp Business API; the practical difference is how the meter runs and where automation starts. respond.io reaches wider across channels — Instagram, Messenger, SMS, live chat and email in the same inbox — which is worth paying for only if you genuinely answer on more than one

tools.name: Restream
tools.what_it_does: Multistreaming studio: broadcast one show to YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook and Twitch at once from the browser, with guests and local recordings. The channel caps are the business model — 3 on Standard at about $16/month annual, 5 on Professional — and each extra teammate is a $25/month seat.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against restream.io) (2026) A free plan (multistream to 2 channels, with Restream branding); Standard about $16/mo billed annually ($19 monthly, 3 channels), Professional $39/mo annual ($49 monthly, 5 channels, Full HD), Business around $199/mo annual (up to 8 channels). Extra team seats cost about $25/seat/mo on every paid tier.
tools.honest_knock: The channel caps are the business model — each tier buys a few more destinations, and every extra teammate is a separate $25/mo seat on top of the plan. Price it at your real destination count and team size, not the sticker.
tools.best_for: creators, podcasters and marketing teams who broadcast one show to many platforms at once, without extra encoding hardware
tools.skip_if: you stream to a single platform (its native studio is free) or you need broadcast-grade production control — an OBS-style tool fits better
compare_with: StreamYard wins on beginner-friendly guest shows, OBS on free pro-grade control; Restream wins on multistream breadth and scheduling

tools.name: Retouch4me
tools.what_it_does: AI retouching plugins for photographers (Photoshop-compatible, Mac/Windows) — lifetime licenses per plugin (Heal/Crop $145, Dodge&Burn $179), full-suite subscriptions from $169/year with retouch credits, or pay-as-you-go cloud retouching at $0.10/photo. Free to try first: signing up gives 20 cloud retouches at no cost (site, verified 23 Jul 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026, all verified on their /pricing page) Three ways to pay. (1) Lifetime plugin licenses, one-time per plugin: Heal and Crop $145 each, Dodge&Burn and Clean Backdrop $179 each — a July 2026 'high season sale' showed 30% off ($101.50/$125.30), time-boxed, not the list price. (2) Subscriptions that include the full plugin set plus a yearly retouch-credit allowance (1 photo = 1 retouch; unused credits roll over up to 5 years while the subscription stays active): Start $20/mo, Pro $35/mo, Business $90/mo list — billed yearly at a 'limited offer' $169/$299/$759 when we checked — with 2,400/6,000/18,000 retouching credits a year, culling credits and 20/40/100 GB MyShot storage, 14-day money-back. (3) Pay-as-you-go cloud retouching at $0.10 per photo. Free: Frequency Separation and Color Match Free, plus a sign-up trial of 20 cloud retouches at no cost (site, re-verified 23 Jul 2026).
tools.honest_knock: Work out which lane you are in before you pay, because the three lanes price the same photo very differently. One plugin forever at $145 is honest value — but a working portrait stack means four or five plugins at $145–$179 each, over $600, while the Start subscription hands you the entire plugin set for $169 a year with 2,400 retouches included. The catch cuts the other way too: own-forever versus keep-paying is the real decision, since the credits' 5-year rollover only holds 'while the subscription is active' — stop paying and the suite and stockpile are gone. Low volume? Price the $0.10-per-photo route first: 100 photos a month is $10.
tools.best_for: high-volume portrait, school and wedding photographers who already live in Photoshop and want repetitive retouching (skin, stray hairs, dust, teeth) automated — owning the plugins outright or renting the whole suite on credits, whichever their volume favours
tools.skip_if: occasional editors — the free tools plus $0.10/photo pay-as-you-go cover light use; or anyone unwilling to do the three-lane maths, because picking the wrong lane here easily doubles what the same workflow costs
compare_with: the credit-based AI retouching desktop app — Evoto bundles everything in one interface paid per export credit, Retouch4me offers lifetime plugins, a credit subscription or pay-per-photo; high volume favours owning the plugins, low volume favours credits. Verify both current price lists yourself.

tools.name: Riverside
tools.what_it_does: Records podcasts and video locally at each end, so guests on poor connections still come out broadcast-quality. The meter is separate-track recording time: Pro is $29/month for 15 hours, and hitting the cap stops new separate-track downloads until the next cycle rather than billing you more.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Free $0: one 2-hour recording, 720p, single track, 44.1 kHz. Pro $29/month ($24 billed annually): 15 hours a month of separate tracks, up to 4K, 48 kHz, 1 studio. Grow $39/month ($34 annually): 20 hours, 2 studios. Webinar $99/month ($79 annually): 25 hours, 3 studios. Business is quote-only with unlimited hours. Pro and Grow include 20 AI credits, Business starts at 60; more are bought separately.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is not recording time, it is separate-track recording time — and separate tracks are the entire reason to use this rather than a video call. Their own wording on hitting the cap: you can still reach your content but cannot download new separate tracks until the next billing cycle or you upgrade. So a busy interview month does not cost you more money, it quietly stops you delivering, which is worse. Fifteen hours on Pro is about seven or eight hour-long interviews once you count retakes and the recording that runs while you set up. The free tier is a demonstration rather than a plan: one 2-hour session, 720p, single track.
tools.best_for: podcasters and interviewers who need broadcast-quality audio and video from guests on bad connections — local recording at each end is genuinely the thing that solves it
tools.skip_if: you record alone, or your guests are always in the room with you, because then a local recorder does the same job once; also skip Pro if you interview more than about eight hours a month, since the track cap is what will stop you
compare_with: the direct local-recording peers — compare the monthly hour allowance for separate tracks, not the headline price

tools.name: Ruby
tools.what_it_does: Live human receptionists answering your calls, plus chat. Billed by receptionist-minute: $250/month for 50 minutes and $395 for 100, rising to $1,725 for 500, with chat bundled from $115/month. Premium rates that pay off only when a missed call is a lost client.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-13, read on their own plans-and-pricing page) Live virtual receptionists billed on included receptionist-minutes: $250/mo for 50 minutes, $395/mo for 100, $720/mo for 200 and $1,725/mo for 500, with larger volumes quoted on request. Standalone live chat is $143/mo for 10 chats, $335/mo for 30 and $520/mo for 50; bundled with a receptionist plan those same volumes cost $115, $268 and $416/mo. No free tier and no annual-billing discount. Ruby states there are no activation, onboarding, setup or customization fees.
tools.honest_knock: You're paying premium rates for real human receptionists billed per minute — worth it when a missed call is a lost client, but expensive if your call volume is low or an AI answering service would do the job for a fraction.
tools.best_for: client-driven service businesses (law, home services, clinics) where a live human answering every call directly wins business
tools.skip_if: your call volume is low or mostly routine — an AI answering service or a solid voicemail-to-text setup costs far less

tools.name: Runpod
tools.what_it_does: Serverless GPU compute platform. Rent high-end NVIDIA GPUs by the hour to train and deploy your own machine learning models.
tools.pricing: Pay-per-use GPU cloud (re-verified 2026-07-22 against runpod.io/pricing, Secure Cloud rates): on-demand pods run from $0.27/hr (RTX A5000) and $0.39/hr (L4) up to $2.89/hr for an H100 PCIe, $2.99/hr H100 SXM, $4.39/hr H200 and $7.39/hr B300. Serverless bills per second at a premium over pods in exchange for sub-200ms cold starts and autoscaling: $0.58/hr for the 16GB tier, $2.72/hr for an A100, $4.55/hr for an 80GB H100. Multi-node Clusters start at $1.79/hr per A100 SXM; H100 SXM, L40S and B200 clusters plus all reserved capacity are quote-only.
tools.honest_knock: The honest math is utilization: on the same card serverless runs roughly 1.6-2x the pod rate per compute-hour ($4.55 vs $2.89 for an H100, $2.72 vs $1.39 for an A100 PCIe), which is brilliant for spiky inference and wasteful for steady training — pick the mode per workload, not per habit. And like all GPU clouds, the meter never sleeps: an idle pod you forgot is the cloud version of the subscription graveyard. Set spend alerts before the first experiment, not after the first invoice.
tools.best_for: developers and ML teams that want cheap, per-second GPU compute for inference and experiments without committing to hyperscaler contracts
tools.skip_if: you need enterprise SLAs, compliance guarantees and managed everything (hyperscalers exist for that), or your workload is steady enough that owned/reserved hardware wins
compare_with: close GPU-cloud rivals — compare per-GPU-hour on the exact card you need and whether serverless cold-start speed matters for your workload

tools.name: Salesflare
tools.what_it_does: CRM for small B2B teams that auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar. $29–99/user/month with no caps on contacts or pipelines. Deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and basic reporting unless you export.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against salesflare.com) $29–99/user/mo (Growth ~$29–39, Pro ~$49); 30-day free trial, no card, no onboarding fees and no caps on contacts or pipelines (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and reporting feels basic unless you export. Integrations cover the essentials (Gmail, Outlook, Zapier) but niche tools lean on Zapier — and at higher seat counts the price overlaps fuller CRMs.
tools.best_for: small B2B teams whose reps hate data entry — Salesflare auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar
tools.skip_if: you need deep customisation, a big integration marketplace, or built-in calling and invoicing — Pipedrive or a fuller CRM fit better
compare_with: the more customisable, bigger-integration pipeline CRM

tools.name: Salesflow
tools.what_it_does: LinkedIn outreach automation for outbound sales teams — connection requests, follow-up sequences and Open InMails, with email steps for multichannel campaigns, plus admin panel, seat management and shared templates for agencies. Priced per seat, from about $79 per user per month billed annually.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-02) Their own pricing page returns a 403 to us, so these figures come from independent reviews read on 2 August 2026 rather than from Salesflow directly — verify on their site before you buy. Single User is reported at $99 per user per month, or $79 per user per month billed annually, plus VAT where it applies, including 400 LinkedIn invites, up to 2,000 follow-up messages and 800 Open InMails a month. Team tiers are reported as Starter from $70 per seat at 5+ seats, Pro from $39.95 per seat at 20+ seats and Agency from $29.98 per seat at 50+ seats, with discounts of 15% at six months and 30% at twelve.
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat price falls steeply with team size — roughly $79 alone against $29.98 at fifty seats — so a solo operator pays two to three times what an agency pays per seat for the same product. And the monthly quotas are the real ceiling: 400 invites and 800 Open InMails is a fixed budget, not a starting point.
tools.best_for: outbound sales teams and agencies running LinkedIn sequences across several seats, where the per-seat price drops and the admin panel earns its keep
tools.skip_if: you are one person sending a handful of connection requests a week — the quotas are far above what you need and the seat price is at its highest

tools.name: Salesmessage
tools.what_it_does: Business texting and SMS marketing in one shared inbox. Reach customers where they actually reply — two-way texting, automation and team collaboration.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-08, re-verified on their own pricing page) Repackaged since our last check into two named plans plus Enterprise, metered in message credits. Monthly billing: Basic is $25 a month for 500 credits a month; Pro is $329 a month for 10,000 credits a month; Enterprise is contact-for-pricing with custom credits. Both plans carry a credits dropdown that raises the allowance for a fixed add-on: on Basic, 1,000 credits is +$24, 2,500 is +$74, 5,000 is +$154 and 7,500 is +$224 a month; on Pro the ladder runs from 15,000 credits at +$150 up to 50,000 at +$1,170 a month, in 5,000-credit steps. Annual billing is shown as two months free: Basic $21 a month billed yearly for 6,000 credits a year (12,000 credits +$252, 30,000 +$756, 60,000 +$1,560, 90,000 +$2,268) and Pro $277 a month billed yearly for 120,000 credits a year (180,000 +$1,512, rising to 600,000 at +$11,796). Seats and numbers are priced apart from the plan: the first seat is free and each additional seat is $10.00 a month or $100.00 a year; the first number is free and each additional number is $5.00 a month or $50.00 a year. The page defines the meter itself: SMS is 1 credit per 160 characters, MMS is 2 credits, calling is 1 credit a minute and call forwarding is 2 credits a minute. A 14-day free trial runs, and a 30-day money-back guarantee is offered, refunded less the message credits used. The page no longer publishes a per-credit overage rate, nor terms for taxes, carrier fees or country availability, so we quote none.
tools.honest_knock: Two things changed here and both cost money. First, calling now runs on the same meter as texting — 1 credit a minute, 2 a minute when forwarding — so voice minutes eat the allowance you budgeted for messages. Second, the plan ladder is a canyon: $25 to $329 a month with nothing between them, and the credits dropdown raises your allowance without adding a single seat. Size the credits, not the headcount. An MMS is 2 credits, so one picture message to 1,000 contacts is 2,000 credits — four times the entire monthly allowance on Basic. Seats and numbers bill on top of every plan beyond the first of each: a five-person team on one number is $40 a month over the sticker, and the annual headline of $21 and $277 is a per-month display of a bill charged yearly. Note what the page has stopped saying since our previous check: there is no published per-credit overage rate anymore, so what happens when you run out mid-cycle is not stated where you buy — ask before you commit. And US business texting carries a regulatory layer of its own: 10DLC registration and carrier surcharges bill separately from anything quoted here, and opt-in and opt-out handling stays your legal responsibility — the platform enables compliance, it does not absolve you.
tools.best_for: sales and service teams that want two-way texting and calling in one CRM-linked inbox, and can estimate their monthly credit burn — messages plus call minutes — before they sign
tools.skip_if: your audience doesn't respond to SMS, or your volume is low enough that the fixed 10DLC overhead outweighs the sending; also skip it if you need a lot of seats cheaply, or if your real usage lands in the gap between the $25 and $329 plans, since the only bridge on offer is a bigger credit bundle on the small plan
compare_with: the business-SMS peer group — compare credits-per-dollar AND what the meter counts, now that call minutes draw on the same balance; the sticker rows look more alike than the invoices

tools.name: SaneBox
tools.what_it_does: Email triage that moves low-priority mail out of the inbox and works with any provider. From $4.54/month for one account on a two-year commitment — $9.49 month to month — up to $22.04 for four accounts with every feature. The honest catch: you are paying monthly to filter mail that modern email clients increasingly sort for free.
tools.pricing: (read in a live browser on their own pricing page, 18 Aug 2026 — the figures are rendered client-side, so a plain fetch shows nothing) Three plans, and the advertised price is the two-year rate. Snack $4.54/mo billed $109 every 2 years, $5.42/mo billed $65 annually, or $9.49 month to month: 1 email account and 2 of the Sane features. Lunch $7.46 / $9.08 ($109 a year) / $15.99: 2 accounts and 6 features. Dinner $22.04 / $26.58 ($319 a year) / $42.99: 4 accounts and every feature, plus phone support. The free trial is 7 days with all features on up to 4 accounts. Education, non-profit and government get another 25% off on request during the trial.
tools.honest_knock: It works with any email provider, which is a genuine advantage over the built-in tools in Gmail and Outlook, but you are paying monthly to filter mail that modern clients increasingly sort for free — the value is real only if your inbox is genuinely overwhelming and native filters are not cutting it. Price it on the plan you would actually keep: the headline rate is a two-year commitment, and month to month the same Snack plan is $9.49 rather than $4.54.
tools.best_for: heavy-email professionals drowning in a cluttered inbox who want AI triage that works across any mail client
tools.skip_if: your inbox is manageable or your mail client's built-in filtering already handles it — you don't need to pay for this

tools.name: Seamless.ai
tools.what_it_does: B2B contact database with AI list-building, plus an MCP server so Claude or ChatGPT can run the searching and enrichment. Paid plans are quote-based, reported around $147/month for 250 credits. Independent tests put deliverability near 74%, and contracts auto-renew with 30–60 days' notice to cancel.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A free plan with 50 credits; everything above it is sales-led and quote-based, and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved a published figure. Third-party guides report an entry around $147 a month for roughly 250 credits, ranging up to $150-500 per user a month — those are not Seamless's numbers and we could not verify them. What we can say from the public record is that credits, not seats, are what the contract rations, and that buyers report the renewal conversation being harder than the first sale.
tools.honest_knock: Data accuracy is the recurring complaint — independent tests put email deliverability around 74% (20–30% bounce) versus ZoomInfo's ~2–3%, so real cost per usable contact climbs. The buying experience is the other weak spot: sales-led, auto-renew with 30–60 day written cancellation, and reports of charges after a 'confirmed' cancellation.
tools.best_for: teams that want a huge real-time contact database and AI list-building for less than ZoomInfo, and can tolerate cleaning the data
tools.skip_if: data accuracy is your top priority (ZoomInfo bounces far less), or you want simple no-contract pricing — the bounce rates and auto-renewal bite
compare_with: the more accurate and the cheaper data tools

tools.name: Section Library: AI Sections
tools.what_it_does: Shopify app that adds 200+ ready-made theme sections plus AI-generated custom ones (Gemini 3.1 Pro), all inside the native theme editor so layouts change without a developer. Free plan gives 8 credits a month; paid runs $9, $19 or $29 a month for 25, 55 or 90 credits. Live since October 2023 with a single App Store review.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/section-library) Free plan: 8 credits a month, access to the free sections only, basic AI generation. Starter $9 a month: 25 credits, all sections accessible, AI section generation, email support. Pro $19 a month: 55 credits, all sections, priority support. Business $29 a month: 90 credits, all sections, priority support. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days, and the listing shows no free trial on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial. One thing the pricing table never states is what a credit actually buys: whether one credit is one AI generation, one section added to a theme, or something else is defined nowhere on the listing, and the credit count is the only thing separating the four plans. The vendor's own site, sectionlibrary.com, publishes no prices at all, so the App Store listing we link to is the only ladder on record. Developer Optify, 16 Rue Cuvier, Lyon, France; the app launched 10 October 2023. It carries a 5.0 rating from exactly one App Store review, left in October 2023 by a merchant who had the app installed for four minutes.
tools.honest_knock:
Almost three years on the App Store and one review. The app launched 10 October 2023 and, as of 19 August 2026, exactly one merchant has written about it: a five-star note from October 2023 by someone who had it installed for four minutes. That is not evidence of quality and not evidence of trouble — it is an absence of evidence, and on an app that writes sections into your live theme, that absence is the main thing to weigh. On the same listing page Shopify shows Section Store with 2,760 reviews, also free to install, which is what a track record looks like in this category.

Second, the credit is undefined. Every plan is priced in credits and nothing on the listing says what one buys, so you cannot price your own usage before you commit.

Third, the AI half of the product is Google's. Sections are generated by Gemini 3.1 Pro, so output quality and consistency shift when Google ships a new model, which is outside the vendor's hands as much as yours. The library half — the 200+ pre-built sections — is the part that depends on nobody else, and it is the part worth judging the app on.
tools.best_for: Shopify merchants who want ready-made theme sections and the occasional AI-generated layout inside the native theme editor, and who can live with an app that has almost no public track record
tools.skip_if: you are rebuilding a store you cannot afford to break and want a page builder with thousands of merchants behind it, or you need your monthly cost known in advance — the credit unit is never defined

tools.name: Securify
tools.what_it_does: Country blocker and fraud filter for Shopify: blocks countries, IP ranges, bots, VPNs and risky emails at checkout, and holds suspicious orders automatically. Free plan; paid $5.99 to $49 a month.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-18 on apps.shopify.com/easy-block-customer-ip-country) Free plan available with a free trial on the paid tiers. Paid runs Pro $5.99, Advanced $9.49 and Growth $49 a month. Rating 4.4 from 68 reviews, and it carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge. The App Store lists it as “Country Blocker Fraud Securify” from siimple.ai.
tools.honest_knock: Blocking by country and IP is a blunt instrument and it cuts both ways: every rule that keeps out a fraudster also keeps out a customer travelling, using a corporate VPN, or living behind a carrier NAT. The app is honest enough to give you a live log of what it blocked, and that log is the part to actually read — a rule set nobody reviews quietly costs sales. Also worth separating in your head: blocking bots from your analytics is a reporting fix, while blocking fraud at checkout is a money fix, and the two need different rules.
tools.best_for: stores seeing real fraud or bot traffic that want country, IP, VPN and email-risk rules plus automatic holds on suspicious orders, and who will review the block log rather than set and forget
tools.skip_if: you are blocking on a hunch rather than on measured fraud — start by reading your order data, because a blocked legitimate customer never tells you they were blocked

tools.name: Seel
tools.what_it_does: Shopper-paid returns and shipping protection for Shopify, BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce. Customers add Worry-Free Purchase at checkout and Seel pays the refund instead of you — free for the merchant.
tools.pricing: Free for the merchant, because Seel is shopper-paid — the fee lands on your customer's checkout rather than your invoice. Customers who add Worry-Free Purchase (formerly Return Assurance) pay roughly $2-$5, reported elsewhere as 3-5% of order value; Seel sets that figure with its own algorithm and publishes no rate card. No merchant subscription and no platform fee (verified 2026-08-02).
tools.honest_knock: Two things to weigh, and neither is the price you pay — because you do not pay one. First, you cannot set the fee. Seel's algorithm prices it, so if it lands too high for your niche and shoppers stop opting in, your only lever is switching the feature off entirely. Second, the charge appears on your checkout, not Seel's: shopper-side complaints filed with the BBB describe the fee arriving in the cart with the opt-out easy to miss, and that lands on your brand. Test it as a customer before you enable it. Also check the platform list — Shopify, BigCommerce and Adobe Commerce only, with no WooCommerce, Wix or custom storefront support.
tools.best_for: stores selling final-sale, high-consideration or hard-to-size products, where return anxiety is the thing killing the order — merchants report conversion lifting around 5% and shoppers taking the option roughly 24% of the time
tools.skip_if: your margin already absorbs returns comfortably, or you need control over what appears on your own checkout — the fee is set by Seel and shown to your customer either way
compare_with: the other shopper-paid model, but with merchant-side workflow control Seel does not offer

tools.name: Seller Investigators
tools.what_it_does: Amazon FBA reimbursement recovery on contingency: a free 48-hour audit, then a 25% commission charged only after Amazon deposits recovered funds. No subscription. Ask which cases Amazon would have settled automatically before you sign.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own site) One number, and it is the whole model: a 25% commission, charged only after Amazon has deposited recovered funds in your account. We found it stated twice — on the home page (“only pay a 25% commission fee when your money is back with you”) and again in the FAQ (“no risk or upfront commitment, with a 25% recovery fee only after Amazon deposits recovered funds into your account”). The audit is free, takes 48 hours and carries no obligation. There is no subscription and no /pricing page, because there is nothing else to price. Cases they say they cover include inbound shipment discrepancies, items lost in transit or in the warehouse, items damaged or disposed of by Amazon, unfair reimbursements and customer returns.
tools.honest_knock: Contingency pricing is the honest kind — you pay only out of money that arrived — but 25% of a recovery is not the same as 25% of a profit, and there is one question that decides whether this is worth it for you. Amazon reimburses some categories automatically, and its policies on that have changed more than once. So ask, before you sign: which of these cases would Amazon have settled on its own within the claim window, and what exactly is the 25% charged on — the gross amount recovered, or what is left after Amazon's own fees? A free audit that finds $20,000 sounds decisive until you learn how much of it was already on its way. Ask for the split, in writing, before the audit turns into an engagement.
tools.best_for: established FBA sellers with enough inventory movement that discrepancies add up and nobody in-house has time to file case-by-case claims — the contingency model means an audit costs you nothing but the access you grant
tools.skip_if: you are a small seller whose monthly discrepancies are modest, where 25% of a small recovery buys less than the hour it takes to file yourself; also skip it until you have asked what share of the claim Amazon would have paid automatically, because that is the part of the bill that buys you nothing
compare_with: the comparison worth making, and the two are related — the Seller Investigators partner link runs through Carbon6's own domain. Carbon6 sells a suite of Amazon seller tools on published monthly subscriptions; this is a single contingency service with no subscription at all. If reimbursement recovery is the only job you need done, paying a percentage of what comes back is the cheaper shape; if you want inventory and profit tooling alongside it, the suite is the better buy

tools.name: Seller Snap
tools.what_it_does: AI repricer and seller-analytics platform for Amazon and Walmart — what the vendor calls game-theory repricing, aimed at Buy Box share rather than racing to the bottom, plus min/max profit calculation, 80+ analytics data points and imports from tools like InventoryLab and SkuVault. Starter is $100/month billed annually (annual only); month-to-month starts at $250. 15-day free trial, no credit card. A July 2026 interface release adds live Buy Box insight with SKU-level filters, multi-store management from one screen including bulk cost updates, repricing from mobile, historical inventory-value tracking, saved views, customizable columns and a dark mode.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-07-24, read in a live browser on their own pricing page, both the monthly and the annual column) Four tiers, and the axis that sets your price is capacity, not features — all four list the same six feature groups (Amazon & Walmart, AI repricing technology, min & max calculation, analytics, connectivity, integrations). Starter: $100/month, annual billing only, for 1 marketplace, 1 user, 1,000 SKUs and $15,000 revenue. Accelerator: $250/month billed monthly, or $175/month paid annually, for 1 seller ID, 3 users, 1,000 SKUs and $30,000 revenue. The page prints those two revenue figures without a period; Seller Snap told us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both caps are calculated per month, so read them as $15,000/month and $30,000/month. Standard: $500/month billed monthly, or $425/month paid annually, for 1 seller ID, 3 users, 15,000 SKUs and unlimited revenue. Custom is quote-only. Annual billing saves a flat $900 a year on both Accelerator and Standard — the same money, but 30 percent off the smaller plan against 15 percent off the larger one. Every tier carries a 15-day trial with no credit card, and in the monthly view each price is labelled 'Starting at'. Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that readers coming through our link get 10% off for their first three months; it runs through the link, there is no code to enter. Update: asked directly, Seller Snap confirmed by email on 24 July 2026 that the Starter and Accelerator revenue caps are calculated per month. Their pricing page still does not say so — we are passing on the vendor's answer, not something you can verify on the page yourself.
tools.honest_knock: Read the caps before you read the prices, because the caps are what you are actually buying. Two of them deserve scrutiny. First, the revenue limits — $15,000 on Starter, $30,000 on Accelerator — are printed with no period attached on the pricing page. We asked, and Seller Snap confirmed to us in writing on 24 Jul 2026 that both caps are calculated per month. That is the reading that costs you money: $15,000 a month is roughly $500 a day, so a seller who already clears that sits above Starter before signing up, and $30,000 a month puts the ceiling of Accelerator within reach of a shop doing $1,000 a day. Measure your own monthly revenue against the tier first, because the page will not do it for you. Second, the SKU limit sits at 1,000 on both of the lower tiers, so catalog growth alone — not revenue, not users — can push you up a step. And the steps are steep: leaving Accelerator for Standard means $425/month annually or $500 monthly, roughly 2.4 times what you were paying, for capacity rather than for any feature you did not already have. The cheapest door is also not quite $100: Starter is annual-billing only, so the lowest month-to-month entry into the product is $250/month. Finally, 'Starting at' appears above every monthly price on the vendor's own page — treat all of these as floors and confirm your own quote. Worth checking first, though: Amazon already includes a rule-based repricer. Automate Pricing comes with the Professional selling plan and supports rules such as Competitive Featured Offer and Competitive Lowest Price with a seller-set price floor, so if your problem is simply matching the competitive price without going below cost, test that before paying for anything. And note what sets your tier: their FAQ says pricing follows the total number of SKUs in your Seller Central account, not the active ones, so a dormant catalogue costs you money.
tools.best_for: Amazon and Walmart sellers past the hobby stage who compete for the Buy Box on a catalog of up to a few thousand SKUs and want AI repricing and deep seller analytics in one place — the 15-day no-card trial makes it cheap to test against your own listings before any commitment
tools.skip_if: you sell mainly outside Amazon and Walmart (those are the only two marketplaces supported), your catalog and revenue are small enough that a rules-based repricer at a fraction of the price does the same job, or what you actually need is multi-channel competitor price monitoring rather than marketplace Buy Box repricing
compare_with: the other AI-first Amazon repricer we cover: Feedvisor's real platform (Feedvisor360, with ad optimization and dedicated analysts) starts around $1,500/mo, while Seller Snap sits in the $175-$425/mo band on published, self-serve pricing with a no-card trial. If you need multi-channel price monitoring rather than marketplace repricing, compare Pricefy instead — and verify every current price list yourself before you sign.

tools.name: Sellfy
tools.what_it_does: No-code store builder for creators to sell digital products, subscriptions and print-on-demand merch — with zero transaction fees and built-in social-media selling.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17 — and the price went up since our last reading) Starter $39/mo billed monthly or $29/mo billed yearly, for up to $10k of sales a year; Business $79 or $59, up to $50k; Premium $159 or $119, up to $200k; above that Sellfy quotes you. Yearly billing saves 25% and there is a 14-day trial with no free tier. 0% transaction fees on every plan, which is the real argument for it against marketplaces that take a cut. Note the entry price: what our earlier note called '$29 a month' is now the yearly rate, and the monthly rate is $39.
tools.honest_knock: The honest mechanic is the revenue ladder: plans cap by your ANNUAL SALES, so success automatically promotes you to a pricier tier — factor that into margins rather than discovering it at $10,001. The 0% transaction fee is genuinely rare and, for higher-volume sellers, beats percentage-taking platforms decisively; below a few hundred in monthly sales, the flat subscription is the tax instead.
tools.best_for: creators selling digital products, subscriptions and print-on-demand who want a simple store with zero platform commission
tools.skip_if: you sell occasionally (percentage-fee platforms like Gumroad cost nothing idle), or you need a full e-commerce ecosystem (Shopify territory)
compare_with: the creator-store trio — Gumroad takes ~10% but no subscription; the crossover math is simple: past ~$300-400/mo in sales, Sellfy's flat fee wins

tools.name: Sendcloud
tools.what_it_does: European e-commerce shipping platform: connect 160+ carriers, print labels in batches, show delivery options at checkout, send branded tracking (email, WhatsApp, SMS) and run a self-service returns portal — with rules-based shipping automation. Available to online retailers in 8 countries (Netherlands, Belgium, UK, France, Germany, Austria, Italy, Spain). Free plan available.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026, tiers renamed) A genuine Free plan (€0/mo, no courier contract, no subscription — you pay only carrier costs, with limited scope). Paid tiers, billed monthly or yearly (-20%): Lite €28/mo + €0.10 per label, Growth €87/mo + €0.09, Premium €175/mo + €0.08, Pro €639/mo + €0.07; Enterprise is bespoke. Note the double meter: a subscription AND a per-label fee on every paid plan.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing has layers — a per-label fee on top of the subscription, plus carrier surcharges that can land on invoices weeks later. It's built out-of-the-box, so deep customisation is limited, there's no inventory management (ShipStation has it), and high-volume shippers (€12k+/mo) plus pickup-reliability complaints suggest it's happiest with small-to-mid EU stores.
tools.best_for: European e-commerce stores that want easy multi-carrier shipping (DHL, PostNL, Colissimo, GLS, DPD), branded tracking and a returns portal live in under 30 minutes
tools.skip_if: you ship mainly in the US, need inventory management and complex fulfilment, or you're a very high-volume shipper wanting deep customisation — ShipStation fits that better
compare_with: the US-focused fulfilment platform with inventory management

tools.name: Sentaro
tools.what_it_does: Email threat detection that flags phishing, risky and malicious messages right in your inbox. Surfaces the dangerous emails that look perfectly normal — before anyone clicks.
tools.pricing: Not publicly listed (2026) — connects to Google Workspace/Microsoft 365 without MX changes; pricing runs quote-based. Ask for per-mailbox rates in writing.
tools.honest_knock: The category claim (AI catches what filters miss) is plausible — Microsoft/Google native filtering misses sophisticated BEC — but any vendor's accuracy percentage is measured on their own test set, not your mail flow. The honest procurement move: run their trial alongside your current filtering, count real catches and false positives for two weeks, and price per mailbox against the incumbents with that data in hand.
tools.best_for: SMBs on Google Workspace/M365 that want an extra AI layer against phishing and BEC without infrastructure changes
tools.skip_if: you already run a mature email-security stack (Ironscales/Abnormal-class), or nobody internally will review the flagged-mail queue
compare_with: the established API-based email-security players — compare detected-in-YOUR-inbox counts from parallel trials, not brochure accuracy

tools.name: SEO Space
tools.what_it_does: SEO tool built exclusively for Squarespace, delivered as a Chrome extension paired with a web dashboard. The extension runs inside the Squarespace editor and on live pages, scoring each page and saying in plain language what to change and where the setting lives; the dashboard adds site-wide audits, keyword rank tracking, backlink and competitor data, local SEO tools and scheduled white-label PDF client reports. Pricing is keyed to the number of websites rather than seats, which is why it suits freelancers and studios managing client sites. There is a genuinely usable free plan — a scan of up to 50 pages without a card; paid pricing is keyed to the number of websites, with the most-popular position (5 sites) at $33.33/month billed annually, read 17 Aug 2026.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-17, re-verified on their own homepage pricing block) One figure is published: Pro, the default position on their website slider, is $33.33/mo billed annually, labelled MOST POPULAR and covering 5 websites. The slider runs 1, 3, 5, 10, 20 and unlimited websites, but the amounts for the other positions are rendered per selection and do not appear in the delivered page, so we do not quote them. Yearly billing is sold as "4 Months Free", which means the equivalent monthly rate is higher than the headline — the page does not print it next to the plan. Pricing is by number of websites, not per seat, and their own line "All Plans Include Every Feature" means a higher position buys site slots rather than extra capability. Free entry is real: a scan of up to 50 pages with no card, plus a 7-day trial of Pro, also with no card. An earlier reading (21 Jul 2026) recorded named Starter/Pro/Expert tiers at 1/3/5 sites with their own amounts; the page no longer shows that structure, so those figures have been withdrawn rather than carried forward.
tools.honest_knock: Squarespace has been quietly absorbing the job this tool was invented for. The platform's own SEO panel, checklist, sitemaps and structured data are free, its AI-suggested titles, descriptions and alt text are available on Fluid Engine 7.1, and on 7 July 2026 it announced AI Visibility — brand tracking across AI search — included on 7.1 plans with no extra subscription, though metered against plan-varying AI credits rather than unlimited. If you own a single Squarespace site, a large share of what you would pay for here is now a friendlier wrapper around something the platform already does. The tool earns its keep on volume and client work, not on one site. Note too what their own pricing block says out loud — 'All Plans Include Every Feature' — so moving up the ladder buys site slots, not a better tool.
tools.best_for: Squarespace freelancers and studios billing for several client sites — pricing by number of websites rather than per seat, multi-site dashboards and white-label PDF reports are things the big per-seat SEO suites never bothered to build for Squarespace, and the extension tells you where the setting actually lives in the editor
tools.skip_if: you run a single Squarespace 7.1 site and have no clients — Squarespace's own free SEO panel, AI-generated descriptions and AI Visibility now cover much of what you would be paying for, and the free plan here will tell you whether the paid layer adds anything for your site before you spend
compare_with: SEO Space wins on translation, not data: it knows where each setting lives in the Squarespace editor, while Ahrefs and Semrush have vastly deeper indexes and cost several times more. Pick by whether your bottleneck is knowing what to fix or knowing where to fix it

tools.name: Serpstat
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one SEO platform — keyword research, competitor analysis, rank tracking, site audit and backlink data — from $50/month on annual billing ($69 month-to-month), with a 7-day trial that takes a card and auto-renews.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-24, read on their own pricing page) Four plans, and the page opens on the annual view — so the first number you see is not the month-to-month price. Individual $69/month, or $50 on annual billing. Team $129, or $100 annually. Team x2 $209, or $169. Agency $499, or $410. There is a hidden middle step: two dropdowns inside the Team column (position checks 50,000 or 99,999, API credits 200,000 or 400,000) move Team to $169/month monthly or $135 annually, so Team is really three price points. Seats are capped rather than sold: Individual is single-user, Team 3, Team x2 6, Agency 30, and no per-seat price is published anywhere — a fourth user means the next tier. The limits matter more than the prices: 100 searches a day on Individual (500 / 1,000 / 5,000 above it), export rows 50,000 a month, and no API at all on the entry plan. The 7-day trial takes a card, charges $1 to verify, turns on auto-renewal and bills the plan after seven days unless you cancel.
