tools.honest_knock: The thing you are actually buying is data coverage, and that is the one thing you cannot verify — Serpstat's own published figures do not agree with each other. Re-read on 24 July 2026, their homepage says 529 billion backlinks, their data hub says 1.1 trillion, and their backlinks page says 1.7 trillion in the prose while its own spec block on that same page says 1.1 trillion. The keyword count reads 8.62 billion on one page and 7.46 billion on another. That is not evidence the data is thin; it is evidence that these numbers cannot serve as a basis for your decision. Judge it on your own searches during the trial instead. Two other things to weigh: backlink reports are capped at 10,000 results per report on Team, Team x2 and Agency alike, so paying from $129 to $499 buys more of everything except a deeper backlink report; and 'maximum pages to scan' in a single crawl (5,000 / 25,000 / 50,000) is a far smaller number than the monthly 'pages to audit' allowance it sits next to.
tools.best_for: solo SEOs and small in-house teams who want the whole workflow — keywords, rankings, audit, competitors — under one subscription at roughly a third of what the incumbents charge, and who will judge the data on their own market during the trial rather than on published database sizes
tools.skip_if: your work depends on deep backlink analysis, since the 10,000 results per report ceiling does not move no matter which tier you buy; or you need more than three seats, because seats are not sold separately and the next tier roughly doubles the bill
compare_with: the closest self-serve rival on price and scope — both sell the full workflow well under what the incumbents charge, so the decision comes down to which one's data holds up on your own market and how each counts its limits. Compare the units carefully: a daily allowance and a monthly stock are not the same number, and both vendors mix them. Verify both current price lists yourself.

tools.name: ServiceM8
tools.what_it_does: Job management for trades and service contractors: scheduling, quotes, job cards and invoicing.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page, USD) Priced by jobs per month, with unlimited users on every paid tier. Free $0: 1 user, 30 jobs a month, 10 AI uses a day. Starter $29: unlimited users, 50 jobs. Growing $79: 150 jobs. Premium $149: 500 jobs. Premium Plus $349: 1,500+ jobs. A 14-day free trial is offered.
tools.honest_knock: Unlimited users on every paid tier is genuinely unusual in this category and worth saying first: put your whole crew in without the bill moving. The meter is jobs instead, and jobs are the thing you least control. Fifty a month on Starter is roughly two a working day, which a two-van operation passes in a busy month — and the next step is not a small one, it is $29 to $79. Count your jobs in your best month rather than your average, because that is the month that will bump you, and a seasonal trade will spend part of the year paying for a tier it does not need. The free tier at 30 jobs and one user is a real trial, not a plan.
tools.best_for: trades and service businesses with a crew, where per-user pricing elsewhere punishes you for having enough people — this is one of the few tools in the category that does not
tools.skip_if: you are a sole trader doing a handful of jobs a month — the free tier covers that, and at low job volume the paid tiers are buying capacity rather than features
compare_with: the direct job-management peers — compare on jobs included versus users included, because that is the axis these differ on

tools.name: Shiftie
tools.what_it_does: Rota building, clock-ins, leave and shift swaps for shift-based businesses. Charged per active employee — roughly £2.75 a month, dropping to about £1.50 once you pass 30 staff, with entry plans from about £39. Not an HR or payroll platform, so those stay separate purchases.
tools.pricing: Per active employee, per month (2026): roughly £2.75/employee, dropping to about £1.50 once you pass ~30 staff; entry plans from about £39/mo. You only pay for active users, and all plans include a 28-day free trial.
tools.honest_knock: It's focused, affordable rota software — which means it does scheduling, clock-ins, leave and swaps well, but it isn't a full HR or payroll platform, so a growing business will still bolt on payroll and HR tools around it. Pricing is genuinely low, but the per-active-employee model means a large seasonal team in a busy month costs more than the headline suggests. For shift-based scheduling specifically, it's a clean, cheap fit.
tools.best_for: shift-based businesses (hospitality, retail, leisure) that want quick rota building, clock-ins and leave management without spreadsheet pain
tools.skip_if: you need full HR, payroll and performance management in one system, or your team doesn't work in shifts at all
compare_with: comparable scheduling platforms — Shiftie tends to undercut on price; compare on payroll/HR features you actually need

tools.name: Shippo
tools.what_it_does: Multi-carrier shipping software for e-commerce. Compare rates, print discounted labels and automate tracking across carriers — shipping that scales with your store.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-11, read on their own pricing page) App plans. Starter is free: up to 30 labels a month, discounted USPS, UPS, FedEx and DHL Express rates, 1 user login, and 5¢ per label if you connect your own carrier account. Pro is listed as "Starts at $17/mo", with an annual option quoted at $205/year (a 10% saving); it covers 1-200 labels a month, makes your own carrier accounts free, and adds branded tracking pages, chat and phone support and up to 5 user logins. The comparison table puts Pro at up to 10,000 shipments a month with $0.08 per label beyond that. Premier is contact-us: unlimited shipments, 15+ user logins and a dedicated account manager. Non-US address validation is billed separately at 9¢ per validation on Starter, 8¢ on Pro and 6¢ on Premier. API calls not tied to a Shippo label are billed at API Starter rates.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing is honest but layered. The free tier stops at 30 labels a month, and its 5¢ per label on your own carrier accounts quietly adds up. Pro looks like a flat $17 a month until you read the comparison table: it covers up to 10,000 shipments and then bills $0.08 for every label beyond that, so a good sales month adds a variable line to a subscription that reads as fixed. Address validation outside the US is metered too, at 9¢, 8¢ or 6¢ depending on plan. The real money is elsewhere anyway — in the carrier rate discounts, which vary by lane and weight. Run your five most common shipments through it against your current rates; that comparison decides, not the subscription price.
tools.best_for: e-commerce sellers shipping across multiple carriers who want rate comparison, label printing and tracking in one place with genuine rate discounts
tools.skip_if: you ship a handful of packages monthly through one carrier (their native tools are fine), or you're big enough for direct carrier contracts to beat aggregated rates
compare_with: the direct shipping-software peers — compare discounted rates on your actual lanes and the workflow features your volume needs

tools.name: Shoeboxed
tools.what_it_does: Turn paper and digital receipts into organized, IRS-ready expense data with OCR plus human verification — syncs with QuickBooks and Xero.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Starter about $97/yr (30 digital scans/mo, 1 Magic Envelope/yr); Pro ~$297/yr (200 scans/mo, monthly paper scans, QuickBooks/Xero sync); Plus ~$79/mo; Paper Plus ~$179/mo for heavy mail-in volume. 30-day money-back guarantee.
tools.honest_knock: Its unique trick — the Magic Envelope, where you literally mail a stuffed envelope of paper receipts and humans digitize them — is also the meter to watch: envelope frequency defines the tiers, and heavy paper businesses land in the $179/mo bracket quickly. If your receipts are already digital, cheaper scan-only apps exist; Shoeboxed earns its price precisely when physical paper is the problem.
tools.best_for: businesses drowning in PAPER receipts — trades, field crews, owners with shoeboxes of history — who want them humanly digitized, verified and IRS-ready
tools.skip_if: your receipts are mostly digital already (lighter OCR apps cost less), or your accountant's tooling ingests receipts natively
compare_with: app-first expense tools — Shoeboxed's differentiator is the mail-in human digitization; if you don't need that, compare on OCR quality alone

tools.name: Shorby
tools.what_it_does: Link-in-bio pages and short links, with messenger deep-links into WhatsApp or Telegram and retargeting pixels firing on every click. It charges from about $15/month where Linktree does not charge at all, so the gap only pays off if messenger selling or ad retargeting is genuinely your funnel.
tools.pricing: (2026) Rocket about $15/mo, Pro ~$29/mo (analytics, custom domains), Agency ~$99/mo (multi-client); 7-day trial, no permanent free tier.
tools.honest_knock: In a category where the market leader has a generous free plan, Shorby charges from day one — so it has to earn the gap, and its case rests on two genuinely differentiated features: messenger deep-links (one tap into WhatsApp/Telegram chats) and retargeting pixels firing on every click. If you use neither, Linktree's free tier wins; if messenger-first selling or ad retargeting is your funnel, the $15 pays for itself.
tools.best_for: creators and businesses that sell via messenger conversations or retarget link-in-bio traffic with ad pixels
tools.skip_if: you just need a links page (free tools abound), or your audience doesn't click through to chat apps
compare_with: the free-tier giants — Shorby's paid-only stance is justified only by its messenger and pixel features; decide on those

tools.name: Shore
tools.what_it_does: Booking and business software for local service businesses (salons, barbers, wellness, coaches): 24/7 online appointments via your website, Google and Instagram, calendar and staff scheduling, client profiles, automated reminders that cut no-shows, plus email marketing and POS. Fixed monthly price with unlimited bookings — no per-booking commission.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-15, read on their own pricing page, in euros) Three packages, each per month and each currently marked down from a struck-through list price: Starter €59.90 down to €49.90 with 2 employees included, Growth €89.90 down to €79.90 with 4 employees, and the top tier €129.90 down to €119.90 with unlimited employees. Card payments run at up to 1.35% on every tier. Starter holds the booking calendar, online booking via your own site plus Google and Instagram, email and SMS reminders, deposits and the iPad POS register; Growth adds the marketing layer — newsletters, WhatsApp reminders, Google review requests, vouchers, customer segments; the top tier adds shift planning, revenue reports per employee, register analytics and a direct DATEV connection. Shore reorganised this grid during August 2026: the same page carried five packages split by Booking, Marketing and POS when we captured it on 4 August. The page is region-specific — these are the euro tiers — so verify your own country's. POS hardware and card processing are billed separately.
tools.honest_knock: It's built for local appointment businesses, and that's also the boundary: the integration list is short (calendar, Google, Instagram, Meta), and once you add POS and payments the monthly total climbs well past the entry price. If you only need a booking link, this is more machine than you need.
tools.best_for: salons, barbers, spas, wellness studios, physical therapists, craftspeople and local retailers that want bookings via Google and Instagram, no-show-reducing reminders, marketing and (optionally) POS in one fixed-price system
tools.skip_if: you just need a simple scheduling link (a Calendly-class tool is lighter) or you run a business without appointments at all
compare_with: commission-based salon platforms or lighter pure-scheduling tools

tools.name: Signal House
tools.what_it_does: SMS and Voice API positioned as a Twilio alternative. Usage-based with no platform fee: $0.0065 per SMS segment with no minimum, down to $0.0030 above 10m, and $1.00 a month per local number. A2P 10DLC fees are published; voice rates are not.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-07, read on their own pricing page) Usage-based, no platform subscription. SMS on a 10DLC local number costs $0.0065 per segment with no minimum, falling on volume: $0.0050 from 500k segments a month, $0.0045 from 1m, $0.0040 from 2m, $0.0035 from 5m and $0.0030 from 10m. Numbers are $1.00 a month, dropping to $0.50 between 500 and 1,000 numbers and $0.25 above 1,000. MMS is $0.0200 per segment, $0.0170 above 500k. Toll-free numbers are $1.00 a month with SMS from $0.0079 down to $0.0050. Number lookup is $0.005. A2P 10DLC registration is billed separately: $4.50 for the brand, $15 one-time per campaign, then $1.50 a month for a low-volume campaign or $10 a month for a standard one. Carrier fees are passed through on top: outbound AT&T $0.0035, Verizon $0.0045, T-Mobile $0.0045. A2P approval is quoted at 72 hours or less, dropping to 48 hours above 500k segments a month.
tools.honest_knock:
Two things are missing from a page that is otherwise unusually specific. The first is voice. The product is sold as an SMS and Voice API and the pricing page publishes no voice rate at all — nor short code pricing. If the voice half is why you are looking, you cannot budget it from public information and will have to ask.

The second is the arithmetic behind the Twilio comparison, which is the whole pitch. Take the entry rate with no minimum. Signal House is $0.0065 a segment against Twilio’s $0.0083, which reads as a 22% saving. But carrier fees are a pass-through and identical either way: add T-Mobile’s $0.0045 to both and you get $0.0110 against $0.0128 — about 14%, not 22%. Numbers narrow it further, $1.00 against $1.15. So the saving is real and it is worth having at volume, but it is a discount on the platform margin rather than on your bill, and the headline does not make that distinction. On a million segments a month that difference is roughly $1,800 a month against Twilio’s list — worth switching for, provided the voice side does not turn out to be where the money goes.

Worth noting on the other side: Signal House prints its A2P 10DLC registration fees on the pricing page, and Twilio’s equivalent page says only that fees apply and points elsewhere. Being able to see the whole bill before you sign is not nothing.
tools.best_for: teams sending real SMS volume in the US who already know what an A2P 10DLC campaign is and want a cheaper per-segment rate than Twilio’s list without giving up published pricing. The volume ladder is genuinely steep — from $0.0065 down to $0.0030 — so the case gets stronger the more you send, and the number discounts above 500 numbers suit anyone running many local presences.
tools.skip_if: you are mainly buying voice, because there is no published rate to compare and no way to model the cost. Skip it too if your volume is small: at a few thousand messages a month the per-segment saving against Twilio is a few dollars, and you would be trading a mature ecosystem and documentation for that. And if you are not already registered for A2P 10DLC, budget the brand and campaign fees plus the approval wait before you compare anything — those apply wherever you send from.
compare_with: the comparison Signal House invites, and it is checkable. On the entry tier Signal House charges $0.0065 a segment against Twilio’s $0.0083, and $1.00 a month for a local number against $1.15. Carrier fees are pass-through and the same on both, so the all-in gap is nearer 14% than the 22% the message rate alone suggests. What Twilio has that does not show up in a rate table is depth: a far larger ecosystem, more documentation and a longer track record, plus voice pricing you can actually read. Both price lists here were read on 2026-08-07 — verify them yourself, because usage-based rates move and neither vendor publishes every fee in one place.

tools.name: Signeasy
tools.what_it_does: E-signature and contract management for SMBs — unlimited signing and sending, templates, audit trails and integrations, priced per seat.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against signeasy.com) (2026) Free trial. Personal $10/mo billed yearly ($120) — single seat, built around signing. Business $20/mo per seat billed yearly ($240/seat) adds unlimited sending and collaboration; Business Pro $30/mo per seat ($360/seat) adds end-to-end contract management with roles.
tools.honest_knock: The $10 Personal plan is annual-billed and single-seat — and note that sign-unlimited is not send-unlimited: proper unlimited sending starts at Business, $20 per seat on a yearly commitment, while contract-management features gate at Business Pro, $30 per seat.
tools.best_for: small teams that want straightforward unlimited sending and signing per seat, with contract management one tier up
tools.skip_if: you only sign occasional documents, or you are a solo sender at volume — Personal is single-seat and sending-limited
compare_with: DocuSign is the enterprise default with the deepest integration catalog; Signeasy is the simpler, cheaper-per-seat alternative for SMB sending and signing

tools.name: SignNow
tools.what_it_does: Electronic signatures and custom eSignature workflows by airSlate. Send, sign and manage documents on any device — legally binding and team-friendly.
tools.pricing: Business from ~$8/user/mo (annual), Premium ~$15, Enterprise ~$30 — with unlimited users on most plans, roughly 60% under DocuSign (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's built for straightforward everyday signing — if you need deep contract-lifecycle (CLM) features, a heavier platform fits better.
tools.best_for: teams that sign at volume and want unlimited users at a flat rate — roughly 60% under DocuSign for the same core job
tools.skip_if: you need the deepest enterprise integrations and workflows — that's where the incumbent still earns its premium

tools.name: Similarweb
tools.what_it_does: Competitive intelligence on web traffic, search and ads — what your competitors' visitors do.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-14, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown — that is still the finding. The page presents a feature matrix across suites — Competitive Intel, Strategic SEO, Ads Intel, Gen AI Intel and AI Studio — split between entrepreneurs and businesses and enterprises, with every business tier routed to sales: 'please contact our sales team to discuss a custom package tailored to your needs.' A free trial is offered without a stated length. Up to 37 months of data history is sold as an add-on rather than an inclusion, and API access is either standalone or inside a custom package.
tools.honest_knock: There is no price on the pricing page, and that is the finding. Everything above the entry level is a custom package agreed with a salesperson, which means the number you are quoted depends on what they think you can pay and you have no anchor to argue from. Two specifics worth pinning down before that call: the data history you need is an add-on, not an inclusion — 37 months is sold separately — and API access is priced apart from the seats. Ask for the rate card in writing and ask what happens at renewal, because with no public price there is nothing to hold a renewal quote against.
tools.best_for: marketing and strategy teams who need traffic and channel estimates for competitors and will use them often enough to justify a negotiated annual contract
tools.skip_if: you want a quick check on one competitor — the free tier and public estimates cover that, and the paid product is an annual commitment agreed by phone
compare_with: the tools people weigh this against — both publish their prices, which is itself part of the comparison

tools.name: SimpleTexting
tools.what_it_does: SMS marketing and business texting: run mass-text campaigns, two-way conversations and automations with compliance built in.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Credit-based by monthly volume, from $39/mo (500 credits) up to about $909/mo (50,000), with SMS = 1 credit and MMS = 3. Yearly billing saves 20% — the entry plan is $39 a month billed yearly at $398.40 — and unused credits roll over. Extra credits beyond your plan run 5.5 cents each. Every paid plan includes three user seats, with additional seats at $20/mo each and additional numbers at $10/mo; a local number is $10/mo plus a $4 activation fee, and there is a one-off $4 carrier (10DLC) registration. Toll-free and short-code options sit above that, with short codes beginning at $1,000/mo. Nonprofits, churches and other tax-exempt organisations get 15% off any monthly plan.
tools.honest_knock: The credit model plus US carrier (10DLC) fees and per-number/per-seat add-ons mean the sticker isn't the whole bill — and SMS marketing only works with genuine opt-in and a real offer, not blasting a cold list.
tools.best_for: US businesses that want straightforward, compliant SMS marketing and two-way texting with rollover credits
tools.skip_if: you don't have a real opted-in list or a compelling offer — texting a cold audience burns money and trust

tools.name: SimplyBook.me
tools.what_it_does: Online booking and scheduling system for service businesses — booking website and widget, provider calendars, automated reminders and online payments. Free plan for 50 bookings a month with one provider; paid plans from EUR 11.90 a month billed annually.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-02, read on their own pricing page, in euros) Free EUR 0: 50 bookings a month, 1 custom feature, 1 provider, no card needed. Basic EUR 11.90/month billed annually or EUR 13.90 monthly: 100 bookings, 3 custom features, 5 providers. Standard EUR 24.90 annual or EUR 29.90 monthly: 500 bookings, 8 custom features, 15 providers. Premium EUR 49.90 annual or EUR 59.90 monthly: 2,000 bookings, unlimited custom features, 30 providers. Enterprise is quote-only. Annual billing saves a stated 17%. Their own page says no setup fees, no transaction fees and no per-user charges — payment processors bill their own rates separately. A 14-day trial of premium features runs without a card.
tools.honest_knock: The plan ladder is set by bookings per month and by how many custom features you may switch on, and those two ceilings move independently — so you can outgrow a plan on features while nowhere near the booking cap, or the reverse. Free and Basic also carry SimplyBook.me branding on your booking page; white-label starts at Premium.
tools.best_for: service businesses that take appointments and want a booking page, reminders and online payment without building one
tools.skip_if: you only need a simple calendar link for one person — a free scheduling link does that without a booking system on top

tools.name: Smartli
tools.what_it_does: AI writing suite for e-commerce: product listings, ad copy, SEO text and brand assets. Monthly runs $39 (Starter) to $299; on annual billing Starter disappears and Pro drops to about $24/month. Each of the nine tools is competent rather than deep, so leaning hard on one job means outgrowing it.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 5 Aug 2026, on smartli.ai) Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 7-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). Starter was $29/mo when we first checked, so the entry price has gone up.
tools.honest_knock: Smartli bundles nine AI tools — copy, SEO, images, logos — into one suite, and that breadth is also the honest catch: each individual tool is competent rather than best-in-class, so a team that leans hard on one job may outgrow it toward a specialist. And like all AI copy, its product descriptions and ad copy need a human edit and a fact-check — never publish specs or claims it invents about your product. For a store that wants many content jobs handled cheaply in one place, it's efficient.
tools.best_for: e-commerce sellers who want an affordable all-in-one AI suite to draft product listings, ad copy, SEO text and basic brand assets in one place
tools.skip_if: you need best-in-class depth in one area (a specialist copy or image tool), or you won't edit and fact-check AI output before it ships
compare_with: Jasper or Copy.ai plus a separate image tool
specialist AI-content tools — Smartli's edge is bundling many jobs cheaply; compare on the one job you'll use most

tools.name: SmartSuite
tools.what_it_does: One flexible work management platform to plan, track and automate any process. Projects, CRM and operations side by side — replace a stack of scattered tools with a single source of truth.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) No free plan — a 14-day trial of Professional with no credit card. Team is $15 per seat a month billed annually, or $20 billed monthly, with a minimum of 3 billable users, 5,000 records per solution and 50 GB of storage. Professional is $32 per seat annually, or $36 monthly, with a minimum of 5 billable users, 100,000 records and 100 GB. Enterprise is custom-priced. The minimums matter more than the rate: a three-person team on Team pays for three seats whether or not all three log in, and Professional cannot be bought for fewer than five.
tools.honest_knock: It's a broad, do-everything work-management platform, so the power comes with a learning curve and a per-seat cost that adds up for bigger teams — a single source of truth if you commit, overkill if you just need a task list.
tools.best_for: teams consolidating projects, CRM and operations into one flexible, database-driven work-management platform
tools.skip_if: you need a lightweight to-do or a single-purpose tool — SmartSuite's breadth is wasted and its learning curve isn't worth it

tools.name: SMTP.com
tools.what_it_does: Reliable transactional and bulk email delivery via SMTP relay and API: high-deliverability sending for app notifications, receipts and campaigns, with real-time analytics and dedicated IPs — built for volume senders.
tools.pricing: (2026) Fixed-volume plans: Essential $25/mo (shared IP, 50k emails), Starter $80/mo (dedicated IP begins here), Growth $300/mo, Business $500/mo (~1M emails), plus custom high-volume tiers. Add-ons (Reputation Defender, Insight Engine) run ~20% of plan cost; verification ~$0.01/address.
tools.honest_knock: It's a veteran, reliable relay, but two honest notes. Pricing is volume-tiered, so a shared IP on the cheapest plan is fine for low volume while serious senders need the dedicated-IP tiers (and the IP warm-up discipline that comes with them). And the value-add features — reputation and verification — are metered on top at ~20% of plan cost, so the real bill is higher than the base tier. It's infrastructure, not a marketing suite; you bring the campaigns.
tools.best_for: businesses and developers needing dependable high-deliverability transactional or bulk email via SMTP relay and API, with dedicated IPs at scale
tools.skip_if: you send low volume and a free/cheap SMTP tier covers you, or you want a full marketing-email platform with templates and automation built in
compare_with: close relay/API peers — Postmark leans transactional-fast, SendGrid broader; compare on IP options and deliverability at your volume

tools.name: SMTP2GO
tools.what_it_does: Reliable transactional and bulk email delivery. Send via a simple SMTP relay or API with strong deliverability, real-time analytics and global sending infrastructure.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against smtp2go.com) (2026) Free 1,000 emails/mo (200/day); Starter about $15/mo (10,000 emails, overage ~$1/1k); Professional ~$75/mo (100,000, dedicated IPs, ~$0.85/1k overage); custom above ~3M/mo. Annual = two months free.
tools.honest_knock: It's the pragmatic middle of email infrastructure: simpler and better-supported than the hyperscale APIs, cheaper than most, with genuinely useful reporting — but sending reputation is still yours to earn. A relay delivers what your domain deserves: without proper SPF/DKIM/DMARC and list hygiene, no provider saves you. Check the overage line if your volume is spiky; it's fair but real.
tools.best_for: businesses that want dependable transactional/bulk sending via SMTP or API with human support and clear per-volume pricing
tools.skip_if: you're inside a marketing platform that already sends for you, or you need advanced template/campaign tooling bundled in
compare_with: close relay peers — Postmark leans transactional purity; SMTP2GO wins on support reputation and price at SMB volumes

tools.name: SocialBee
tools.what_it_does: Social media management and scheduling with content categories. Plan, recycle and publish posts across all your channels from one calendar.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Bootstrap $29/month ($290 a year, $24.42/month): 5 profiles, 1 workspace, 1 user. Accelerate $49/month ($490 a year): 10 profiles. Pro $99/month ($990 a year): 25 profiles, 5 workspaces, 3 users per workspace. Agency tiers: Pro50 $179, Pro100 $329, Pro150 $449 a month for 50, 100 and 150 profiles. Add-ons: a set of 5 extra profiles $15/month, an extra user $10/month, an extra workspace $10/month. AI generation is unlimited on every tier.
tools.honest_knock: You are billed per social profile, not per person, and a profile is one brand account on one network. A single business posting to Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, X and TikTok has used the whole Bootstrap allowance before a second brand or a client exists. The second thing is that people cost extra on top: Bootstrap and Accelerate are single-user plans, so a two-person team on eight profiles is $49 plus $10, not $29. Count your profiles across every network first — that number, not your team size, decides the tier.
tools.best_for: solo marketers and small agencies who post to several networks on a schedule and want evergreen recycling rather than a queue that empties
tools.skip_if: you post to one or two networks by hand and are happy doing it, because the value here is category-based recycling across many profiles and that only pays back at volume
compare_with: the standing comparison — count your profiles across every network and price all three on that number

tools.name: Softr
tools.what_it_does: Build custom AI business apps, client portals and internal tools without code. Connect Airtable, Google Sheets or your data and launch in an afternoon.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) A free plan with unlimited apps, up to 3 builders, 5 app users, 5,000 database records, 500 workflow actions and 5 AI credits a month. Paid on yearly billing: Basic $19/month, Pro $99/month and Business $329/month, with Enterprise on custom limits; the pricing page opens on the Yearly tab and advertises two months off, so month-to-month costs more. Extra builder seats are priced per tier — $5/month on Basic, $10 on Pro and $20 on Business. Non-profits and education get a stated 50% discount, which is worth asking for rather than assuming.
tools.honest_knock: Builder seats are billed on top of the plan. Pricing counts builders and app users separately, so a public-facing app with a lot of end users gets expensive fast. It fits internal tools and client portals with a known audience, not an open signup.
tools.best_for: teams building internal tools, client portals or member apps on top of Airtable or Google Sheets without code
tools.skip_if: you're building a public consumer app with unpredictable, high user counts — the per-user model works against you there

tools.name: Spiky.ai
tools.what_it_does: AI meeting intelligence for revenue teams — records and analyses sales calls, tracks keywords and talk patterns, and coaches reps. Free tier at 3 meetings per user, then $15 to $40 per user per month on annual billing.
tools.pricing: Read in a live browser on their own pricing page, 31 Jul 2026, across both billing toggles. There is a genuine free tier, capped at 3 meetings per user per month. On annual billing Plus is $15, Pro $24 and Premium $40 per user per month; switch to monthly and the same three read $18, $29 and $49. Annual saves up to 18%. Trials need no card. Meeting allowances: 3 on Free, 30 on both Plus and Pro, unlimited on Premium.
tools.honest_knock: The number to check first is the meeting cap, not the price. Plus and Pro both stop at 30 meetings per user per month, so the step from $15 to $24 buys features, not capacity. A rep taking two calls a day passes 30 in three weeks, which pushes you to Premium at $40 — nearly triple the entry price — for volume rather than capability. Price this from your team's actual call count and you will land on the right tier; price it from the feature table and you will not.
tools.best_for: sales and customer-facing teams that already run most conversations on video and want the coaching layer — talk-time, keyword tracking and call review — without buying a full revenue-intelligence platform
tools.skip_if: your team's calls are mostly ad hoc or on the phone rather than video, or the meeting volume per rep sits well above 30 a month, in which case only the top tier fits and the cheaper plans are a false economy
compare_with: the other conversation and outreach tools we cover — Spiky's angle is coaching from the recording rather than sequencing the outreach; compare on meeting volume, because that is what sets your tier

tools.name: Spocket
tools.what_it_does: Dropshipping platform with vetted US and EU suppliers. Find fast-shipping products, add them to your store in a click and automate order fulfillment.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Four monthly plans: Starter $39.99 (25 unique products), Pro $59.99 (250 products), Empire $99.99 (10,000) and Unicorn $299.99 (25,000). Annual billing is advertised as eight months free, which the page quantifies as savings of $432, $516 and $2,563 on the upper plans, bringing Pro to about $24 a month. There is a 7-day trial and no per-order platform fee on top of the subscription — 0% transaction fee is stated on every tier.
tools.honest_knock: Spocket's pitch is faster-shipping US and EU suppliers, and that's real — but you still pay twice: the monthly subscription and the wholesale product cost, so margins depend on picking items with room to mark up. Catalog breadth is narrower than giant AliExpress-based tools (that's the trade for vetting and shipping speed), and the low Starter product cap pushes serious stores up to Pro quickly. It reduces, not removes, the usual dropshipping risks.
tools.best_for: dropshippers who want vetted US and EU suppliers with faster shipping and one-click store integration, prioritizing delivery speed over raw catalog size
tools.skip_if: you want the widest possible catalog at the lowest sourcing cost (AliExpress-based tools fit), or your margins can't absorb both subscription and wholesale cost
compare_with: AliExpress-oriented alternatives with bigger catalogs but often slower shipping — Spocket trades breadth for US/EU speed

tools.name: Stamped
tools.what_it_does: Reviews, ratings and loyalty platform for e-commerce: collect product reviews and user-generated content, run rewards and loyalty programs, and show social proof to lift conversions on Shopify and other stores.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-11, read on their own pricing page with the bundle toggle on and all three products ticked) There is no free plan, and the bill is driven by your monthly order volume rather than by a flat plan fee. Bundled, all three products came to about $18/month at the 200-order step and $79/month at 1,000 orders; $798/month is the figure at the 5,000-order step, not the price of the suite. Standalone, Reviews is around $23/month at 200 orders and $99 at 1,000. Plans include up to two domains and each additional store is $100/month after a first free month. Overage charges were dropped. A re-read on 12 August 2026 was not possible: the pricing page returns 403 to non-browser clients from both of our networks.
tools.honest_knock: The $798/month figure that circulates for the full suite is the 5,000-order step, not an entry price — at 200 orders the same three-product bundle came to about $18/month when we read it. Read the order band, not the headline. What does bite is the shape: each product is its own subscription and the price steps hard with volume, so a good month raises the bill in several places at once, and a second storefront is another $100/month. Start with one product and price the step above the volume you actually expect.
tools.best_for: mid-market Shopify brands that want reviews and loyalty in one platform instead of juggling separate apps
tools.skip_if: you're an early-stage store — the removed free plan and $199+/product pricing are steep before you have the volume to justify them
compare_with: other reviews and loyalty apps, some far cheaper

tools.name: Stampezee
tools.what_it_does: Digital stamp cards for local businesses, replacing paper punch cards. Stamp Start is free for one branch, one card and up to 100 stamps; Stamp Lite is $29.99/month for two branches and three cards. Public pricing stays thin, so re-check the tiers before committing.
tools.pricing: Stamp Start is free and covers 1 branch, 1 stamp card and up to 100 stamps; Stamp Lite is $29.99/mo and lifts that to 2 branches and 3 stamp cards. Tiers confirmed to us directly by Stampezee (2026-07-22) — their public pricing page stays thin, so re-check before committing.
tools.honest_knock: The category is honest and proven (digital stamp cards beat lost paper cards), and the platform is young with limited public pricing and review coverage — so start on the free plan, run one real campaign, and measure repeat-visit lift before paying. The deeper truth of loyalty programs: the mechanics are 10% of the outcome; a reward worth returning for is the other 90%.
tools.best_for: local businesses (cafés, salons, retail) that want a simple digital stamp-card loyalty program starting free
tools.skip_if: you need POS-integrated loyalty with CRM depth (bigger platforms exist), or your offer isn't repeat-visit shaped
compare_with: the digital-stamp peer set — compare per-location pricing and whether Apple/Google Wallet passes are included

tools.name: StoreSEO
tools.what_it_does: SEO suite for Shopify: bulk meta titles and descriptions, image compression and alt text, JSON-LD schema, sitemap submission, instant indexing requests and Search Console reporting, with AI credits for generated copy. Free forever for 25 products; paid runs $14.99, $39.99 or $249.99 a month by product count.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/storeseo) Free Forever covers 25 products with SEO scoring, 200 AI credits, 25 image optimisations, up to 5 tracked keywords, an LLMs.txt generator and Agents.md editor, an SEO migrator, alt-text optimisation and 24/7 chat support. Paid tiers are Lite $14.99, Essential $39.99 and Advanced $249.99 a month, each with a 7-day free trial. Lite covers 100 products, 500 image optimisations and 1,000 AI credits and adds one-click schema markup, instant indexing requests, Google Analytics and Search Console and automatic sitemap submission. Essential covers 250 products, 2,000 images and 5,000 credits. Advanced covers 10,000 products, 50,000 images, 50,000 credits and adds multilingual SEO. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Worth knowing: storeseo.com sells a Growth plan at $99.99 a month (1,000 products, 5,000 images, 12,500 AI credits, 200 keywords) that does not appear on the App Store listing at all, and also sells credit top-ups from $10 for 5,000 credits and $50 for 25,000. Rating 5.0 from 674 App Store reviews. Developer Storeware, Milton, Delaware; the app launched 19 October 2021 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock: Know what an SEO app can and cannot do before you buy any tier. This one fixes the mechanical layer well — meta titles and descriptions in bulk, alt text, compressed images, JSON-LD, sitemaps, indexing requests — and none of that creates demand for products nobody is searching for. It is maintenance, not marketing, and on a catalogue of 25 products the free tier already does most of it. Two specifics worth a raised eyebrow. The pricing gap between Essential at $39.99 for 250 products and Advanced at $249.99 for 10,000 is filled by a $99.99 Growth plan that lives on the vendor's own site but not on the App Store listing our link points to, which is a strange place to hide a tier. And the AEO/GEO features — the LLMs.txt generator, the Agents.md editor, the separate “agentic” ranking — are a bet, not a channel: no major search or AI vendor has committed to reading llms.txt, so treat those numbers as a hypothesis you are testing rather than traffic you are buying.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores with a few hundred products and no in-house SEO help, who want metadata, schema, alt text and indexing handled in bulk and reported against Search Console
tools.skip_if: you have fewer than 25 products, in which case the free tier is the whole product, or you expect an app to fix a demand problem rather than a metadata one

tools.name: Storylane
tools.what_it_does: Interactive product demos you can embed, with analytics on who watched what.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Free $0: 1 seat, 1 published demo live at a time, unlimited views. Starter $50/month ($40 annual), 1 seat, extra seats $40 each, unlimited demos, de-anonymises 250 visitors/month. Growth $625/month ($500 annual), 5 seats, extra seats $100 each, 2,500 visitors/month. Premium $1,500/month ($1,200 annual), 10 seats, 10,000 visitors/month. Enterprise quote-only. Their RepX chat product is separate again, starting at $2,000/month for up to 10,000 monthly visitors.
tools.honest_knock: The jump from Starter to Growth is $50 to $625 a month — twelve and a half times — and the free tier is capped at one live demo, so the moment you want a second demo published you are on the ladder. What is actually being sold at each step is visitor de-anonymisation: 250 a month on Starter, 2,500 on Growth, 10,000 on Premium. Price that against what you already pay a separate tool to do, because it is the meter that decides your tier, not the number of demos. Extra seats are charged on top at $40 to $100 each, which means a five-person sales team on Starter is not $50 a month, it is $210.
tools.best_for: sales and marketing teams who show a product before a call and want to know which prospects clicked what — the free tier is genuinely usable for one demo
tools.skip_if: you need more than one live demo but nowhere near 2,500 identified visitors a month, because that is exactly the gap the price ladder does not serve; a screen recording and a calendar link may do the job for less
compare_with: the direct interactive-demo peers — compare the visitor-identification allowance at your tier, since that is what you are really buying

tools.name: Streak
tools.what_it_does: CRM built directly inside Gmail: manage pipelines, leads and deals from your inbox with email tracking, mail merge and shared views — ideal for teams that live in Google Workspace.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Pro about $49/user/mo annual ($59 monthly), Pro+ ~$69, Enterprise ~$129; ~20% annual discount. The free CRM tier was eliminated in 2024-25, though free email power tools (tracking, mail merge 50/day, snippets) remain.
tools.honest_knock: The pitch — CRM living inside Gmail — is also the ceiling: everything happens in the inbox, which power users love and growing teams outgrow (reporting, permissions, cross-team process). And note the trajectory: the free tier is gone and per-seat prices sit at real-CRM levels now, so the 'lightweight Gmail add-on' framing no longer matches the invoice. If the inbox is truly where your deals live, few tools feel this natural.
tools.best_for: solo founders and small Gmail-native teams whose pipeline genuinely lives in email threads and who want zero context-switching
tools.skip_if: your team needs shared process outside the inbox (a standalone CRM scales better), or you're price-sensitive — the Gmail convenience now costs full CRM money
compare_with: standalone SMB CRMs at similar or lower per-seat — Streak's edge is literally living in Gmail; that's the whole trade

tools.name: Success.co
tools.what_it_does: Strategy execution and OKR platform. Turn goals into action: set objectives, track KPIs and scorecards, run meetings and align teams so strategy actually gets executed rather than just planned.
tools.pricing: Team-based subscription (2026); specific rates aren't published in full — expect per-user pricing, verified on their site. There's a 30-day free trial, and 501(c)(3) nonprofits get a 50% discount. Get a quote for your team size.
tools.honest_knock: The honest truth about strategy-execution and OKR software is that the tool is the easy part — value comes entirely from the cadence around it (setting real objectives, updating scorecards, running the weekly meeting). Buy it without leadership committing to that rhythm and it becomes another dashboard nobody opens. It's genuinely useful as the backbone for a team that already runs on goals; it won't create that discipline on its own.
tools.best_for: leadership teams that already run on goals and want one place to set objectives, track KPIs and scorecards, and keep strategy execution on cadence
tools.skip_if: your team won't commit to a regular goal-review rhythm (the software alone won't create it), or a simple shared doc already keeps you aligned
compare_with: close OKR/EOS-style execution platforms — compare on how well each fits your existing operating rhythm and per-user cost

tools.name: Sunsama
tools.what_it_does: Daily planning that pulls tasks from your other tools into one deliberate schedule.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) The page gives two different numbers and it is worth knowing both. The plan card says $17 a month billed yearly, or $22 billed monthly, for the Pro plan, with unlimited usage and integrations; Enterprise is quote-only. The FAQ on the same page says Sunsama costs $25 a month per person, or $20 a month on yearly plans, and gives a worked example of $50 a month for two people. There is a free trial with no card required. The page also explains, unprompted, that they price at $25.00 rather than $24.99 because they consider the latter 'deceitful psychological trickery'.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing page contradicts itself: the plan card says $17 yearly and $22 monthly, the FAQ on the same page says $20 yearly and $25 monthly. One of those is stale, and until you know which, treat $25 as the number you might actually be charged. That is an odd thing to have to say about a company that goes out of its way on that same page to explain why it refuses to use $24.99 pricing — the transparency is real and so is the inconsistency. The other thing to be clear about is that this is per person with no team discount mentioned: two people is two subscriptions, and their own example says $50.
tools.best_for: people whose problem is deciding what to do today rather than tracking what exists — it pulls from your existing tools and forces a daily plan, which is the whole product
tools.skip_if: you already plan your day and just want a task list, because that is free everywhere; also skip it for a team, since there is no team pricing and the per-person cost multiplies straight through
compare_with: the direct daily-planning peers — all three are per person, so compare on which one actually gets you to close the planning ritual each morning

tools.name: Superfiliate
tools.what_it_does: Creator-led growth for D2C brands: run influencer, affiliate and referral programs in one platform across Shopify, Meta and TikTok Shop — discovery, automation, gifting and revenue tracking.
tools.pricing: Tiers run roughly $299/mo to $999/mo (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's a real investment — built for brands already running creator and affiliate programs, and overkill if you're just testing your first affiliate offer.
tools.best_for: e-commerce brands turning customers and creators into affiliates with branded co-branded storefronts — if the volume justifies $299+/mo
tools.skip_if: you're testing affiliate marketing for the first time — the $299 entry assumes a program that's already producing

tools.name: SurveyMonkey
tools.what_it_does: Survey and feedback platform: build surveys, collect responses at scale and analyze results for market research, CX and employee feedback. A native Salesforce integration pushes responses straight into Salesforce, triggers workflows off the answers themselves (churn-risk follow-up or an NPS detractor landing on a rep's desk, for instance) and ties feedback back to accounts and pipeline, so sales and CS read it inside the tool they already work in rather than in a separate reporting dashboard.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, served in euros from an EU address) The free tier is nearly useless for real research (10 questions, 25 responses). Team plans are €30 and €75 per user per month, both starting at a minimum of 3 users and billed annually, so the real entry point for a team is €90 a month rather than €30. Individual paid plans sit alongside those. Overage is charged at €0.10 per additional response once you pass your plan's limit, and on paid plans response limits are counted across all surveys and all users rather than per survey. SurveyMonkey Audience responses are sold separately.
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is a teaser, response caps trigger $0.15-per-response overages that become a hidden cost on big studies, branding and customisation are limited, and a lot of the good analytics and logic sit behind higher tiers.
tools.best_for: teams that need research-grade survey logic (skip logic, randomisation, quotas) with compliance (HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2) and 200+ integrations
tools.skip_if: you just need a simple form (Google Forms is free) or you're cost-sensitive with high response volumes — the overage fees add up
compare_with: the free-basic and the design-led form tools

tools.name: SurveySparrow
tools.what_it_does: Conversational surveys and NPS with a polished respondent experience. A limited free plan, then roughly $19–39/month on Basic up to $149 on Business. Response limits on the lower tiers and a contact-sales wall on API and higher volume make budgeting fiddly, and there is no true monthly billing.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) The plan prices are not in the page itself — they render only after the plan selector loads, and neither our July nor our August 2026 capture retrieved an amount. What the page does publish is the discount structure: yearly billing saves up to 40%, students and education get 50% off, nonprofits 15%, and a startup programme offers $2,000 of credit for $500. Our earlier reading put paid survey plans at roughly $19-39/mo (Basic), Starter around $59 and Business around $149, with the CX and reputation suites quoted, billed quarterly or annually rather than monthly — treat those as indicative and take your figure from the selector.
tools.honest_knock: The conversational-survey UX is the draw, but response limits on lower tiers and the 'contact sales' wall on advanced features (API, higher volume) make budgeting fiddly — and there's no true monthly billing.
tools.best_for: teams that want engaging, conversational surveys and NPS with a polished respondent experience
tools.skip_if: you just need a quick, occasional form — a free tool like Google Forms or Tally covers it without a subscription

tools.name: Survicate
tools.what_it_does: Customer feedback platform for continuous surveys: NPS, CSAT and in-product micro-surveys across web, in-app, email and link — with templates, audience targeting and native integrations (Segment and RudderStack among them) that pipe feedback straight into your CRM and analytics.
tools.pricing: (prices read 2026-08-17 on survicate.com/pricing) A 10-day trial of all features, no card. Growth starts at $114/mo billed annually and is metered on feedback, not seats: 250 survey responses and 1,000 data points a month, 10 user seats across 2 teams, one dashboard. Pro starts at $349/mo billed monthly or annually, with a custom yearly response pool, advanced survey logic and 10 dashboards. Enterprise starts at $569/mo. Note that the entry price moved up during 2026 - we had $89 on this page before this read - so check the current figure before you budget.
tools.honest_knock: The plan is metered by response volume, not by surveys — a viral NPS month can push you a tier up, and the free plan's 30-day retention quietly deletes your history. Mind the billing asymmetry too: Starter is monthly-only while Growth and up expect an annual commitment.
tools.best_for: product and CX teams running always-on feedback — NPS, CSAT and in-app surveys — piped into the CRM and analytics stack they already use
tools.skip_if: you just need an occasional one-off questionnaire (a simpler form tool covers that) or your response volume is huge — response-metered pricing punishes scale
compare_with: Typeform wins on beautiful long-form forms, SurveyMonkey on cheap general-purpose surveys; Survicate wins on continuous product feedback with deep integrations

tools.name: Switcher Studio
tools.what_it_does: Multi-camera live production and streaming from iPhones and iPads you already own, with overlays and pay-per-view monetisation. Studio runs around $45/month on annual billing. iOS-only — no Android or desktop app — and wireless multi-cam is only as reliable as the venue's Wi-Fi.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against switcherstudio.com) (2026) Studio around $45/mo on annual billing (about $65 monthly) and Suite around $69–$71/mo annual (about $99 monthly); a Studio Seasonal tier near $55/mo runs on a 3-month commitment for event users. 14-day trial, no free plan.
tools.honest_knock: It's iOS-only — iPhones and iPads, no Android and no desktop app — so your whole capture setup lives in Apple's ecosystem. And wireless multi-cam is only as reliable as your venue's Wi-Fi; a shaky connection is the failure mode nobody markets. The monetization features (pay-per-view, subscriptions) are genuinely strong, but only matter if you're actually selling access.
tools.best_for: creators, churches, events and small businesses that want multi-camera live production and streaming using iPhones and iPads they already own — no broadcast hardware
tools.skip_if: you're on Android or Windows, you need rock-solid wired production for high-stakes broadcasts, or a single-camera stream is all you'll ever need
compare_with: OBS is free but desktop and technical; Switcher trades that for wireless iPhone simplicity at a subscription price

tools.name: Synthesia
tools.what_it_does: AI avatar video for training, explainers and onboarding: type a script, no camera or actors needed. Priced in video-minute credits — Basic is free with about 10 minutes a month and no downloads, Starter $18/month billed yearly for 120 minutes a year. Re-generating an edit spends the minutes again.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) Basic is free. Starter $29/mo billed monthly or $18/mo billed yearly; Creator $89/mo monthly or $64/mo yearly; Enterprise is custom with unlimited minutes. The page currently carries a NEW LOWER PRICES banner claiming plans from $18 a month, a 38% saving. Priced by video-minute credits, so the minute allowance rather than the sticker is what decides which plan you need, and a Studio Express-1 avatar is a paid add-on at $1,000 a year available only on annual plans. One caution we can document: the FAQ block lower down that same page states Starter costs $29 a month or $264 a year and Creator $89 a month or $804 a year, which works out at $22 and $67 a month — not the $18 and $64 shown on the plan cards above it. Both readings were present in our July and August 2026 captures too, so check the figure at checkout rather than trusting either block.
tools.honest_knock: The video-minute caps are tight — 10 min/mo on Starter goes fast when you iterate, and re-generating edits burns minutes. Fantastic for avatar-led training and explainers without a studio, but not for high-volume or cinematic production.
tools.best_for: teams making talking-head training, explainer and onboarding videos without cameras, actors or editing
tools.skip_if: you need lots of video or cinematic, human-shot production — the minute caps and avatar style won't fit

tools.name: Tapita AI SEO Blog Builder
tools.what_it_does: AI blog builder for Shopify: generates SEO-oriented posts with titles, images and keyword suggestions, embeds your products, and schedules bulk publishing from a drag-and-drop editor. Free with 50 one-off credits; Pro is $9.99 a month on Shopify Basic but rises with your Shopify plan to $14.99, $39.99 or $69.99.
tools.pricing: (read 2026-08-19 on apps.shopify.com/tapita-ai-seo-blog-builder) Free plan available: unlimited blog posts, 50 credits that do not recur, extra credits at $0.06 each, unlimited SEO audits, the drag-and-drop editor with autosave, author, product and table-of-contents blocks and 24/7 live chat. Pro is $9.99 a month or $101.89 a year, a 15% saving, and adds 250 AI credits a month, publish scheduling, content strategy suggestions, one-click multi-language AI translations, AI keyword suggestions, weekly idea suggestions and hands-on help fixing SEO issues. The headline price applies on Shopify Basic only: the listing states +$5 on the Grow plan, +$30 on Advanced and +$60 on Shopify Plus, so Pro is $14.99, $39.99 or $69.99 a month depending on which Shopify plan you are on. All charges are billed in USD and recur every 30 days. Rating 4.9 from 450 App Store reviews. Developer Tapita; the app launched 14 February 2022 and carries Shopify's “Built for Shopify” badge.
tools.honest_knock: Publishing volume is the trap this tool makes cheap. It generates posts quickly and schedules them daily or weekly in bulk, and a Shopify blog filled with unedited AI articles is precisely the pattern search engines have spent the last two years demoting — the app lowers the cost of production, not the bar for ranking. Used the other way round, as a drafting and structuring tool for posts you actually edit, it is sensible and cheap. Two practical points on the price: the $9.99 headline holds only on Shopify Basic, and the surcharge takes it to $69.99 a month on Shopify Plus, which is the sort of detail that belongs in a headline rather than a footnote. And the listing never says how many of the 250 monthly credits a single post costs, so the allowance cannot be planned against until you ask.
tools.best_for: Shopify stores that want structured, product-linked blog drafts and a publishing schedule, and that will edit what comes out before it goes live
tools.skip_if: you intend to bulk-publish AI articles unedited, or you are on Shopify Plus and can buy a full content tool for what the surcharge takes this to

tools.name: Tapstitch
tools.what_it_does: Fashion-first print-on-demand for brand-builders: premium heavyweight blanks (streetwear tees, oversized hoodies), bigger print areas and made-to-order apparel with no inventory — integrates with Shopify.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17) No subscription and no monthly fee — you pay per item, production plus shipping, so there is no plan price to compare. Our monthly captures of the catalogue put item prices roughly between $2.99 and $19.99 depending on the blank. The honest catch is margin rather than fees: Printify's lower product and shipping costs mean noticeably higher profit per sale, while Tapstitch's premium heavyweight blanks (around 250 GSM tees and 350-380 GSM hoodies) sit at retail-grade prices, roughly $35-50 for a tee at the finished end. Price the finished garment against your retail price, not the platform.
tools.honest_knock: Printify is cheaper, higher-margin and has a far bigger catalogue — if you're optimising for profit per sale or product breadth, that's the real trade-off. Tapstitch earns its place when garment quality and brand feel matter more than squeezing the last point of margin.
tools.best_for: creators building a real apparel or streetwear brand who care about fabric, fit and how the product feels in hand
tools.skip_if: you want the cheapest option or the widest catalogue — for pure margin and product breadth, traditional POD like Printify wins

tools.name: Tax1099
tools.what_it_does: Per-form e-filing of 1099s, W-2s and related forms, falling to about $0.68 a form at high volume, with an eFile Plus subscription near $249/year for frequent filers. TIN matching, W-9 requests, state filing and corrections can each carry their own charge, so tally the add-ons.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-17, with a caveat) Pay-as-you-go per-form e-filing that drops with volume — our dated reading puts it as low as about $0.68 a form at high volume, with a free Essential account for creating payers and recipients and running TIN matching, and an eFile Plus subscription around $249 a year for teams that file often. Those tiers are not published in a form our capture can read, so verify the current per-form bands on their own page before budgeting a season. The structure to understand is that the price per form falls as your count rises, so the effective cost depends entirely on volume rather than on a plan.
tools.honest_knock: Per-form pricing is genuinely cheap for a handful of 1099s, but it's metered — TIN matching, W-9 requests, state filing and corrections can each carry their own charge, so a business filing across many recipients and states should tally the add-ons, not just the headline per-form rate. It's a filing tool, not a bookkeeping system; it assumes your payee data is already clean.
tools.best_for: businesses and accountants who need to e-file 1099s, W-2s and related forms accurately and cheaply, especially seasonal or higher-volume filers
tools.skip_if: you only file one or two forms a year (the IRS's own free options may suffice) or you want full bookkeeping rather than just the filing step
compare_with: TaxBandits or the IRS IRIS portal
TaxBandits is a close paid equivalent; IRIS is free but barer — Tax1099 wins on integrations and bulk workflows

tools.name: TaxCycle
tools.what_it_does: Professional tax preparation and CRA e-filing for Canadian accountants and bookkeepers. Quote-based and priced by module and firm size, with reported figures ranging from roughly CAD 1,680 into five figures for full suites. Canada-only, and not a consumer filing app.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-17 against taxcycle.com) Quote-based, not listed publicly (2026); all prices in CAD before tax. It's professional-firm software with tiered pricing by module and firm size — reported figures range widely (roughly CAD $1,680 up into five figures for full suites). Get a written quote for your module mix.
tools.honest_knock: This is professional preparer software priced for firms, not a consumer filing app — the cost only makes sense if you're preparing returns for clients at volume. Pricing is opaque and module-based, so the real annual number depends on exactly which forms (T1, T2, T3, etc.) and seats you need; budget the full suite, not one module. It's also Canada-only. For a Canadian accounting or bookkeeping practice, its CRA integration and smart checks are the draw.
tools.best_for: Canadian accountants and bookkeepers who prepare and e-file client returns and want fast, checked, CRA-integrated professional tax software
tools.skip_if: you're an individual filing your own personal return (consumer software is far cheaper), or you're outside Canada
compare_with: the established Canadian preparer suites — TaxCycle competes on speed and UX; compare on the specific modules your practice files

tools.name: Team Pulse
tools.what_it_does: Projects, tasks, chat, files and a light CRM pipeline in one tool. The tiers gate on members and projects at once, and the pipeline does not exist below the $79 Growth plan — Starter at $29 is a single seat with five projects. The listed rates assume annual billing.
tools.pricing: (2026) Genuinely free tier: $0/mo for 1 member, 2 projects, unlimited collaborators, chat/tasks/files. Paid (billed annually): Starter $29/mo ($348/yr) — 1 member, 5 projects, NO pipelines; Growth $79/mo ($948/yr) — 3 members, 10 projects, 1 pipeline, AI; Pro $159/mo ($1,908/yr) — 10 members, 20 projects, 2 pipelines; top tier $299/mo ($3,588/yr) — 40 projects, 1,500 AI credits.
tools.honest_knock: The tiers gate on TWO axes at once — member count and project/pipeline count — so you can hit a wall on either. The CRM pipeline is a big part of the pitch, but it doesn't exist below the $79 Growth plan (Free and Starter have none), and member limits are tight: Starter is a single seat, Growth just three. The listed rates also assume annual billing.
tools.best_for: solo operators and small teams who want projects, tasks, chat AND a lightweight CRM pipeline with AI in one simple tool, and value the real free tier to start
tools.skip_if: you need more than a handful of team members (seat caps climb the tiers fast), or you only need project management — dedicated PM tools give far more generous member limits
compare_with: ClickUp is the established all-in-one work platform with generous free seats; Team Pulse bundles a CRM pipeline plus AI in a simpler package — cleaner to start, but the member and project caps are tighter as you grow

tools.name: Teikametrics
tools.what_it_does: Advertising optimisation for Amazon and Walmart sellers, with inventory and catalogue signals.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Essentials, for up to $10K a month in ad spend: $149 a month billed annually, or $179 billed monthly. Advanced, for over $10K a month in ad spend: custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. Enterprise is for over $100K a month in ad spend, quote-only. A free trial and a free opportunity assessment are offered.
tools.honest_knock: Read the Advanced tier carefully, because it is not a subscription — it is a subscription plus a percentage. Three per cent of ad spend above $10,000 means a seller spending $40,000 a month pays an extra $900 on top of whatever the custom base is, and that line scales with the thing the product is supposed to make more efficient. That is not automatically wrong — it aligns them with your growth — but it does mean your bill rises when your advertising does, and you should model it at your expected spend rather than your current one. The $10K threshold is the number to watch: crossing it changes the pricing model, not just the price.
tools.best_for: Amazon and Walmart sellers spending enough on ads that a few points of efficiency covers the fee — under $10K a month the flat $149 is straightforward
tools.skip_if: your ad spend is small or seasonal, because the flat fee at low spend is a large share of your budget and the percentage model at high spend needs modelling before you commit
compare_with: the direct marketplace-advertising peers — compare total cost at your real monthly ad spend, including any percentage component

tools.name: Tellent
tools.what_it_does: Modular people-management platform — applicant tracking (Recruitee), core HR and performance management with AI automation, for hiring and managing teams.
tools.pricing: Modular (2026): Recruitee ATS from about €270-292/mo (Start) and €343-371/mo (Advance), Optimize from ~€1,374/mo; HR Manage (HRIS) ~$111/mo and HR Grow (performance) ~$111/mo as separate modules. ~20% off annual; 18-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: The modular pricing is honest — buy only the ATS, or only HRIS — but note the ATS floor: ~€270/mo prices it for teams that hire continuously, not for the company filling two roles a year. And as with every ATS, the workflow fit (approval chains, career-site needs, integrations with your assessment tools) matters more than the feature list; the 18-day trial is enough to run one real vacancy through it — do that.
tools.best_for: European scale-ups hiring continuously that want a collaborative ATS (and optionally modular HRIS/performance) with transparent per-module pricing
tools.skip_if: you hire occasionally (job boards + a spreadsheet honestly suffice), or you want one all-in-one HR suite rather than modules
compare_with: Greenhouse is the ATS benchmark at higher cost; Personio bundles HR-first — Tellent sits between on price with EU roots

tools.name: Tenable
tools.what_it_does: Exposure and vulnerability management (makers of Nessus): scan, prioritize and remediate security weaknesses across IT, cloud and OT — for security teams of any size.
tools.pricing: Nessus Professional runs about $4,390-$4,790/yr and Nessus Expert about $6,390-$6,790/yr; cloud Tenable Vulnerability Management starts around $3,500+/yr for ~100 assets and scales with asset count (2026). Multi-year deals discount; enterprise contracts range widely.
tools.honest_knock: Note on how we link this one, updated 28 Jul 2026: between 21 and 28 July our partner link was dead — Tenable's shop subdomain stopped resolving, so we pointed the link at Tenable's own product page and earned nothing from it. Tenable confirmed on 28 July that the links are repaired; we re-tested them that day and the link now works again, lands on the same Nessus product page, and does pay us a commission. This is serious, enterprise-grade security tooling with an enterprise price and a learning curve — not a set-and-forget scanner. You need someone who can act on the findings, or you're paying for reports nobody reads.
tools.best_for: security teams and IT-mature companies that need continuous, authoritative vulnerability scanning and can remediate what it finds
tools.skip_if: you have no one to triage and fix findings — a managed security service or a lighter scanner fits a small team better

tools.name: TestGorilla
tools.what_it_does: Pre-employment skills testing: assessment library, custom questions and candidate scoring.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Free $0 with 10 credits a month, no card needed, including preset custom questions and 1 full-access seat. Core $142/month on an annual commitment, $1,704 billed annually, with the full test library, analytics and 2 full-access seats. Plus starts from $400/month with an annual commitment starting at $4,800, described as scaling with your hiring needs. Prices are shown in USD with GBP, EUR, AUD and INR available.
tools.honest_knock: Both paid tiers are annual-commitment only. Core is not $142 a month in any meaningful sense — it is $1,704 up front, and there is no monthly option to test it with real candidates first. That matters more here than in most categories, because hiring is lumpy: a company that hires in two bursts a year is paying for ten quiet months. Plus is worse to budget for, because it 'starts from' $400 and the page will not say what moves it. The free tier is credit-metered rather than feature-limited, which makes it a genuine trial — use it on a real vacancy before you sign a year.
tools.best_for: companies hiring steadily enough that a year of testing is cheaper than one bad hire, and who will actually use the library rather than writing their own questions
tools.skip_if: you hire a few people a year — the annual commitment is the whole problem, and the free tier plus a well-designed take-home task covers occasional hiring
compare_with: the direct skills-testing peers — compare on whether a monthly plan exists at all, because that is where these differ most

tools.name: TextExpander
tools.what_it_does: Text-expansion tool: you type a short abbreviation and it expands into a stored snippet system-wide on macOS and Windows and in Chrome, with fill-in fields, nested snippets, date maths and scripting. The real product is the team layer — a shared snippet library with permissions, sign-up by email domain, auto-subscribe for new hires, usage statistics and SSO — aimed at support, clinical-admin, recruiting and sales teams that need everyone sending the same approved wording. The vendor self-attests SOC 2/SOC 3 and HIPAA compliance with a BAA available, which is the clearest argument for paying rather than using a free expander. There is a free plan (5 active snippets); paid tiers start at $5 per user/month billed annually, and the 30-day trial of the full product needs no credit card.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-18 on the vendor's own pricing page; USD per user/month billed annually, excluding tax) The line-up was rebuilt since our July reading and it now starts at free: Free $0 forever with no credit card, Pro $5 (billed annually at $60), Business $10 (billed annually at $120), Enterprise quoted. Annual billing is sold as two months free against paying monthly; the page does not print the monthly amounts next to the plans, so we do not quote them. The free plan is real but deliberately narrow: 5 active snippets out of an unlimited library, one snippet swap every two weeks, 3 teams, 5 team members and no snippet activity history at all. That history — what lets you see changes and restore deleted snippets — is 24 hours on Pro, 7 days on Business and unlimited only on Enterprise. Team members stay capped at 5 on Free and Pro; unlimited members start on Business, which is also the first tier with single sign-on (Google SSO on Business, all providers plus SCIM on Enterprise). A 30-day trial with full access to every feature and no credit card sits alongside the free plan. The page still carries an important pricing note for international customers, which we could not open on this reading, so treat the listed USD amounts as pre-tax.
tools.honest_knock: On a Mac the operating system already does the basic job free — Apple's built-in Text Replacement syncs static snippets across your Apple devices, though Apple's own documentation notes it is not available in every app — and Espanso covers the power-user case free and open source on Mac, Windows and Linux. On Windows there is no built-in equivalent (contrary to a widely repeated claim, PowerToys has no text-expansion utility), so the case for paying is genuinely stronger there. Do not buy it for mobile: the vendor's own mobile page is an early-access signup form for Android and iOS betas, not a shipping product, even though the surrounding copy is written in the present tense. Add the snippet activity history, which is nothing at all on the free plan and only 24 hours on the $5 Pro tier — 7 days on Business, unlimited only on Enterprise — and the vendor's own note that buyers in VAT/GST countries including the EU, UK and Australia may see an estimated 20% uplift on the listed USD price (read 21 July 2026), and for one person with a few dozen fixed snippets the honest answer is usually don't.
tools.best_for: support, clinical-admin and recruiting teams that need everyone sending identical approved wording — the shared library, permissions, email-domain sign-up, auto-subscribe and SSO are what the paid tiers actually buy, and the SOC 2 and HIPAA-with-BAA posture the vendor advertises is the one thing no free expander offers a compliance-bound team
tools.skip_if: you are one person on a Mac with a couple of dozen fixed snippets — macOS Text Replacement is built in and free, Espanso is free and open source across all three desktop platforms, and TextExpander's own free plan now covers 5 active snippets, so a subscription only starts earning its keep when you need fill-in fields, scripting, or a second person editing the same library
compare_with: Both have a free tier now, and Text Blaze still undercuts every paid rung — Pro $2.99 and Business $6.99 per user per month billed annually, read on their own plans page on 18 August 2026, against $5 and $10 — so TextExpander has to win on OS-level expansion outside the browser and on the SSO, SCIM and HIPAA-BAA paperwork a procurement team asks for, not on price

tools.name: Textline
tools.what_it_does: Business SMS for support and sales teams: shared inboxes, automations and compliance tooling.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) The page we read documents the meters rather than the plans. Add-on message credits are $0.03 each, bought in advance. Backup message credits — their fallback when you run out mid-conversation — are $0.04 each. A 10DLC campaign fee of $15 a month appears on your bill if you use a 10DLC long code, which is the standard route for business texting in the US. Plan prices were not shown on the page we read.
tools.honest_knock: Two costs here are easy to miss and both are per month rather than one-off. The 10DLC campaign fee is $15 a month, charged by the carrier registry rather than by Textline, and it applies to the number type most business texting uses — so it is effectively part of the price whatever plan you pick. And the credit system has two rates: $0.03 for credits you buy deliberately and $0.04 for backup credits that kick in automatically when you run out. That is a 33% premium for not noticing, applied at exactly the moment you are mid-conversation with a customer. Set your top-up threshold high enough that backup credits never trigger.
tools.best_for: support and sales teams that already text customers from personal phones and need a shared, compliant inbox with a record of who said what
tools.skip_if: you send marketing blasts rather than conversations — that is a different product and priced per message elsewhere; also skip it if your volume is low enough that a shared inbox on your existing helpdesk covers it
compare_with: the direct business-texting peers — compare on the per-message rate plus the 10DLC fee, since the platform fee is only part of it

tools.name: Thordata
tools.what_it_does: Proxy infrastructure and scraping stack — residential, mobile, ISP and datacenter proxies plus SERP/web-scraper APIs, priced per GB, IP or 1K requests.
tools.pricing: (price re-verified 2026-08-02 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Usage-metered, with free trials on the APIs. At research time a ~50%-off sale ran: residential proxies from $0.65/GB (list $1.05), mobile $2.20/GB, static ISP and datacenter proxies from $0.75/IP (list $1.50); SERP API from $0.70 per 1K responses, Web Scraper API $0.50/1K, Web Unlocker $1.00/1K, Scraping Browser $2.50/GB.
tools.honest_knock: Everything is a meter — per GB, per IP, per 1K responses — so the bill scales with usage, and the headline rates were SALE prices at research time (roughly half of list): budget on list price, not the promo. And the category-wide caveat we’d give any residential-proxy vendor: those ‘100M+ real residential IPs’ come from consumer devices, so check sourcing ethics and your target sites’ terms before building on it.
tools.best_for: data teams scraping at scale — price intelligence, SERP tracking, AI-training data — who want proxy infrastructure plus ready-made scraping APIs at aggressive per-unit rates
tools.skip_if: you need predictable flat pricing, or your use case skirts site terms — residential proxying carries compliance questions no discount fixes
compare_with: Bright Data is the enterprise incumbent with strict compliance vetting; Thordata undercuts hard on per-unit price — decide whether compliance depth or unit cost matters more for your pipeline

tools.name: Thryv
